homestead.text: Honey: a Butterfree brings honey back to its nest every day, so a Butterfree nesting at the homestead might yield a harvest, if no more is taken than it needs.
homestead.note: Nobody has described taking honey from a Butterfree nest, or how much one stores.

homestead.text: Pollination for the orchard and the Glasshouse Berry rows, if Berry plants need pollinators at all, which no source says.
homestead.note: Rests on the inferred pollinator role.

homestead.text: A flower scout: it finds flowering patches miles away, which would tell a forager where things are in bloom.
homestead.note: Untested: no one has followed a Butterfree to its flowers.

homestead.text: Rain doesn't stop it, which suits a wet highland; cold is another matter, since all its HeartGold records are lowland.
It needs flowers within reach, a sheltered nest site in trees, and handlers who stay out of its wing dust.

microhabitat: flower patches up to about 10 km out
niche.foraging: central-place forager: flies flower to flower collecting honey and carries it home to a nest on its leg hairs

relationships.note: Honey from flowers; the entries' word is honey.
Visits flower after flower and seeks out pollen; no entry says it carries pollen.

Budew opens its bud in the sun to release pollen; Butterfree seeks out patches with tiny amounts of pollen. Budew is in Ilex Forest only when the Sinnoh Sound plays on the radio, and no entry links them.
Same rare Headbutt table in Ilex Forest.
Same rare Headbutt trees; Noctowl hunts at night, when a day-active Butterfree would be resting. Its toxic dust argues against it being easy prey.
Version counterparts in Ilex Forest; together only in National Park's Bug-Catching Contest.

open_questions: What is the nest: where, of what, shared or solitary, and is it where eggs are laid?
What is the honey for? It is gathered daily and carried home, but Caterpie eat leaves, so it isn't food for the young unless the young are fed something else.
Does it pollinate? It visits flower after flower, but no entry says it carries pollen.
Does it eat pollen as well as honey?
Which sense finds flowers six miles away?
Can it survive highland winters, or would Blackthorn be a summer-only range?
The line has no HeartGold-SoulSilver egg moves, so no ecotypes can be read from breeding.

Caterpie.summary: The leaf-eating larva of Butterfree. Caterpie climbs trees on sticky feet, eats leaves bigger than itself, hides among foliage of its own green, and when its red feeler is touched it releases a foul smell. It grows by moulting several times, then covers itself in silk and becomes Metapod. In HeartGold it is the animal most often met in Ilex Forest's grass in the morning and by day, and it is never met there at night; in SoulSilver, Weedle takes its place slot for slot.

anatomy.text: A small green larva (0.3 m, 2.9 kg) with a red feeler, or antenna, on top of its head.
Its short feet end in suction pads or cups that stick to any surface, so it can climb slopes, walls and trees without tiring.
anatomy.analogy: Real caterpillars grip with prolegs, fleshy legs on the abdomen ringed with tiny hooks (crochets), rather than with suction.

anatomy.text: The red feeler is where its defensive stench comes from (see Defence). No entry says whether it is also a sense organ.

diet.text: It eats leaves, voraciously: it can eat a leaf bigger than its own body while you watch.
It climbs trees to forage, so it feeds in the foliage of trees and shrubs, not only near the ground.
No entry names its food plants. HeartGold puts it both in Ilex Forest's grass and in its Headbutt trees, so tree leaves are the likeliest food.

habitat.text: A forest animal of foliage and trees.

In HeartGold it is in Ilex Forest's grass (60% of encounters by day, 50% in the morning, none at night) and its common Headbutt trees (30%), on Routes 30 and 31, in National Park, and in Kanto on Route 2 and in Viridian Forest.

In SoulSilver it is absent from Ilex Forest and the routes and appears only in the Bug-Catching Contest in National Park, where Weedle also appears. Caterpie and Weedle are version counterparts that hold identical slots at identical rates.
Its microhabitat is foliage in the understory and lower canopy, where its colour matches the leaves.

behavior.text: Day-active. In HeartGold's tables it appears in the morning and by day and never at night, in Ilex Forest and on every route where it occurs. This rests only on the time-of-day split in the encounter tables.
Its day is climbing and eating; 'tirelessly' and 'tenaciously' are the entries' words for the climbing.
Where it spends the night isn't recorded. Its Headbutt-tree records (which have no time of day) and its leaf camouflage suggest it stays in the foliage.

social.text: No entry describes groups, pairs or any dealings with its own kind.

reproduction.text: Bug egg group, 15 egg cycles, an even sex ratio, medium growth. Nothing in the Pokédex describes eggs or where they are laid; breeding belongs to the adult, Butterfree.
Eggs are probably laid on or near the plants the larva eats, since a hatchling that can only crawl has to start close to food.
reproduction.analogy: Female butterflies lay on the larval food plant, often after testing it with taste receptors on their feet.

defense.text: When its feeler is touched, or to drive enemies away, it releases a horrible stench from the feeler or antennae on its head.
defense.analogy: Swallowtail caterpillars (Papilionidae) have an osmeterium, a forked organ behind the head that they turn out when disturbed, releasing a strong-smelling defensive secretion. Caterpie's red feeler matches it closely.

defense.text: Camouflage: it crawls into foliage that is the same colour as its body.
defense.analogy: Crypsis, blending into the background, is one of the commonest defences of real caterpillars.

defense.text: Shield Dust (it blocks the added effects of attacks taken) is its ability, and String Shot (Lv 1) lets it slow an attacker with silk.
It has enemies to drive away, but no entry names them; the forest's birds are the obvious candidates (see Relationships).

senses.text: Nothing is said directly about its senses. It finds leaves, climbs to them and reacts to touch on its feeler, which is as much as the entries imply.

life_cycle.text: It grows by moulting repeatedly, shedding its green skin each time.
life_cycle.analogy: Larval growth in stages (instars) separated by moults; most real caterpillars pass through about five.

life_cycle.text: At the last moult it covers itself with silk and becomes a cocoon, Metapod. In the games this happens at level 7, and Metapod becomes Butterfree at level 10.
life_cycle.analogy: Complete metamorphosis (holometaboly): larva, pupa, adult. Real butterflies usually pupate as a bare chrysalis hung from a silk pad; spinning a full silk cocoon is mostly a moth habit.

life_cycle.text: Caterpie is the line's feeding stage: the pupa doesn't feed and the adult lives on honey, so almost all the leaf-eating in the Butterfree line is done by Caterpie.

moves_in_the_wild.text: Tackle and String Shot are its moves from hatching. Bug Bite comes at level 15, but it becomes Metapod at 7, so a wild Caterpie rarely if ever has it: its working toolkit is pushing and silk.
String Shot is the game form of its silk, which it uses for its cocoon. Using silk as a safety line or to tangle attackers is a reading of the move, not something the entries say.
moves_in_the_wild.note: Only the cocoon use is canon.

moves_in_the_wild.text: The line has no egg moves in HeartGold and SoulSilver, so breeding gives no basis for distinct Caterpie lineages.

ecology.text: A primary consumer of foliage (trophic level 2), and in HeartGold the leaf-eater most often met on Ilex Forest's floor by day.
Its stench and camouflage are anti-predator defences aimed at hunters that find prey by sight. In Ilex Forest the Headbutt-tree birds, Hoothoot and Noctowl, are the plausible predators.
ecology.note: No entry names a predator of Caterpie.

ecology.text: It turns leaves into the forest's flower-visitor: everything Butterfree is built from was eaten by Caterpie.
It shares the forest grass with Oddish in shifts: Caterpie in the morning and by day, Oddish only at night.

humans.text: Easy to catch (catch rate 255) and common on Johto's first routes; National Park's Bug-Catching Contest includes it in both versions. No entry describes people using it.
Anyone handling one should leave the feeler alone: touching it sets off the stench.

homestead.text: Silk. Caterpie makes silk for its cocoon, and cocoons left behind once Butterfree has emerged could be gathered and spun without harming anything.
homestead.note: Untested: nothing describes how much silk a cocoon holds or what it is like.
homestead.analogy: Eri silk (from Samia ricini) is spun from cocoons after the moth has left, unlike mulberry silk, which is reeled from cocoons whose pupae are killed first.

homestead.text: In a garden it is a pest, not a helper: it eats a lot of leaves. Keep it away from crops and the Glasshouse Berry plants.
Small enough to live indoors (0.3 m, 2.9 kg), but handle it gently: a touch on the feeler sets off the stench.
Whether it can get through a Blackthorn winter is unknown: all its Johto records are lowland forest and routes.

niche.foraging: climbs into foliage and chews leaves, morning and day

relationships.note: Both larvae eat leaves in the same forest. The games never let them share Ilex Forest in one version and give each the other's slots at the same rates; read as competitive exclusion that is a hypothesis resting on a version-exclusive design device.
Together only in National Park's Bug-Catching Contest, in both versions.

Both are in Ilex Forest's common Headbutt trees; Hoothoot (0.7 m, 21.2 kg) is large enough to take a 0.3 m larva. Against it: Hoothoot's grass records are all at night and Caterpie's all by day, so they would meet only at dawn or with the larva resting in foliage; Hoothoot's diet is not stated.
Noctowl catches prey in darkness and is in Ilex Forest's rare Headbutt trees; a larva resting in foliage at night is within reach. Prey is never named.
Carnivine (the 'Bug Catcher Pokémon') hangs from branches to ambush prey; it is in Ilex Forest only when the Sinnoh Sound plays on the radio.
Same grass, opposite shifts: Caterpie morning and day, Oddish night only.

open_questions: Which plants does it eat? No entry names one.
What eats it? Its defences imply predators that hunt by sight, but none is named.
Where does it spend the night? It drops out of the walking tables after dark.
How long is the larval stage in real time? Level 7 says nothing about days.
Does its silk have any use besides the cocoon, and is it worth gathering?
The line has no egg moves in HeartGold and SoulSilver, so no ecotypes can be read from breeding; are there regional differences anyway?

contradictions.text: One feeler or two? Yellow, Gold, Ruby/Sapphire and Diamond/Pearl/Platinum (10.2, 10.3, 10.6, 10.9) describe a single feeler or antenna; Emerald and HeartGold (10.7, 10.10) say antennae.
contradictions.note: A forked organ, like a real swallowtail caterpillar's osmeterium, could be described either way.

Chansey.summary: A rare, gentle, all-female Pokémon that lays nutritious eggs every day, several a day, and gives them away: it shares them with injured Pokémon and people, and won't share them with those who have evil in their hearts. The eggs are so delicious that even people who have lost their appetite eat them eagerly, which is why people try to catch it. It walks carefully so as not to break its egg, but runs away extremely fast. It is said to bring happiness to whoever catches one. In HeartGold and SoulSilver it lives on Kanto's Routes 13, 14 and 15, one encounter in a hundred, and comes to Route 13 in swarms.

anatomy.text: An upright, egg-shaped animal (Gen 4 shape upright), 1.1 m and 34.6 kg, typed Normal, all female: the Egg Pokémon.
It carries an egg and walks carefully to prevent it from breaking.

diet.text: No entry says what Chansey eats.
Laying several nutritious eggs a day needs a great deal of food; what it eats to do so is a gap.
Its eggs are food for others: people eat them, and it gives them to the injured.

habitat.text: It is rare and rarely found; the Gen 3 Pokédex habitat is urban.
In HeartGold and SoulSilver it lives on Routes 13, 14 and 15 at 1% (Lv 25), at any time, in both versions; on Route 13 it comes in swarms (40%). The Johto Safari Zone has it too.

In Red, Blue, Yellow, FireRed and LeafGreen it lived in Kanto's Safari Zone (and in Cerulean Cave in Red, Blue and Yellow). In HeartGold and SoulSilver that Safari Zone is gone, and Chansey lives on the routes just east of Fuchsia instead.

behavior.text: It is extremely fast at running away.
It is gentle and kind-hearted, compassionate and kindly.
Its activity pattern is not stated.

social.text: It shares its nutritious eggs with injured Pokémon and people.
It won't share them with those who have evil in their hearts.
Feeding the injured of other species is altruism across species lines, rare in any animal; the entries give no reason.

reproduction.text: It lays nutritionally excellent eggs every day, several a day.
Fairy egg group, 40 egg cycles, all female, fast growth, base friendship 140 (high).
Eggs laid daily and given away can't all be fertile; they are better read as food the body makes, like milk.
reproduction.note: A reading; nothing says whether the eggs hatch.

defense.text: It runs: carefully walking with its egg, it is extremely fast at running away.
Natural Cure, Soft-Boiled (Lv 12), Refresh and Healing Wish make it hard to wear down, and Minimize (Lv 20) helps it hide.

senses.text: It sees an injured Pokémon and shares its eggs, and it tells those with evil in their hearts, by the entries; how is not said.

life_cycle.text: Happiny becomes Chansey when it levels up holding an Oval Stone by day, and Chansey becomes Blissey with high friendship: 0.6 m and 24.4 kg, then 1.1 m and 34.6 kg, then 1.5 m and 46.8 kg.

moves_in_the_wild.text: Pound, Growl, Tail Whip, Refresh, Soft-Boiled, Double Slap, Minimize, Sing, Fling, Defense Curl, Light Screen, Egg Bomb (Lv 38), Healing Wish and Double-Edge. Soft-Boiled (heals) and Egg Bomb (throws an egg) are the egg in game form.

ecology.text: A producer of food for others: its eggs feed the injured, a resource it puts into the web every day.
Its own diet is unknown; on Routes 13 to 15 it shares the grass with Nidorina, Nidorino, Hoppip and Tangela.

humans.text: People try to catch it for its extremely nutritious eggs, which even those who have lost their appetite eat eagerly.
It is said to bring happiness to those who manage to catch it.

homestead.text: A source of nutritious eggs, laid daily, which it shares with the injured: the homestead's infirmary food.
A healer's companion: Soft-Boiled and Healing Wish, and a habit of seeking out the hurt.
Don't take its eggs by force: it won't share with those who have evil in their hearts.
Chansey leaving an egg on the doorstep of the house where the old man has a cold.

niche.foraging: unknown; it lays several nutritious eggs a day, which feed others
niche.note: Guild left empty: the machine reading's herbivore comes from the Normal type alone.

relationships.note: It feeds them its eggs; they benefit.

ecotypes.name: Bell-healer
ecotypes.reading: The caring lineage of the entries: moves that cure others and help them. A Chansey that tends to the injured beyond sharing eggs. Fits places with many hurt animals, such as busy routes.
ecotypes.behavior: Seeks out the injured.

ecotypes.name: Egg-keeper
ecotypes.reading: A lineage that protects its eggs: it hits back, leaves a decoy and blinds with mud before it runs. The Chansey that won't give its egg to the wrong hands. Fits places where people hunt it for eggs.
ecotypes.behavior: Runs only after it has left a decoy.

open_questions: What does Chansey eat to lay several eggs a day?
Do its eggs ever hatch, or are they only food?
How does it tell those with evil in their hearts (113.11)?
Why is it so rare, if it is so useful to others?

folklore.text: It is said to bring happiness to those who manage to catch it.

Charizard.summary: Charizard is a winged, fire-breathing mountain Pokémon: 1.7 m and 90.5 kg, able to fly to nearly 4,600 feet and breathe fire hot enough to melt boulders. It flies about looking for strong opponents and never turns its fire on one weaker than itself, though its flames can start forest fires by accident. Its tail flame, which in Charmander is a measure of its life, flares whitish-blue when it is furious. Every Charizard in Gen I–IV is raised from a Charmander given to a trainer; the line's wild home is described only as the rocky mountains where Charmeleon's tails shine at night like stars.

anatomy.text: An upright, winged, tailed body of 1.7 m and 90.5 kg, Fire and Flying type.
Wings strong enough to carry it high, close to 4,600 feet (about 1,400 m).
A flame burns at the tip of its tail; it burns more intensely when Charizard breathes out a blast of fire, and flares whitish-blue or light blue when it is furious.
It breathes or spits fire hot enough to melt boulders, or almost anything.
In the juvenile, the tail flame burns from birth and reflects its health; Charmander's life would end if the flame went out.

diet.text: No entry for any stage says what the line eats.
Charmander prefers hot places and hot things, but that is a preference for heat, not a diet; the machine reading's 'thermotroph' came from its Fire type alone.
Charmeleon knocks foes down with its tail and tears them up with its claws, which describes fighting, not necessarily feeding.

habitat.text: Gen 3 Pokédex habitat for the whole line: mountain. Charmeleon live in rocky mountains, where their fiery tails shine at night like stars.
It ranges into forest as well: its flames are known to cause forest fires.
Not found in the wild in any Gen I–IV game. Charmander is a starter gift in Pallet Town (Red, Blue, FireRed, LeafGreen, and HeartGold and SoulSilver after beating Red) and on Route 24 in Yellow.

behavior.text: It flies about in search of strong opponents.
It never turns its fiery breath on an opponent weaker than itself.
This is a change from the middle stage: Charmeleon is hotheaded, constantly seeks opponents, and calms down only when it wins, with no mention of sparing the weak.
Its activity pattern is unknown. Charmeleon's tails are seen shining at night, which shows they are out at night, not necessarily active.

social.text: No entry describes Charizard living in groups or pairs.
Seeking strong opponents while sparing weak ones suggests contests with rivals of similar strength, as ritual or status contests rather than predation.
Charmeleon's tails shining 'like stars' in the rocky mountains implies many individuals within sight of each other at night.

reproduction.text: Monster and Dragon egg groups, 20 egg cycles, 87.5% male; the sex ratio is shared with the other starter lines and is probably a game convention.
The young hatch with the tail flame already burning.
Nothing describes courtship, nests or parental care.

defense.text: Its breath inflicts terrible pain on enemies.
Smokescreen (Lv 10) and Scary Face (Lv 21) are wild level-up moves: smoke to blind and a threat face to deter.
Blaze strengthens its fire when it is close to defeat.
Its sheer size, flight and fire leave few animals that could threaten it; no predator is named.

senses.text: Nothing is said about its senses.
Charmander's tail flame makes a sound as it burns, audible only in quiet places; whether the adult's is louder is not recorded.

life_cycle.text: Charmander (0.6 m, 8.5 kg) becomes Charmeleon at level 16 (1.1 m, 19 kg) and Charizard at level 36 (1.7 m, 90.5 kg). The last step nearly quintuples its mass as it gains wings and the Flying type.
The juvenile's flame shows its strength and emotions: weak when it is weak, bright when healthy, wavering when happy, blazing when enraged; when healthy it keeps burning even if a bit wet.
Charmeleon is the aggressive stage: barbaric in nature, it whips its fiery tail around, slashes with sharp claws and destroys foes without pity; a strong foe makes its tail flare bluish-white.
As Charmeleon, its swinging tail raises the air temperature to unbearable levels, and when agitated it spouts flames that incinerate its surroundings.
Crystal says its fire grows hotter as it gains battle experience; Diamond, Pearl and Platinum give the same idea only as something 'it is said'.
Read as development, the line goes from a fragile juvenile whose flame is its life, through an indiscriminately aggressive adolescent, to a flying adult that chooses its fights.

moves_in_the_wild.text: Fire by level-up: Ember (Lv 7), Fire Fang (Lv 28), Flamethrower (Lv 42), Fire Spin (Lv 49), Heat Wave (Lv 59) and Flare Blitz (Lv 66).
Claws: Slash (Lv 32), with Dragon Claw and Shadow Claw available at Lv 1, matching the sharp claws of the Charmeleon entries.
Flight: Wing Attack comes at Lv 36, as it evolves, and Air Slash at Lv 1. Fly itself is a machine move taught by people.

ecology.text: A fire-maker that changes landscapes: its flames can set forests alight, by accident.
Fires it starts would open the canopy and reset parts of a forest, with knock-on effects for everything living there.
Its trophic position is unknown because its diet is never given.

humans.text: Known to cause forest fires unintentionally, so it is a fire hazard wherever it lives near people.
In the games the line reaches people only as a starter: there are no wild ones.

homestead.text: Air travel and long-range errands: its wings carry it close to 4,600 feet, and Fly (a taught move) lets it carry its trainer.
A heat source in winter, if kept under control: it already features as a candidate for the Hearth hall.
A light after dark: the tail flame of the line shines at night like a star.

Fire safety comes first: keep it away from the hay store, timber and the Glasshouse plantings, and never let it fight near buildings, since its fire melts boulders and can start forest fires by accident.
Its tail flame is a built-in health check: in the juvenile a weak flame means a weak animal, so keepers can read it daily.
Young Charmander need shelter from Blackthorn's rain and snow: their life depends on the tail flame, which only a healthy one keeps burning when a bit wet.

microhabitat: high air up to about 1,400 m
niche.foraging: not described; it flies widely in search of opponents
niche.note: Diet is never stated for any stage, so no guild or trophic level is given.

relationships.note: It sets forest fires by accident.
Charmander prefers them; whether the adult does is not stated.

ecotypes.name: Crag duellist
ecotypes.reading: Dragon Dance raises speed and strength, read here as a display before a fight; Dragon Rush is a full-body charge and Outrage a sustained rampage. A lineage that settles contests with rivals by display and then open combat, the adult's search for strong opponents made central. Fits high crags where flying rivals meet.
ecotypes.behavior: Displays from a high perch, then dives at the challenger.

ecotypes.name: Scree hunter
ecotypes.reading: Rock Slide and Ancient Power bring stone down or hurl it, and Metal Claw is a hard-edged slash. A lineage that works broken rock, loosening scree onto whatever is below and finishing with claws. Fits steep, rocky mountains like those where Charmeleon live.
ecotypes.behavior: Hunts along cliff edges, sending stones down before it follows.

ecotypes.name: Pack raider
ecotypes.reading: Beat Up is an attack the user's companions all join, and Bite and Crunch are jaw attacks. A lineage that hunts or fights in groups and uses its jaws more than its fire. Fits mountain valleys where many Charmeleon live within sight of one another.
ecotypes.behavior: Attacks as a group; the jaws do the work, the fire is held back.

open_questions: What does any stage of the line eat?
Where do wild Charizard live? No Gen I–IV game has a wild one of any stage.
Does the adult's life depend on its tail flame, as Charmander's does?
Does its fire really grow hotter with experience? Crystal says so; Diamond, Pearl and Platinum only report it as hearsay.
Why does it spare weaker opponents? Is it a contest rule, or about energy?
Do Charmeleon live in groups, as 'tails shine at night like stars' suggests?
How does a flame-tailed juvenile survive rain and snow in the mountains?

contradictions.topic: Fire temperature and experience: fact or saying
contradictions.note: Crystal (6.5) states that its fire gets hotter as it gains battle experience; Diamond, Pearl and Platinum (6.10) give the same claim only as 'it is said'. The content agrees; the confidence doesn't.

folklore.text: It is said that Charizard's fire burns hotter if it has experienced harsh battles.
folklore.note: Crystal (6.5) states the same thing as fact.

folklore.text: When it rains, steam is said to spout from the tip of Charmander's tail.
folklore.note: Line folklore, from the juvenile's entries.

Chimchar.summary: A small, very agile fire primate of craggy mountains: it scales sheer cliffs to live on their tops, and burns gas made in its own belly as a flame from its rear end. The fire is a sign of health, burning weakly when it feels sick, and rain can't put it out, but Chimchar puts it out itself before it sleeps, to prevent fires. Nothing says what it eats. It is the first stage of SoulSilver's Infernape, and in the Gen I-IV games it is only ever a starter gift in Sinnoh; no Johto game has one.

anatomy.text: A small upright animal (Gen 4 shape upright), 0.5 m and 6.2 kg, typed Fire: the Chimp Pokémon.
Its fiery rear end is fuelled by gas made in its belly; the gas burns from its rear.
The flame on its tail can be put out and relit: it extinguishes it before sleeping.
A gas made in the belly is most plausibly a product of digestion, so the fire runs on what it eats.
anatomy.analogy: Fermentation in the guts of many plant-eating mammals makes methane, which burns.

diet.text: No entry for any stage of the line says what it eats.
Its line is filed as an omnivore only as a guess from its primate-like body and Human-Like egg group, as Infernape's dossier does; nothing in the Pokédex supports a diet.
Fury Swipes (Lv 15) and Scratch are its feeding-like moves; neither names a food.

habitat.text: It scales sheer cliffs to live atop craggy mountains.
It is never wild in any Gen I-IV game: a starter gift at Lake Verity in Diamond and Pearl and on Route 201 in Platinum. HeartGold and SoulSilver don't have it at all except by trade.
No Gen 3 habitat is given: the line is from Generation 4.

behavior.text: It is very agile, and climbs sheer cliffs.
Before going to sleep it puts out the flame on its tail, to prevent fires.
Putting out its own flame to avoid starting fires is a deliberate, safety-minded act, unusual for a young animal.
It sleeps, so it has a rest period, but whether by day or night isn't said.

social.text: Chimchar's own entries say nothing about groups. Monferno lives in packs with ranks shown by the fire on its tail (391.4), so the young are likely raised in those packs.

reproduction.text: Field and Human-Like egg groups, 20 egg cycles, 87.5% male (the starter ratio), medium-slow growth. Nothing in the Pokédex describes breeding.

defense.text: Its fire can't be put out by rain.
Agility and cliffs are its first defence: it lives where few animals can follow.
Taunt (Lv 9) and Torment (Lv 25) are provoking moves, and Nasty Plot (Lv 23) a scheming one: a cheeky young animal in game terms.

senses.text: Nothing is said about its senses. Its fire shows how it feels: weak when it is sick.

life_cycle.text: It becomes Monferno at level 14 and Infernape at 36: 0.5 m and 6.2 kg, then 0.9 m and 22.0 kg, then 1.2 m and 55.0 kg. The type adds Fighting at Monferno.
Read as development, the flame moves up and spreads: a rear-end flame in Chimchar, a tail fire that shows rank in Monferno, a crown of fire that never goes out in Infernape.

moves_in_the_wild.text: Its level-up list: Scratch, Leer, Ember (Lv 7), Taunt, Fury Swipes, Flame Wheel (Lv 17), Nasty Plot, Torment, Facade, Fire Spin (Lv 33), Slack Off (Lv 39), Flamethrower (Lv 41). Slack Off, a rest that heals, fits an animal that sleeps with its fire out.

ecology.text: Its role can't be set: nothing says what it eats, and no game has it in the wild.
Putting its flame out before sleep suggests it lives where an untended fire would catch: on vegetated ledges, not bare rock.
ecology.note: Read from the reason the entry gives (to prevent fires).

humans.text: It reaches people as a Sinnoh starter, given at Lake Verity or on Route 201.

homestead.text: A small, careful fire: it puts its own flame out before it sleeps, which makes it one of the safer fire-users to keep near buildings.
Watch its flame for illness: weak fire, sick Chimchar.
A climber of sheer cliffs, so it could reach high ledges, roofs and the Ice Path's upper shelves.
Rain can't put its fire out: a light for wet nights on the mountain.
The homestead's Chimchar, snuffing its tail every night before it curls up, as careful as anyone in the house.

niche.foraging: unknown; no entry says what any stage eats
niche.note: Omnivore guessed from the primate-like body and Human-Like egg group only, as for Infernape.

relationships.with: gas made in its own belly

ecotypes.name: Troop helper
ecotypes.reading: Infernape's cooperative lineage in the young: moves that help a partner and borrow a partner's moves. A Chimchar raised in a pack that works together. Fits crags where a troop shares the few good ledges.
ecotypes.behavior: Sticks close to its troop; joins in rather than leads.

ecotypes.name: Four-limb striker
ecotypes.reading: The line's fighting lineage, showing early: fire carried into the hands and feet before Infernape grows its fiery hands. A Chimchar that fights with its limbs, not its tail. Fits cliff faces where a fight is close and footing matters.
ecotypes.behavior: Punches and kicks with a flare of fire; a fighter from the egg.

open_questions: What does it eat, and what makes the gas in its belly?
Where would a wild Chimchar live? No game has one in the wild.
Is it active by day or by night?
Is it raised in Monferno's packs, and who looks after the young?

Chinchou.summary: A small electric fish of the dark ocean floor, in depths beyond sunlight's reach. Chinchou's two antennae, which evolved from a fin, are filled with cells that make so much electricity it tingles itself; it shoots positive and negative charges between their tips to make prey faint and to shock its foes. On the dark sea floor its only means of communication is its constantly flashing lights, which it uses to exchange signals with others. In HeartGold and SoulSilver it is hooked on the good and super rods along both regions' coasts, from New Bark Town and Sea Route 41 to Pallet Town, Vermilion and the seas around Cinnabar.

anatomy.text: A small fish (Gen 4 shape fish), 0.5 m and 12.0 kg, typed Water and Electric: the Angler Pokémon.
Two antennae, which evolved from a fin, with positive and negative charges flowing through them.
anatomy.analogy: A real anglerfish's lure is a fin spine moved forward onto the head.

anatomy.text: The antennae are filled with cells that generate strong electricity; it makes so much it even tingles slightly itself.
anatomy.analogy: Electric eels and rays make electricity in stacks of modified muscle cells.

diet.text: A hunter: it lets loose positive and negative charges from its antennae to make its prey faint.
No entry names the prey. At 12 kg, its prey is most likely small fish and other small animals of the sea floor.
Thunder Wave (Lv 6) paralyses and Spark (Lv 20) shocks: the stunning charge in game form.

habitat.text: The dark ocean floor, in depths beyond sunlight's reach; the Gen 3 Pokédex habitat is sea.

In HeartGold and SoulSilver it is hooked on the good and super rods (Lv 20-40) at New Bark Town, Sea Route 41 and Route 47 in Johto, and Routes 26 and 27, Pallet Town, Vermilion City, Cinnabar Island and Sea Routes 20 and 21 in Kanto, at any time, in both versions.
A deep-sea animal on a fisherman's rod near shore is odd; it may rise from the depths, as Lanturn's light is seen rising at night (171.5), but nothing says so.

behavior.text: Its lights flash constantly.
Its activity pattern is not stated (the machine reading's 'day' comes from 'sunlight's reach', which says the opposite); the rods hook it at any time.

social.text: On the dark ocean floor its only means of communication is its constantly flashing lights; it flashes them to exchange signals with others.
social.analogy: Real deep-sea fish, squid and fireflies signal to their own kind with patterns of light.

social.text: An animal that signals to others lives among others: Chinchou is social in some way, though how many live together isn't said.

reproduction.text: Water 2 egg group, 20 egg cycles, an even sex ratio, slow growth. Nothing describes how it breeds; its light signals may serve courtship, but no entry says so.
reproduction.analogy: Fireflies and many deep-sea animals court with patterns of light.

defense.text: It shoots electricity between its antenna tips and zaps its enemies; when it senses danger, it discharges positive and negative electricity.
Volt Absorb heals it when hit by electricity; Confuse Ray (Lv 17) and Supersonic are its other guards.

senses.text: It senses danger, and discharges when it does; how is not said.
It sees its own kind's lights, so it can see in the dark in some way.

life_cycle.text: It becomes Lanturn at level 27: from 0.5 m and 12.0 kg to 1.2 m and 22.5 kg, and from two charged antennae to a bright lure that lights the sea (171.1, 171.3).

moves_in_the_wild.text: Bubble, Supersonic, Thunder Wave, Flail, Water Gun, Confuse Ray, Spark, Take Down, Bubble Beam, Signal Beam, Discharge, Aqua Ring, Hydro Pump and Charge. Signal Beam, a beam of light, fits an animal that signals with light.

ecology.text: A small electric hunter of the deep water: it stuns prey with its charge.
Where the rods hook it, it shares the water with Tentacool on the surface, Shellder on the bottom and its own adult, Lanturn.

humans.text: Nothing is said about Chinchou and people.
Illuminate, its other ability, makes wild Pokémon more likely to appear: in game terms its light draws others in.

homestead.text: Not a highland animal: it lives on the dark sea floor. Met only on coastal trips, on the end of a line.
Don't take one off the hook barehanded: it shocks what touches it when it senses danger.
The night the line came up with a blinking light on the end of it.

microhabitat: dark ocean floor beyond sunlight's reach
niche.foraging: stuns prey with positive and negative electricity from its antennae

relationships.with: small fish and other small sea-floor animals
relationships.note: It stuns prey; the prey is unnamed.

ecotypes.name: Current-trapper
ecotypes.reading: A lineage of strong currents: it traps prey in a whirlpool, darts after it and thrashes. Fits seas with strong tidal flow.
ecotypes.behavior: Hunts in moving water rather than waiting on the bottom.

ecotypes.name: Deep-calm signaller
ecotypes.reading: A lineage of still, dark water: a strange beam, a veil of mist, a mind left calm. The flashing-light talker of 170.2, where nothing else lights the water. Fits the deepest, calmest sea floor.
ecotypes.behavior: Flashes long patterns to others and rarely moves.

open_questions: What does Chinchou eat?
What do its light signals say, and to whom?
How does a fish 'beyond sunlight's reach' end up on rods near the shore?
Does its electricity come from food, or does it make it from nothing?

Clefairy.summary: A small, rare, moon-bound Pokémon of quiet mountains. Clefairy collects moonlight with the wings on its back, and the stored moonlight apparently lets it float in midair. It is rarely seen except on the night of a full moon, when groups come out to play; at dawn the tired Clefairy go back to their quiet mountain retreats and sleep nestled against each other. It is said that happiness comes to anyone who sees a gathering of Clefairy dancing under a full moon. Its cuteness makes it popular, even as a pet. In HeartGold and SoulSilver it lives in Mt. Moon, one encounter in twenty, in both versions.

anatomy.text: A small upright animal (Gen 4 shape upright), 0.6 m and 7.5 kg, typed Normal: the Fairy Pokémon.
It has wings on its back; the moonlight it stores in them apparently gives it the ability to float in midair.
It flies using the wings on its back to collect moonlight.

diet.text: No entry says it eats food. It collects and stores moonlight, which gives it the power to float.
Moonlight stored as energy makes it a lunar phototroph in the web; whether it also eats is unknown.
Moonlight (Lv 37) and Cosmic Power (Lv 25) are in its own list.

habitat.text: Quiet, deep mountains, where it is thought to live with others and where it sleeps; the Gen 3 Pokédex habitat is mountain.
It is rare and found only in certain areas.
In HeartGold and SoulSilver it lives in Mt. Moon (1F and 2F, 5%, Lv 8) at any time, in both versions; the Johto Safari Zone has it at night when its blocks call for it.
Mt. Moon, 'a mountain where a star fell' in the Pokégear's words, is the 'quiet mountain' of its entries in Kanto.

behavior.text: On every night of a full moon, groups of Clefairy come out to play; when dawn arrives they return to their mountain retreats and sleep nestled against each other.
Though rarely seen, it becomes easier to spot on the night of a full moon.
Its activity follows the moon: out on full-moon nights, asleep by day. The HGSS tables have it at any time inside Mt. Moon, where the moon isn't visible.

social.text: It lives with others: groups play together on full-moon nights and sleep nestled together.
Follow Me (Lv 16), which draws attacks to itself, and Healing Wish (Lv 46), which gives its life to heal a partner, are self-sacrificing group moves.

reproduction.text: Fairy egg group, only 10 egg cycles, 25% male (three in four are female), fast growth.
Its young, Cleffa, become Clefairy with high friendship.

defense.text: Rarity and retreat: it stays hidden in quiet mountains and comes out mostly on full-moon nights.
Cute Charm can infatuate what touches it; Magic Guard protects it from all damage but attacks. Sing (Lv 7) and Minimize (Lv 19) are sleep and hiding.

senses.text: Nothing is said about its senses; it responds to the full moon, so it senses moonlight.

life_cycle.text: Cleffa becomes Clefairy with high friendship, and Clefairy becomes Clefable with a Moon Stone: 0.3 m and 3.0 kg, then 0.6 m and 7.5 kg, then 1.3 m and 40.0 kg.
Its whole line turns on the moon: moonlight stored in its wings, play under the full moon, and a Moon Stone to become Clefable.

moves_in_the_wild.text: Pound, Growl, Encore, Sing, Double Slap, Defense Curl, Follow Me, Minimize, Wake-Up Slap, Cosmic Power, Lucky Chant, Metronome, Gravity, Moonlight, Light Screen, Meteor Mash and Healing Wish: song, play and the sky.
Meteor Mash and Gravity in a Pokémon of the mountain 'where a star fell' are a nice coincidence; nothing links them in the entries.

ecology.text: An energy-eater of moonlight in the web, so it competes with nothing for food, by the entries; inside Mt. Moon it shares the cave with Zubat, Geodude, Paras and Sandshrew.
Its predators are not named. Golbat feasts on the blood of people and Pokémon (42.8), and its young, Zubat, shares Mt. Moon with Clefairy.
ecology.note: Co-occurrence and the line's stated diet only.

humans.text: Its magical and cute appeal has many admirers; its adorable behaviour and cry make it highly popular, and it is popular as a pet.
It is rare and difficult to find.

homestead.text: A night companion for full-moon evenings, when it is at its most active.
It sleeps nestled with others: keep more than one, and give them a quiet, dark corner by day.
It may need moonlight more than food: a clear-sky place at night.
homestead.note: Untested whether it needs food.

homestead.text: Clefairy dancing on the meadow above the homestead on the first full moon of the year, and everyone who watches feeling lucky.

niche.foraging: collects moonlight with the wings on its back
niche.note: Moonlight is the only intake any entry names.

ecotypes.name: Moon-dancer
ecotypes.reading: A lineage of the full-moon gatherings: moves that heal and give to others. The Clefairy whose dances bring happiness, by the old saying. Fits open mountain meadows under clear skies.
ecotypes.behavior: First out on full-moon nights, last to sleep.

ecotypes.name: Mimic trickster
ecotypes.reading: A lineage that lives by charm and copying: it mimics, it fake-cries, and it takes what it wants. Fits places with people, where cuteness pays.
ecotypes.behavior: Begs, copies and pockets things.

open_questions: Does Clefairy eat anything, or live on moonlight alone?
What do they do on full-moon nights: play, courtship, gathering moonlight?
Is Mt. Moon Square, open to the sky on top of Mt. Moon, where Kanto's Clefairy gather under the full moon?
Why are three in four Clefairy female?

folklore.text: It is said that happiness will come to those who see a gathering of Clefairy dancing under a full moon.
They are thought to be rare, as they do not appear often.

Crobat.summary: A four-winged bat whose hind legs have become a second pair of wings, built for fast, nearly silent flight in the dark. Crobat sneaks up on prey on wings that barely make a sound, and on long flights it rests one pair while flying on the other. Its line is the most familiar night animal of Johto's caves: eyeless, echolocating Zubat that roost by day and avoid sunlight, and Golbat, which drink the blood of people and Pokémon and are common in the Ice Path next to Blackthorn. Crobat itself is never wild; it comes only from a Golbat that is close to its trainer.

anatomy.text: A large bat (1.8 m, 75.0 kg) with four wings: its hind legs have turned into a second pair.
Four wings make it faster and quieter in flight, and clumsier on the ground.
anatomy.analogy: Owls achieve near-silent flight differently, with comb-like leading edges and soft fringes on their flight feathers that break up turbulence.

anatomy.text: Golbat has four sharp fangs with small holes for sucking blood, able to puncture even thick, tough hides.
Zubat has no eyes (or eyes grown shut) and finds its way by ultrasonic cries from its mouth.

diet.text: Crobat hunts by stealth: it sneaks up on its intended prey with wings that barely make a sound. The prey is not named.
Golbat drinks blood, from people and Pokémon alike: more than ten ounces (about 300 ml) at a gulp, and it won't stop until it is full, even if it then gets too heavy to fly well.
diet.analogy: The common vampire bat (Desmodus rotundus) also lives on blood alone and can take about half its body weight in a feed, which leaves it heavy enough that it has to shed water quickly before flying.

diet.text: Golbat looks for neck veins and strikes from behind without warning.
Whether Crobat still drinks blood is not stated; its moves suggest it does (Leech Life at Lv 1, Bite, Poison Fang), and its stealthy approach fits the same feeding.

habitat.text: Caves and dark places: Zubat forms colonies in perpetually dark places and roosts by day in caves, old buildings and deep forest. Its Gen 3 Pokédex habitat is cave.
Crobat rests by hanging from a tree branch with its rear legs, so it roosts in trees as well as caves.
Crobat is not found in the wild in any Gen I-IV game.

Golbat is common in the Ice Path (30% on every floor at any hour in HeartGold and SoulSilver; 50-60% in Crystal) and present at the Blackthorn entrance of Dark Cave, so the line lives right around Blackthorn. Zubat and Golbat are in nearly every Johto cave, plus some routes at night.

behavior.text: Nocturnal: Crobat turns active when night comes; Golbat is most active in pitch-black, moonless nights; Zubat sleeps until sundown.
Zubat avoids sunlight, which burns it slightly or makes it unhealthy; it spends daylight hanging upside down, unmoving, in dark places.
Crobat flies long distances by switching wings: flying on one pair means it has come a long way, and by alternately resting front and rear wings it can fly all day without stopping.
It flies so silently through the dark that it may go unnoticed even close by.

social.text: Zubat are colonial: they gather by day and hang from the ceilings of caves and old buildings.
Nothing says whether Golbat or Crobat live in colonies.

reproduction.text: Flying egg group, even sex ratio, 15 egg cycles (shorter than most). Nothing is said about roost nurseries or young.

defense.text: Silence and darkness are its cover; no entry describes predators of the line.
Inner Focus, its only ability, means it can't be made to flinch. Its own moves include Confuse Ray, Supersonic, Screech and Haze.

senses.text: Echolocation: Zubat emits ultrasonic waves from its mouth and reads their reflections to find its way and detect obstacles and targets.
senses.analogy: Most bats echolocate the same way, by reading the echoes of their own calls, though unlike Zubat all real bats have working eyes.

senses.text: Its eyes grew shut over generations of living in pitch-black caverns, by the Emerald account.
senses.analogy: Cave animals often lose their eyes over evolutionary time, as in the blind cave form of the Mexican tetra (Astyanax mexicanus).

senses.text: Whether Crobat keeps echolocating is not said, but its silent approach to prey in the dark implies a sense that works without light.

life_cycle.text: Zubat (0.8 m, 7.5 kg) becomes Golbat at level 22 (1.6 m, 55.0 kg), and Golbat becomes Crobat (1.8 m, 75.0 kg) when it levels up with high friendship.
The new hind wings appear at the last change. Crystal describes them as growing 'as a result of its pursuit of faster, yet more silent flight', a striving-produces-the-trait explanation.
life_cycle.note: Lamarckian phrasing, and Emerald's 'over the course of evolution' blurs individual development with descent. Worth a reviewer's eye.

life_cycle.text: That the final stage needs a close bond with a trainer, not age or size, means wild Crobat may be rare or absent.
life_cycle.note: A friendship trigger read as biology.

moves_in_the_wild.text: The feeding moves are its own: Leech Life (Lv 1), Bite (Lv 13), Poison Fang (Lv 39), and Cross Poison at Lv 1 for Crobat; draining and biting, as the blood-drinking canon would predict.
Supersonic (Lv 5) and Screech are the sound-producing moves of an echolocating animal used offensively.
Mean Look (Lv 33) stops prey escaping, which matches Golbat's refusal to let go once it bites.
Wing Attack, Air Cutter and Air Slash are its own flight moves; Fly is taught.

ecology.text: A blood-feeding micropredator of large animals, people included (trophic level about 3): it takes a meal without killing the host.
Colonial cave roosts concentrate the line, and their droppings (not described) would feed cave communities as bat guano does in real caves.
ecology.note: Guano is not mentioned anywhere in the entries.

ecology.text: Golbat is in the Ice Path with Swinub and Jynx, and on Mt. Silver with Sneasel and Larvitar. Since it drinks the blood of Pokémon, these are its likeliest hosts there.
ecology.note: Co-occurrence plus a general diet; no entry names a host species.

ecology.text: Zubat shares Sinnoh's Wayward Cave with Gible (Zubat 35%).

humans.text: Golbat attacks people at night and drinks their blood, seeking neck veins.
Crobat is the opposite case: it exists only through a strong bond with a person.
Zubat roosts under the eaves of old houses as well as in caves.

homestead.text: A local threat: Golbat are common in the Ice Path and at Dark Cave's Blackthorn entrance, and they drink the blood of people and Pokémon at night. Shut the nursery, pens and Glasshouse at dusk, and expect them in the Ice Path cold vault.
A bonded Crobat as a night scout: fast, silent flight in the dark, unnoticed even close by.
A long-range courier: it can fly all day by resting its wings in turn.
Night travel: the line is built for it, and Zubat's echolocation finds obstacles in total darkness.
Needs: a dark, quiet roost for the day, away from sunlight, which harms the young.
It walks badly; give it perches, not floor space.

niche.foraging: silent nocturnal approach and blood-feeding through punctured skin, guided by echolocation
niche.note: Blood-feeding is Golbat's; Crobat's own prey is not named. 'Parasite' in the sense of a blood-feeding micropredator that leaves its host alive.

relationships.note: Golbat feeds on their blood.
Day roosts.
Ice Path (Golbat).
Mt. Silver (Golbat).
Wayward Cave, Sinnoh (Zubat).

ecotypes.name: Sleeper's bat
ecotypes.reading: A lineage that feeds on hosts it has put to sleep: Hypnosis induces sleep, and Feint Attack is an approach that never misses. A quiet way to take blood from a large animal without a struggle. Fits pasture and farmland near cave roosts, where large animals sleep in the open.
ecotypes.behavior: Lands beside a sleeping animal, keeps it asleep, feeds and leaves before it wakes.
ecotypes.analogy: Common vampire bats mostly feed on sleeping livestock, approaching on the ground.

ecotypes.name: Wind-rider
ecotypes.reading: A lineage for open air: Gust and Whirlwind are blasts of wing-driven air, Brave Bird a reckless full-speed dive. A strong, fast flier that commutes far from its roost to feed. Fits windy highland ridges and sea cliffs.
ecotypes.behavior: Flies further and higher than cave-bound kin; dives on prey in the open.

ecotypes.name: Fleeing-prey hawk
ecotypes.reading: A chaser rather than a sneak: Pursuit hits harder at prey that tries to flee, Quick Attack closes the distance first. A lineage that takes active, flying prey on the wing. Fits forest edges and clearings at night, where flying prey is abundant.
ecotypes.behavior: Hunts moving prey in the air; less dependent on sleeping hosts.

open_questions: Does Crobat still drink blood, or does its stealth serve some other prey?
Does Crobat echolocate, and does it have eyes? Zubat's entries disagree about eyes.
If four wings make it 'tough to stop and rest' (169.2), how does that fit Sapphire's account of resting on a branch (169.5)?
Do Golbat and Crobat form colonies like Zubat?
Which Pokémon does Golbat actually feed on in the Ice Path and on Mt. Silver?
Are wild Crobat possible, given that the trigger is friendship with a trainer?

contradictions.text: Resting: Silver and SoulSilver say four wings make it tough to stop and rest; Sapphire describes it resting by hanging from a branch with its rear legs.
Activity: Diamond says Crobat becomes active at night; Emerald says it can fly all day without stopping.
contradictions.note: 'All day' may mean continuously rather than in daylight.

contradictions.text: Zubat's eyes: Emerald says they grew shut over time; FireRed and Diamond say it has no eyes.

Cubone.summary: A small, lonely Pokémon that lost its mother after its birth and always wears her skull, so no one has ever seen its real face. Cubone pines for the mother it will never see again: when it thinks of her it cries, its cries echo inside the skull as a sad melody, and seeing her likeness in the full moon it weeps; the stains on the skull are its tears. When it is lonesome it is said to cry loudly. Marowak is the Cubone that has overcome that grief and grown tough. In HeartGold and SoulSilver it lives in Kanto's Rock Tunnel, with Marowak, Onix, Geodude and Machop.

anatomy.text: A small upright animal (Gen 4 shape upright), 0.4 m and 6.5 kg, typed Ground: the Lonely Pokémon.
It wears the skull of its dead mother as a helmet and never removes it; no one has ever seen its real face.
The stains on the skull are made by the tears it sheds.

diet.text: No entry says what Cubone eats.
The machine reading's rock-eater comes from its Ground type alone; nothing supports it.

habitat.text: No entry says where it lives; the Gen 3 Pokédex habitat is mountain.
In HeartGold and SoulSilver it lives in Rock Tunnel (35%, Lv 10-13), at any time, in both versions; the Johto Safari Zone has it by day.

behavior.text: When it thinks of its dead mother, it cries, and its crying makes the skull rattle hollowly; its cries echo inside the skull and come out as a sad melody.
If it is sad or lonely, the skull it wears shakes and emits a plaintive, mournful sound.
Seeing a likeness of its mother in the full moon, it cries.
Its activity pattern is not stated; the full-moon crying puts it awake on moonlit nights at least.

social.text: Lonely by name and by its entries: it lost its mother after its birth and pines for her.
An orphan that grieves for its mother points to a young that normally stays with its mother for a long time.
social.analogy: Young elephants and great apes stay with their mothers for years, and orphans show signs of distress.

social.text: Its adult form taps out messages to others by pounding boulders with its bone (105.3): the line does talk to its own kind.

reproduction.text: Monster egg group, 20 egg cycles, an even sex ratio, medium growth.
Every entry has its mother dead; none says whether every Cubone loses its mother, or how.

defense.text: The skull helmet covers its head and face.
Bone Club (Lv 7), Bonemerang (Lv 21) and Bone Rush (Lv 37) are bone weapons; Rock Head protects it from recoil and Lightning Rod draws in electricity.

senses.text: It sees a likeness of its mother in the full moon: it sees well enough at night to see the moon's face.

life_cycle.text: It becomes Marowak at level 28: from 0.4 m and 6.5 kg to 1.0 m and 45.0 kg.
Marowak is the evolved form of a Cubone that has overcome its sadness at the loss of its mother and grown tough (105.6). Growing up, in its entries, is grieving.

moves_in_the_wild.text: Growl, Tail Whip, Bone Club, Headbutt, Leer, Focus Energy, Bonemerang, Rage, False Swipe, Thrash, Fling, Bone Rush, Endeavor and Double-Edge. Rage and Thrash fit an animal driven by feeling.

ecology.text: Its diet is unknown, so its place in the web is unset.
In Rock Tunnel it shares the dark with Marowak, Onix, Geodude, Machop, Machoke, Zubat and Kangaskhan.
Its adult collects bones, rumoured to come from a Marowak graveyard (105.4, 105.5): the line uses the remains of its dead.
ecology.note: Rumour, in the entries' own words.

humans.text: No one has ever seen its real face.

homestead.text: An orphan that grieves: if one is taken in, it needs company more than work.
homestead.note: Inferred from its loneliness; the capability is what it needs, not what it gives.

homestead.text: Leave the skull alone; it never removes it.
The night of the full moon, and the sound from the barn that turns out to be singing.

niche.foraging: unknown
niche.note: Guild left empty: the machine reading's lithovore comes from the Ground type alone.

ecotypes.name: Mourning singer
ecotypes.reading: A lineage of the sad melody (104.2): songs and cries, and a wariness that sees blows coming. Fits echoing caves where its sound carries.
ecotypes.behavior: Sings in the dark on moonlit nights.

ecotypes.name: Skull-charger
ecotypes.reading: A lineage that uses the helmet as a weapon: head-down charges and kicks. The Cubone already on its way to the tough Marowak of 105.6. Fits rocky ground with rivals about.
ecotypes.behavior: Lowers its head and charges.

open_questions: What does Cubone eat?
Does every Cubone lose its mother? How?
Who raises an orphaned Cubone?
Where is the Marowak graveyard the rumours tell of?

folklore.text: When it becomes lonesome, it is said to cry loudly.
A Marowak graveyard exists somewhere in the world, rumours say; Marowak get their bones from it.

Cyndaquil.summary: A small, timid fire-backed animal that spends most of its time curled into a ball or hunched over, and shows its fire only when something frightens or angers it. The flames on its back are its whole defence: they flare when it is startled, burn hottest when it is angry, and sputter with incomplete combustion when it is tired, so its fire tells you its mood and its energy. No entry says what it eats or where a wild one lives; in every Johto game it comes from a professor in New Bark Town. It is the first stage of HeartGold's Typhlosion.

anatomy.text: A small animal, 0.5 m and 7.9 kg, typed Fire, with a Gen 4 body shape of humanoid (it stands on two legs).
Fire comes out of its back: it shoots or flares flames from there when angry, surprised or attacked.
The flames are a combustion that can be incomplete: when it is tired they splutter fitfully, so the fire depends on the animal's own condition, not on an outside fuel.
Incomplete combustion when tired suggests the fire burns something the body supplies and runs short of, a fuel or gas made from what it eats.
anatomy.note: No entry names the fuel. Quilava's 'superheated air' (156.4) points the same way.
anatomy.analogy: Incomplete combustion in a flame starved of oxygen or fuel gives a smoky, guttering burn, which is what 'splutter fitfully' describes.

diet.text: No entry for any stage of the line says what it eats.
The machine reading files it as a thermotroph only because it is a Fire type; nothing in the Pokédex says it takes in heat.
diet.note: Kept out of the niche, as Typhlosion's dossier does.

diet.text: Fury Swipes, Crush Claw and Foresight are egg moves of the line: some lineages may dig and scratch for food on the ground, but this is a reading of moves, not a record of diet.

habitat.text: The Gen 3 Pokédex habitat is grassland; no entry describes where it lives.
It is never wild in any Gen I-IV game. In Gold, Silver, Crystal, HeartGold and SoulSilver it is a gift in New Bark Town; in Emerald a gift in Littleroot Town.
With no wild record anywhere, its natural range in Johto or Kanto is unknown.

behavior.text: It is timid and always curls itself up in a ball.
It usually stays hunched over.
It has a timid nature, and when startled the flames on its back burn more vigorously.
Curling up and staying hunched keep the back, and so the fire, outermost: the resting posture is already the defensive one.
Its activity pattern is not stated, and with no wild encounters there are no tables to read it from.

social.text: Nothing is said about groups, pairs or how it treats its own kind.

reproduction.text: Field egg group, 20 egg cycles, 87.5% male (the usual starter ratio), medium-slow growth. Nothing in the Pokédex describes breeding or young.

defense.text: If attacked, it flares up its back for protection.
The fire on its back burns hottest when it is angry, and the flaring flames intimidate foes.
It protects itself by flaring the flames on its back, vigorous when it is angry; when tired, the flames splutter, so a worn-out Cyndaquil is a poorly defended one.
Smokescreen (Lv 6) fits an animal whose fire smokes: a cloud to hide in before it runs. Defense Curl (Lv 22) is the curl-into-a-ball habit in game form.
The defence is a display first: fire shown to intimidate, used to burn only if that fails.
defense.analogy: Deimatic (startle) displays, like a moth flashing eyespots, scare off an attacker before any fight.

senses.text: Nothing is said about its senses. Being startled easily implies it notices threats quickly, but how is not described.

life_cycle.text: It becomes Quilava at level 14 (the archive also lists 17), and Typhlosion at 36: from 0.5 m and 7.9 kg to 0.9 m and 19.0 kg, then 1.7 m and 79.5 kg.

Development turns a timid, curled-up juvenile into a nimble middle stage covered in nonflammable fur that turns its back to show its fire before battle, and then a large animal that hides in its own heat haze: the fire goes from a startle defence to a weapon.
The body shape changes from upright two-legged (humanoid) to four-legged (Quilava, quadruped).

moves_in_the_wild.text: Its own level-up list is fire and escape: Smokescreen, Ember (Lv 10), Quick Attack (Lv 13), Flame Wheel (Lv 19), Defense Curl, Swift, Lava Plume (Lv 31), Flamethrower (Lv 37), Rollout (Lv 40) and Eruption (Lv 49). Rollout after Defense Curl matches a ball-shaped animal that can roll away.
Eruption, its last level-up move, is the strongest when the user is unhurt; it fits an animal whose fire is fiercest when it is fresh and splutters when it is tired.

ecology.text: Its place in a food web can't be set: nothing says what it eats or where a wild one lives.
A small, timid fire-bearer in grassland would be a fire risk in dry grass whenever it is startled. Nothing in the games shows it starting a fire.
ecology.note: Follows from the flames and the listed habitat only.

humans.text: It reaches people as one of the three Johto starters, given by Professor Elm in New Bark Town.
Its moods are easy to read from its back: bright flames mean anger or fright, guttering flames mean it is tired.

homestead.text: A small heat source that a Trainer can read at a glance: steady flames, a settled animal; spluttering flames, a tired one.
It needs a quiet place to curl up. Sudden noise or handling will make it flare, so keep it away from dry straw and bedding.
A Fire type, so it would cope with heat better than the cold of the highlands; it would want a warm corner in winter.
homestead.note: Nothing says how it copes with cold.

homestead.text: The homestead's Cyndaquil as the hearth-keeper's apprentice: curled by the stove, flaring only when the kettle whistles.

niche.foraging: unknown; no entry says what any stage eats
niche.note: Guild left empty, as for Typhlosion: the machine reading's thermotroph comes from the Fire type alone.

ecotypes.name: Grass-root forager
ecotypes.reading: The same lineage as Typhlosion's grass-root foragers, seen in the young: claws for scratching and a move for finding what hides. A juvenile that forages head-down in the grass, which is also the hunched posture the entries describe.
ecotypes.behavior: Scratches and roots in the grass with its back held up and ready to flare.

ecotypes.name: Last-ditch flarer
ecotypes.reading: Reversal hits hardest when the user is nearly beaten, and Flare Blitz throws the whole body into the flames. A lineage whose timid young do nothing until cornered, then go all in. Fits open grassland with little cover, where a small animal can't always run.
ecotypes.behavior: Curls up and waits out most threats, then explodes into fire when there is no way out.

open_questions: What does it eat, and what does its fire burn? Spluttering when tired (155.4) says the fuel comes from the body.
Where would a wild Cyndaquil live? The games never put one in the wild; 'grassland' is the only habitat on record.
Is it active by day or night?
Does it ever start grass fires when startled?
Why 87.5% male, and what does that mean for a wild population (a game convention for starters, or biology)?

Delibird.summary: A cliff-nesting bird of cold mountains that carries its food bundled in its tail wherever it goes, ferries it to its chicks all day, and throws it at anything that attacks. Several entries add that it shares that food with people lost in the mountains, and tell of an explorer who reached the top of Mt. Everest thanks to one; the tales are kept under folklore here. No entry says what the food actually is. In HeartGold and SoulSilver it lives only in SoulSilver's Ice Path.

anatomy.text: A winged body, 0.9 m and 16.0 kg, typed Ice and Flying.
It carries its food bundled up, or rolled up, in its tail.
anatomy.analogy: Clark's nutcracker (Nucifraga columbiana), a bird of western North American mountains, carries pine seeds in a pouch under its tongue to its caches.

anatomy.text: Whether the tail is a pouch or a wrap is not said; 'bundled' and 'rolled' suggest the tail folds around the load.

diet.text: No entry says what its food is.
It carries food all day long and always has it with it, wherever it goes.
Its only level-up move is Present (Lv 1), the games' version of handing over, or throwing, a parcel.
The Water 1 egg group and the egg move Splash hint at a tie to water, perhaps fishing, but nothing says it eats fish.
diet.note: Egg groups are a breeding mechanic, not a diet record.

habitat.text: It nests at the edge of sharp cliffs, in the mountains.
In HeartGold and SoulSilver it is a SoulSilver exclusive: 20% on all four Ice Path floors (1F, B1F, B2F, B3F) at any time of day, Lv 22-23. In HeartGold the same 20% slot holds Zubat instead.

Silver also had it at all times; Crystal only at night (40%); Gold not at all. Elsewhere: Icefall Cave in FireRed only (5%), and swarms on Route 216 (Diamond, Pearl) and Route 217 (Platinum). The Gen 3 Pokédex habitat is mountain.
It is met inside the Ice Path but nests on cliffs, so the cave is probably where it travels or shelters rather than where it breeds.

behavior.text: It spends all day carrying food to its waiting chicks.
It has a habit of sharing food with people lost in the mountains.
behavior.note: Stated as a habit in Diamond, Pearl and Platinum; the older entries tell it as tales.

behavior.text: Vital Spirit (it can't fall asleep) suits an animal said to work all day.
All-day food carrying points to a day-active bird, but Crystal's tables have it only at night and the HGSS tables don't split it.

social.text: Parents provision their chicks at the nest.
Whether it nests alone or in cliff colonies is not said.
Sharing food with lost people is an unusual habit: it gives a resource to another species at a cost to itself.

reproduction.text: It raises chicks in a nest at a cliff edge and feeds them all day.
Water 1 and Field egg groups, 20 egg cycles, even sex ratio.

defense.text: If attacked, it throws its food at the opponent.
Present is the game form of that throw.
Throwing the food spends the provisions it carries for its chicks, so it is presumably a last resort.

senses.text: Nothing is said about its senses. Finding lost people implies it notices them, but how is not described.

life_cycle.text: A single-stage species: no evolution in Generations I-IV.
Chicks are fed at the nest; nothing describes how long they stay or when they fledge.

moves_in_the_wild.text: Present is its only level-up move, the narrowest wild repertoire in the highlands community. Everything else is an egg move, a tutor move or a machine (Fly among them), so its wild behaviour has to be read from the entries, not the moves.

ecology.text: A carrier: it moves food from wherever it forages to cliff nests, so it shifts nutrients across the landscape, with spillage and droppings collecting below the nests.
ecology.note: Follows from the carrying habit; scale unknown.
ecology.analogy: Seabird colonies fertilise the cliffs and slopes below them with droppings, producing nutrient-rich soils.

ecology.text: No predator of Delibird is named. In SoulSilver it shares the Ice Path with Golbat, which drinks the blood of Pokémon.
ecology.note: Co-occurrence plus Golbat's stated diet only.

ecology.text: Its trophic level can't be set until its food is known.

humans.text: Its reputation is as a saviour of people lost in the mountains: it shares its food with them.
A famous explorer is said to have reached the peak of Mt. Everest thanks to a Delibird sharing its food.
humans.note: A single anecdote; filed under folklore as well.

homestead.text: It carries a bundle of food all day; it could carry small loads, such as a parcel between the homestead and Blackthorn, if it can be trained to carry something other than its own food.
homestead.note: Load size and willingness to carry objects are unknown.

homestead.text: A companion for Ice Path crossings: its habit of sharing food with lost people makes it the community's closest thing to a mountain rescuer.
homestead.note: The habit is described for wild birds and lost strangers; untested in a trained one.

homestead.text: Ice-typed, so it would be at home in the highland winter.
It would need a high ledge or cliff shelf to nest on, and something to carry.
The homestead's Delibird as the post: a bird that turns up at the door with a tail-bundle from town.

niche.foraging: unknown food, carried in the tail all day and delivered to chicks

relationships.note: Nest sites.
Graveler gouge horizontal holes in sheer cliff faces; a cliff-nesting bird could use them. Neither entry mentions the other.
Shares the Ice Path in SoulSilver; Golbat drinks Pokémon blood. Untested.

ecotypes.name: Nest guard
ecotypes.reading: Three moves that strike first. A lineage that defends nest and food by hitting before it is hit, instead of throwing its food away. Fits crowded cliff ledges where thieves come close.
ecotypes.behavior: Keeps its bundle; drives intruders off fast.

ecotypes.name: Snow roller
ecotypes.reading: Two rolling moves: a lineage that travels downslope by rolling, bundle and all. Fits long, open snowfields above the Ice Path, where rolling is cheaper than flying.
ecotypes.behavior: Comes down the mountain tumbling; walks or flies back up.

ecotypes.name: Far-seer
ecotypes.reading: A foresight move is odd for a bird. A lineage reading ahead could be the one behind the tales of Delibird appearing for lost travellers; Aurora Beam is a light display that would carry in the dark of the Ice Path. The most speculative of the three.
ecotypes.behavior: Turns up where it is needed before it is called.

open_questions: What food does it carry, and where does it get it?
Is it day-active (all-day carrying, 225.2) or night-active (Crystal's night-only tables)?
Does it nest in the Ice Path, or only on cliffs outside it?
How does it find lost people (225.6), and why share food meant for its chicks?
Should the reconstruction treat Delibird as present in the Ice Path (SoulSilver, where it takes a 20% slot) or absent (HeartGold, where Zubat takes that slot)?
Its egg groups (Water 1, Field) and the egg move Splash hint at water. Does it swim or fish?

folklore.text: There are tales about lost people who were saved by the food it carried.
A famous explorer reached the peak of Mt. Everest thanks to a Delibird sharing its food.

Dewgong.summary: The pure white adult of Seel, a streamlined swimmer of frigid seas with ice floes. Dewgong stores thermal energy in its body and swims a steady eight knots even in intensely cold water; the colder it gets, the friskier and more active it becomes. It sleeps under shallow water by day and looks for food at night when it is cold, loves to snooze on bitterly cold ice, and its white coat hides it from predators in snow. A mariner long ago mistook one asleep on a glacier for a mermaid. In HeartGold and SoulSilver it lives in the Seafoam Islands.

anatomy.text: A sea-lion body (Gen 4 shape fish), 1.7 m and 120.0 kg, typed Water and Ice.
Its body is snowy white, covered with pure white fur.
Its streamlined body has little drag in water, and it uses its long tail to change direction quickly.
It stores thermal energy in its body.
anatomy.analogy: Marine mammals keep warm in icy water with blubber and a high metabolic rate.

diet.text: It looks for food at night, when it's cold.
The food isn't named. Seel hunts prey under ice (86.6), so the line is a cold-water predator; fish are likely but unrecorded.

habitat.text: Frigid seas with ice floes; it snoozes on bitterly cold ice and on glaciers. The Gen 3 Pokédex habitat is sea.
In HeartGold and SoulSilver it lives only in the Seafoam Islands (walking, 24%, Lv 35-38), at any time, in both versions.

behavior.text: It sleeps under shallow ocean waters during the day, then looks for food at night when it's cold.
The colder the temperature, the friskier it gets; the colder the weather, the more active it becomes.
It swims at a steady 8 knots even in intensely cold waters and is unharmed by intense cold.

social.text: Nothing is said about groups.

reproduction.text: Water 1 and Field egg groups, 20 egg cycles, an even sex ratio, medium growth.

defense.text: In snow, its pure white coat obscures it from predators.
defense.analogy: Harp seal pups are white, hidden on the ice for their first weeks.

defense.text: Thick Fat resists fire and ice; Sheer Cold (Lv 34, learned on evolving) is its strongest blow.

senses.text: Nothing is said about its senses.

life_cycle.text: It evolves from Seel at level 34, from 1.1 m and 90.0 kg to 1.7 m and 120.0 kg, gaining the Ice type.

moves_in_the_wild.text: Seel's list with Signal Beam and Sheer Cold added: Icy Wind, Encore, Ice Shard, Rest, Aqua Ring, Aurora Beam, Aqua Jet, Brine, Sheer Cold, Take Down, Dive, Aqua Tail, Ice Beam and Safeguard.

ecology.text: A night-feeding cold-water predator at the top of Seafoam's small web, with the Gyarados.
It has predators, by its own entry (its coat hides it from them), but none is named.

humans.text: A mariner long ago mistook a Dewgong asleep on a glacier for a mermaid.

homestead.text: Happiest in the coldest weather: the highland winter would suit it better than any summer.
A fast, steady swimmer in icy water: it could tow a small boat across a cold lake.
homestead.note: Towing untested.

homestead.text: It sleeps by day under shallow water; it needs a cold pool with a shallow end.
The 'mermaid' of the Blackthorn lake, seen once in a winter dawn by the postman.

niche.foraging: looks for food at night, when it's cold
niche.note: Food never named; filed as a predator with Seel.

relationships.note: Never named.
To sleep on.

ecotypes.name: Floe sleeper
ecotypes.reading: A lineage that defends its sleeping place: a startling first strike, a move that stops a move, and a doom-song that ends a long fight. The 'mermaid' singing on the ice. Fits floes and glaciers.
ecotypes.behavior: Sleeps in the open and drives off what wakes it.

ecotypes.name: Ice-hole driller
ecotypes.reading: Seel's horn lineage, grown up: the Dewgong that keeps breathing holes open for others under the ice. Fits seas that freeze over.
ecotypes.behavior: Keeps holes open all winter.

open_questions: What does Dewgong eat at night?
What preys on it, that its white coat hides it from (87.10)?
How does it store thermal energy (87.1)?
Do Seel and Dewgong live together in Seafoam, or apart?

folklore.text: The sight of a Dewgong sleeping on a glacier was mistaken for a mermaid by a mariner long ago.

Diglett.summary: A tiny mole that lives about a yard underground, feeding on plant and tree roots. Diglett's skin is very thin: in light its blood heats up and it grows weak, so it prefers dark places and sticks its head out only when the sun isn't bright. It burrows at a shallow depth, leaving raised earth in its wake, and wherever it digs through a field it leaves the soil perfectly tilled for planting, which is why Diglett are raised on most farms. Its tunnels are sometimes Onix's, which Diglett use as homes. In HeartGold and SoulSilver it fills Diglett's Cave, the tunnel between Route 2 and Vermilion City, and is found on Route 48 and under the rocks of Vermilion.

anatomy.text: A tiny burrower (Gen 4 shape blob), 0.2 m and 0.8 kg, typed Ground: the Mole Pokémon.
Its skin is very thin. If it is exposed to light, its blood heats up, causing it to grow weak.

diet.text: It feeds on plant roots, about one yard underground, and chews on tree roots.
diet.analogy: Real pocket gophers and mole rats live underground on roots and tubers.

habitat.text: Underground, about a yard down, at a shallow depth; it prefers dark places and may pop up in caves. The Gen 3 Pokédex habitat is cave.

In HeartGold and SoulSilver it is nine encounters in ten in Diglett's Cave (Lv 13-19), with Dugtrio; it is also on Route 48 in Johto (Lv 20, rarely), under the rocks of Vermilion City by Rock Smash, and in the Johto Safari Zone; at any time, in both versions.

behavior.text: It spends most of its time underground; it sometimes appears above ground, sticking its head out only when the sun isn't bright.
Because of its dark habitat, it is repelled by bright sunlight.
It leaves raised earth in its wake, making it easy to spot.
behavior.analogy: Real moles leave the same raised ridges across a lawn.

behavior.text: Above ground it would be out at dawn, dusk or on dull days, by the entries; underground, time of day hardly matters, and the tables have it at any time.

social.text: Nothing is said about Diglett living together. Diglett's Cave holds them nine in ten, so they live densely where they live.
Its evolved form is three Diglett: triplets that emerged from one body and think exactly alike (51.6).

reproduction.text: Field egg group, 20 egg cycles, an even sex ratio, medium growth. Nothing describes how it breeds.

defense.text: It stays underground, out of reach.
Arena Trap keeps foes from fleeing and Sand Veil hides it in sandstorms; Dig (Lv 18) and Sucker Punch (Lv 23) are strikes from below and before.

senses.text: Its thin skin reacts to light: light heats its blood. That is the one sense-like thing the entries give it.

life_cycle.text: It becomes Dugtrio at level 26: from 0.2 m and 0.8 kg to three heads, 0.7 m and 33.3 kg.

moves_in_the_wild.text: Scratch, Sand Attack, Growl, Astonish, Magnitude, Mud-Slap, Dig, Sucker Punch, Earth Power, Mud Bomb, Slash, Earthquake and Fissure: digging and shaking the ground.

ecology.text: A soil-maker: wherever it burrows, the soil is left perfectly tilled for planting crops.
ecology.analogy: Real burrowing animals turn and aerate soil the same way.

ecology.text: A root-eater: it takes from the plants above it.
It lives in tunnels Onix leaves: Onix's tunnels are used as homes by Diglett (95.2).
In Diglett's Cave it lives with nothing but its own line: one of the simplest communities in Kanto.

humans.text: Diglett are raised on most farms, because wherever it burrows the soil is left perfectly tilled for growing delicious crops.

homestead.text: Raised on most farms to till the soil: the homestead's plough.
A digger, at a shallow depth.
It eats plant and tree roots: keep it in the vegetable field before planting, and away from the orchard.
Give it shade and dark places; bright sun weakens it.
Rows of raised earth across the potato field every spring morning, and one small brown head watching the clouds.

microhabitat: shallow burrows about a yard underground
niche.foraging: eats plant and tree roots underground
niche.note: Activity left open: underground, and above ground only when the sun isn't bright.

relationships.note: It tills the soil as it burrows.
It uses Onix's tunnels as homes.

ecotypes.name: Colony ambusher
ecotypes.reading: A lineage of crowds: Beat Up calls on every ally, Pursuit and Feint Attack strike the one that runs or looks away. Fits dense colonies like Diglett's Cave.
ecotypes.behavior: Pops up in numbers around an intruder.

ecotypes.name: Stony-ground digger
ecotypes.reading: A lineage of hard ground: rocks, old power and clods of mud. Diglett that dig through stony mountain soil rather than farm fields. Fits rocky caves and hillsides.
ecotypes.behavior: Digs deeper and comes up less often.

open_questions: If Diglett eat plant roots, how do farms that raise them keep their crops?
Does Diglett dig its own tunnels, or mostly use Onix's?
How do three Diglett come to be one Dugtrio?
What eats Diglett, underground?

Ditto.summary: A small purple blob that can become anything. Ditto rearranges its whole cellular structure to transform into whatever it sees, copying an opponent's genetic code to become an almost perfect duplicate. The copy fails in two ways: if made to laugh it can't hold the disguise, and if it transforms from memory rather than sight it gets the details wrong. When it sleeps it turns into a stone so it won't be attacked, and when it meets another Ditto it hurries to copy it exactly.
