Does the brain change at evolution make every Gyarados violent, or only some?
Should the red Gyarados of the Lake of Rage count as part of the lake's community?

folklore.text: It is said that the change in its brain cells at evolution is to blame for its wildly violent nature.
They say that during past wars and strife, Gyarados would appear and leave blazing ruins in its wake.

Haunter.summary: The middle stage of the Gengar line, and the most plainly predatory: Haunter lurks in total darkness, silently stalking its next victim, and steals life force by licking with a tongue made of gas. A victim it licks or touches starts shaking and can't stop, until death in the older entries. It slips through walls and lurks inside them to watch, and if one beckons you while floating in the dark, the entries say never to go. It still weighs only 0.1 kg. In HeartGold and SoulSilver it lives on Route 8, at night, one encounter in three.

anatomy.text: A gas body with arms (Gen 4 shape arms), 1.6 m and 0.1 kg, typed Ghost and Poison: the Gas Pokémon.
Its tongue is made of gas, and it has gaseous hands.
It can slip through any obstacle, block walls included.

diet.text: It licks with its gaseous tongue to steal the victim's life force; it will try to lick a person and steal their life away.
It lurks in darkness for prey.
It hides in the dark, planning to take the life of the next living thing that wanders close by.
Life force taken by licking makes it an energy-feeder rather than a flesh-eater: nothing is said to be consumed.

habitat.text: Darkness: total darkness where nothing is visible, and the inside of walls. The Gen 3 Pokédex habitat is cave.
In HeartGold and SoulSilver it is wild only on Route 8, between Saffron and Lavender, at night (30%, Lv 19), in both versions; the Johto Safari Zone has it only when its blocks call for it.
Gold and Silver had it on Route 8 too; Crystal also put it in Rock Tunnel at night.

behavior.text: In total darkness Haunter lurks, silently stalking its next victim.
It beckons while floating in darkness; anyone who approaches will be licked.
It lurks inside walls to keep an eye on its foes, and likes to tap shoulders in the dark with a gaseous hand.
If you feel watched in darkness when nobody is around, Haunter is there.
Nocturnal: every HeartGold and SoulSilver table has it at night only.

social.text: Nothing is said about groups; every entry describes a lone stalker.

reproduction.text: Amorphous egg group, 20 egg cycles, an even sex ratio, medium-slow growth; nothing describes breeding.

defense.text: Haunter is a dangerous Pokémon.
It passes through walls and hides inside them, and Levitate and its Ghost type leave little that can hit it.
Destiny Bond (Lv 50) takes its attacker down with it, and Spite and Curse punish what fights it.

senses.text: It stalks in total darkness, where nothing is visible, so it finds its victims by something other than sight; what is not said.

life_cycle.text: It evolves from Gastly at level 25 and becomes Gengar only by trade, going from 0.1 kg to 40.5 kg.
It is where the line's gas grows limbs and a tongue: a feeding apparatus, where Gastly could only envelop.
In the games no wild Haunter becomes a Gengar: that needs a trade, so every Gengar comes through people.

moves_in_the_wild.text: Lick at level 1, the feeding act; Mean Look to keep the victim from leaving; Hypnosis, Dream Eater and Nightmare to feed on the sleeping; Shadow Punch (Lv 25, learned on evolving), the gaseous hand.

ecology.text: A night predator of life force on Route 8; whatever it licks is drained but, by the entries, not eaten.
On Route 8 at night it shares the grass with Meowth, Noctowl, Vulpix, Growlithe and Abra. No entry names a predator of Haunter.

humans.text: The entries warn people directly: if one beckons you in the dark, never approach; it will try to lick you and steal your life away.
Its touch causes endless shuddering, and the older entries say the shaking lasts until death.

homestead.text: Not a Pokémon to leave near people at night. Its lick drains life.
It can pass through any obstacle and watch from inside walls: a scout that no door keeps out.
A night guard, if its stalking can be turned on intruders, and only if it can be trusted with the household.
homestead.note: Untested, and the entries give every reason for caution.

homestead.text: The feeling of being watched in the homestead's cellar, explained.

niche.foraging: stalks in darkness and licks to steal life force
niche.note: Psychotroph, as for Gengar: it takes life force, not flesh. Trophic level left null.

relationships.with: the life force of its victims
darkness and the inside of walls

ecotypes.name: Death-song haunt
ecotypes.reading: Gengar's most sinister lineage, in its stalking stage: a song that dooms everyone who hears it and a grudge that drains whatever kills it. A Haunter that makes a place deadly to stay in. Fits old towers and ruins.
ecotypes.behavior: Its haunt empties of other life over time.

ecotypes.name: Fist of shadow
ecotypes.reading: Three elemental punches carried by the line: a Haunter whose gaseous hands strike rather than tap. Fits places with trainers and rivals to fight, where a stalker has to defend its dark corner.
ecotypes.behavior: Taps shoulders, then hits.

open_questions: What is the life force it takes, and does taking it kill (the older entries) or only exhaust?
Why Route 8, in grass by a road, when every entry puts it in total darkness?
Does it live alone?
How does it find victims in total darkness?

contradictions.note: Yellow and SoulSilver say the shaking lasts until death; Platinum says only that its touch causes endless shuddering.

folklore.text: Because it can slip through block walls, it is said to be from another dimension.

Heracross.summary: A great horned beetle, clad in a steel-hard shell, that gathers in forests seeking the sweet sap of trees, its favourite food, and loves sweet honey. Usually docile, it chases off anyone who disturbs it while it sips, and hurls rivals away with its prized horn to keep the honey to itself: it charges, slips under a foe, and scoops up and flings it, with power enough to throw 100 times its own weight or topple a massive tree. Clawed feet planted in the ground or in bark give it footing. In HeartGold and SoulSilver it lives in the trees, shaken out by Headbutt, on Johto's Routes 33, 42, 44, 45, 46, 47 and 28, at Azalea Town and Mt. Silver, and in Kanto at Vermilion, Celadon and Routes 7, 11 and 16.

anatomy.text: A big upright beetle (Gen 4 shape humanoid), 1.5 m and 54.0 kg, typed Bug and Fighting: the Single Horn Pokémon.
Completely clad in a steel-hard shell, with a prized horn.
Sharp claws on its feet, planted firmly in the ground or in tree bark; powerful legs.

diet.text: Tree sap is its favourite food; Heracross gather in forests seeking the sweet sap of trees.
diet.analogy: Real rhinoceros and stag beetles feed on tree sap, and males fight over the best sap flows.

diet.text: It loves sweet honey, and sips it.
Bug Bite, from the move tutor, is an eating move in game form.

habitat.text: Forests, where it gathers at sap trees; the Gen 3 Pokédex habitat is forest.

In HeartGold and SoulSilver it lives in trees, found by Headbutt, at any time, in both versions: on Routes 33, 42, 44, 45, 46 and 47 and at Azalea Town in Johto; on Route 28 and at Mt. Silver (Lv 39-48); and in Kanto at Vermilion City, Celadon City and Routes 7, 11 and 16.

behavior.text: It is usually docile, but if it is disturbed while sipping honey it chases off the intruder with its horn.
It charges in a straight line at its foe, slips beneath the foe's grasp, and scoops up and hurls the opponent with its horn.
Its activity pattern is not stated; the Headbutt tables have it at any time.

social.text: Heracross gather in forests at sap trees: a feeding gathering.
To keep all the honey to itself, it hurls rivals away with its prized horn.
Gathering together yet fighting over the food: competition at a shared, limited resource.

reproduction.text: Bug egg group, 25 egg cycles, an even sex ratio, slow growth; it does not evolve. Nothing describes how it breeds.

defense.text: A steel-hard shell, and the horn: it throws foes over great distances.
Swarm and Guts make it stronger when hurt or ailing; Endure, Counter (Lv 25) and Reversal (Lv 43) turn a beating into a counterattack.

senses.text: Nothing is said about its senses; it finds sap trees in the forest, so it can find them somehow.

life_cycle.text: It does not evolve: hatched as Heracross and stays one, 1.5 m and 54.0 kg.
No larval stage is recorded, unlike real beetles.
life_cycle.analogy: Real beetles hatch as grubs and pupate before becoming adults.

moves_in_the_wild.text: Night Slash, Tackle, Leer, Horn Attack, Endure, Fury Attack, Aerial Ace, Brick Break, Counter, Take Down, Close Combat, Reversal, Feint and Megahorn: the horn and the throw.

ecology.text: A sap and honey feeder: it lives on what trees give and on honey.
It has power enough to topple a massive tree: in a forest, a disturbance as well as a feeder.
On Kanto's headbutt trees it lives beside Combee, which gather honey from flowers (415.2); Heracross loves honey and keeps it to itself. They would compete, if they meet at the same honey.
In Johto's trees it shares the bark with Aipom nearly everywhere, and with Spearow on most routes.

humans.text: Nothing is said about Heracross and people; it is docile unless disturbed while feeding.

homestead.text: Strength: it can throw around an object 100 times its own weight, and topple a massive tree. The homestead's logger and hauler.
Clearing ground: felling and moving trees.
Never disturb it at the honey or the sap; keep the beehives where it can't reach them.
The stump-puller, at work, and the bowl of honey that is its wage.

niche.foraging: sips tree sap and honey, and drives rivals off

relationships.note: Both want honey; they share Kanto's headbutt trees.

ecotypes.name: Sap-tree holder
ecotypes.reading: A lineage that holds its tree: it hardens, takes the blows and returns them double. Fits forests with few sap trees and many rivals.
ecotypes.behavior: Will not leave its sap flow, whatever hits it.

ecotypes.name: Intruder-chaser
ecotypes.reading: The chaser of 214.2: it runs down what it disturbs and charges with everything. Fits busy woods where it is disturbed often.
ecotypes.behavior: Chases intruders a long way from the tree.

open_questions: Where do Heracross find honey: in Combee hives, or in flowers?
Does it hatch as a grub, or as a small adult?
Why does it gather with others if it fights them for the food?
Does it damage the trees it feeds from?

Hoothoot.summary: A small owl with a perfect sense of time. Hoothoot stands on one foot, switching feet too fast to see, and begins to hoot at precisely the same time every day, thanks to an internal organ that tracks the Earth's rotation; some trainers use it as a clock. No entry says what it eats or when it is active, but HeartGold and SoulSilver meet it in grass only at night, and in Ilex Forest it is the animal most often shaken out of the Headbutt trees.

anatomy.text: A small owl (0.7 m, 21.2 kg) that always stands on one foot.
It switches its standing foot so quickly that the movement can rarely be seen.
anatomy.analogy: Many real birds rest on one leg, which is thought to cut heat loss from the bare legs.

anatomy.text: It has an internal organ that senses and tracks the Earth's rotation.

diet.text: Not stated in any entry.
Its evolved form catches prey in darkness, and Hoothoot's own moves include Peck (Lv 9) and Foresight (Lv 1), so it is most likely a small predator.
In Ilex Forest the larvae and pupae of its common Headbutt trees are the obvious candidates (see Relationships).
diet.note: Rests on sharing the same trees and on size; no entry links them.

habitat.text: A forest animal. In HeartGold and SoulSilver it is in Ilex Forest's common (60%) and rare (50%) Headbutt trees, in Headbutt trees across Johto from New Bark Town to Ecruteak City, and in grass at night on Routes 29 to 31 and 35 to 37 and in National Park.
Its nearest records to Blackthorn are the Headbutt trees of Route 43 and the Lake of Rage.
It lives in the trees, in both kinds of Headbutt tree, which puts it alongside every other tree-dweller in the forest.

behavior.text: It begins to hoot at precisely the same time every day.
Whatever happens, it keeps rhythm by tilting its head precisely in time.
Nocturnal by the encounter tables: every grass record of Hoothoot in HeartGold and SoulSilver is at night. Headbutt records have no time of day, and no entry states its activity.

social.text: Nothing is said about groups or pairs. Its daily hoot at a fixed time might be a signal to others, but no entry says who hears it.
social.note: A reading of the hooting; untested.

reproduction.text: Flying egg group, 15 egg cycles, an even sex ratio. Nothing in the Pokédex describes nesting or young.

defense.text: Even when attacked it doesn't brace itself on both feet.
Its abilities are Insomnia (it can't be put to sleep) and Keen Eye (its accuracy can't be lowered); Hypnosis (Lv 5) and Reflect (17) are its defensive moves.

senses.text: A perfect sense of time, from an organ that senses the Earth's rotation.
senses.analogy: Real animals keep time with internal circadian clocks that run on their own and are reset each day by light, not by sensing the Earth's rotation; in birds the pineal gland is part of that clock.

senses.text: Keen Eye and Foresight suggest sharp sight, and its evolved form sees in near darkness.

life_cycle.text: Hoothoot becomes Noctowl at level 20; the adult is larger (1.6 m, 40.8 kg), sees in near darkness and flies silently onto prey.

The timekeeping entries all belong to Hoothoot and Noctowl's are all about vision, silent flight and thought: read as development, the young owl is described by its clock and the adult by its hunting.

moves_in_the_wild.text: Peck (9) and Take Down (25) for attack; Uproar (13) is a loud, sustained call; Confusion (21), Zen Headbutt (33) and Extrasensory (37) are psychic.
Foresight (Lv 1) lets it hit targets that evade, which reads as a knack for finding hidden prey.
Dream Eater (49) works only on a sleeping target and follows Hypnosis, but Hoothoot evolves at 20, so a wild one almost never has it.

ecology.text: Probably a small nocturnal predator of the canopy (trophic level about 3), though its diet is undescribed.
Being in both Headbutt tables, it overlaps every other tree-dweller: the larvae and pupae of the common trees, and Pineco, Butterfree or Beedrill, and Noctowl in the rare ones.
Bird Pokémon peck Pineco by mistake; Hoothoot and Noctowl are Ilex Forest's only birds, so they are the likely culprits.

humans.text: Some trainers use them in place of clocks.
Platinum says it marks time precisely, and that some countries regard it as a wise friend (see Folklore).

homestead.text: A living clock: it hoots at precisely the same time every day, which would mark a daily routine with no equipment.
Night watch: a night-active bird with keen eyes in the trees around the homestead would notice movement after dark; a Noctowl would do it better.
homestead.note: Its night activity rests on encounter tables only.

homestead.text: Local: it lives in the Headbutt trees of Route 43 and the Lake of Rage, the nearest records to Blackthorn. It needs trees to perch in and a quiet day roost.

niche.foraging: unknown; probably a perch-based hunter of small animals, as its evolved form hunts in darkness

relationships.note: HeartGold: both in the common Headbutt trees, and a 0.3 m larva is within reach of a 0.7 m owl. Caterpie is day-active and Hoothoot night-active, so it would be a larva resting in foliage, and Caterpie's stench (10.3) is aimed at exactly such enemies.
SoulSilver: same trees and sizes as for Caterpie; Weedle's warning colours and barb make it a risky meal.
An immobile pupa in the same trees; whether a peck gets through an iron-hard shell is doubtful.
As for Metapod, plus a poison barb.
Attempted only: birds peck Pineco by mistake and its shell protects it.
Same rare Headbutt trees, same nights; Noctowl is more than twice the size, so they may take different prey.
Rare Headbutt trees, HeartGold.
Rare Headbutt trees, SoulSilver.

ecotypes.name: Sound hunter
ecotypes.reading: A lineage that hunts by sound in deeper darkness: an ultrasonic call and an attack out of the dark. Fits dense, dark forest like Ilex, where sight alone fails.
ecotypes.behavior: Calls more and hunts later into the night.

ecotypes.name: Canopy ambusher
ecotypes.reading: A lineage that drops onto prey from a perch without warning. Fits closed-canopy forest with plenty of perches and prey on the branches.
ecotypes.behavior: Waits motionless on one foot, then strikes from above.

ecotypes.name: Display mimic
ecotypes.reading: A lineage given to social display: copying others' actions and showy feather displays. Fits dense owl populations where neighbours have to be told apart and territories advertised.
ecotypes.behavior: Mirrors rivals and fluffs its feathers at them.
ecotypes.analogy: In real birds, ritualised feather displays are mostly for courtship and territory.

open_questions: What does it eat?
Is it nocturnal? Only the encounter tables say so.
What is the time-sensing organ, and what is the daily hoot for: territory, contact, courtship?
At what time does it hoot, and does the time shift with the seasons?
Why does it stand on one foot, even under attack?

folklore.text: Some countries consider it a wise friend, versed in the world's ways.
folklore.note: A belief people hold about it, not a description of the animal.

Hoppip.summary: A tiny pink plant-like Pokémon so light (0.5 kg) that it drifts on the wind. Hoppip must grip the ground firmly with its feet to keep from being blown away, and can be carried off by the gentlest breeze, even all the way to the next town. When it senses strong winds coming, it links its leaves with other Hoppip so they cling together, and they gather in clusters against the wind, though they enjoy gentle breezes. It is said that when Hoppip gather in fields and mountains, spring is on the way. In HeartGold and SoulSilver it lives by day on Routes 32, 33 and 48 in Johto and Routes 13, 14 and 15 in Kanto.

anatomy.text: A tiny upright plant-animal (Gen 4 shape upright), 0.4 m and only 0.5 kg, typed Grass and Flying: the Cottonweed Pokémon.
Its body is so light it must grip the ground firmly with its feet to keep from being blown away.
It has leaves, which it links with other Hoppip.

diet.text: No entry says what Hoppip eats or how it feeds.
Synthesis (Lv 4) is a sunlight-healing move and Chlorophyll speeds it in sunshine: in game terms a sun-dependent plant, so it most likely lives on sunlight as plants do.
diet.note: Read from a move, an ability and a type, not an entry.

diet.text: Mega Drain (Lv 25), Giga Drain (Lv 37) and Leech Seed (Lv 22) drain other living things: in principle it could feed that way too.
diet.note: Battle moves; no entry says it.

habitat.text: Fields and mountains, where it gathers in spring by the saying; the Gen 3 Pokédex habitat is grassland.
In HeartGold and SoulSilver it lives on Routes 32 and 33 by day and morning, on Route 48 at any time, and on Kanto's Routes 13, 14 and 15 by day and morning, in both versions.
A wind-drifter's range is wherever the wind takes it: it may even float all the way to the next town.

behavior.text: It drifts and floats with the wind; it can be carried away on even the gentlest breeze.
behavior.analogy: Dandelion and thistle seeds travel the same way, on a parachute of fluff.

behavior.text: They do enjoy gentle breezes.
Diurnal: the HGSS tables have it by day and morning only except on Route 48.

social.text: To keep from being blown away by the wind, they gather in clusters.
If it senses strong winds approaching, it links its leaves with other Hoppip to prepare against being blown away.
Linking together against the wind is cooperation for survival, the clearest of any small Pokémon in Kanto.

reproduction.text: Fairy and Grass egg groups, 20 egg cycles, an even sex ratio, medium-slow growth. Nothing describes how it breeds.
Gathering in spring is when many animals breed; the saying doesn't say so.

defense.text: Its powders are its defences: Poison Powder (Lv 12), Stun Spore (Lv 14), Sleep Powder (Lv 16) and Cotton Spore (Lv 28). Leaf Guard keeps off status in sun.
Its main danger in the entries is the wind itself.

senses.text: It senses the approach of strong winds.

life_cycle.text: It becomes Skiploom at level 18 and Jumpluff at 27: 0.4 m and 0.5 kg, then 0.6 m and 1.0 kg, then 0.8 m and 3.0 kg.
Skiploom is found with it on Route 14 by day.

moves_in_the_wild.text: Splash, Synthesis, Tail Whip, Tackle, the three powders, Bullet Seed, Leech Seed, Mega Drain, Cotton Spore, U-turn, Worry Seed, Giga Drain, Bounce and Memento: seeds, spores and a hop.

ecology.text: A tiny producer in the web: if it lives on sunlight, it sits with the plants at the bottom.
ecology.note: Its diet is unrecorded.

ecology.text: A wind-drifter carries itself, and anything stuck to it, between places: a disperser of seeds and spores by the habit, if not by any entry.
ecology.note: Speculative.

ecology.text: Half a kilogram makes it prey-sized for almost anything; on Routes 13 to 15 Pidgeotto hunts by day where it lives, but nothing names Hoppip as prey.
ecology.note: Co-occurrence and size only.

humans.text: People read its gatherings as a sign: when Hoppip gather in fields and mountains, spring is on the way.

homestead.text: A spring herald for the highland farm: watch the fields for its clusters.
Keep several; a lone Hoppip in a highland wind will be blown away. It needs others to link with.
Its powders (sleep, stun, poison) need care around livestock.
The first Hoppip of the year, gripping the fence post at the top of the meadow with both feet.

niche.foraging: unknown; read as a sun-fed plant from Synthesis and Chlorophyll
niche.note: No entry gives its diet.

relationships.note: It drifts on it.

ecotypes.name: Linked-leaf colony
ecotypes.reading: A lineage of the clusters: helping, healing and keeping a partner at its task. Hoppip that link leaves against the wind and stay linked. Fits windy uplands.
ecotypes.behavior: Never drifts alone; clusters at the first gust.

ecotypes.name: Psychic drifter
ecotypes.reading: An odd lineage for a plant: psychic moves carried by the line. Perhaps the Hoppip that sense the wind earliest. Fits open hills where weather changes fast.
ecotypes.behavior: Links up before anyone else feels the wind change.

open_questions: What does Hoppip eat? Sunlight, soil, or something it drains?
How far does it drift, and does it come back?
Is the spring gathering a breeding gathering?
What eats Hoppip?

folklore.text: It is said that when Hoppip gather in fields and mountains, spring is on the way.

Horsea.summary: A small sea-horse of coral and rock, the first stage of the rival's Kingdra. Horsea eats small insects and moss off rocks, and is known to shoot down flying bugs with precision blasts of ink from the surface. It swims by flicking the fins on its back, moving in any direction or even backwards while still facing forward, anchors itself with its coiled tail when the current runs fast, and nests in the shade of corals. When danger comes it sprays a dense black ink and flees. In HeartGold and SoulSilver it lives in the Whirl Islands and the deepest floor of the Seafoam Islands.

anatomy.text: A small water animal (Gen 4 shape blob), 0.4 m and 8.0 kg, typed Water: the Dragon Pokémon.
It swims by flapping or flicking the fins on its back, which lets it move in any direction, or backwards, while still facing forward.
anatomy.analogy: Real seahorses swim upright the same way, driven by a fast-beating dorsal fin.

anatomy.text: Its tail is wound up like a coil; it keeps its balance with it and wraps it round rocks or coral to hold on in a fast current.
It can spray water, or a special dense black ink, from its mouth.

diet.text: Horsea eats small insects and moss off of rocks.
It is known to shoot down flying bugs with precision blasts of ink from the surface of the water.
diet.analogy: Archerfish knock insects off overhanging leaves with jets of water from below the surface.

diet.text: In the sea caves where the Johto games put it there are no flying insects to shoot, so there it would take the small animals and growth on the rocks: the sea's equivalent of insects and moss.
Water Gun (Lv 11), Octazooka (an egg move: an ink shot) and Bubble are its shooting moves.

habitat.text: The sea, among coral and rock: it nests in the shade of corals and anchors to rocks; the Gen 3 Pokédex habitat is sea.

In HeartGold and SoulSilver it lives in the Whirl Islands (1F, B2F: surf 30-60%, Good Rod 10%, Super Rod 30%) and on the Seafoam Islands' B4F (surf 30%, Lv 30-40), at any time of day, in both versions.
Both are sea caves, the sheltered, current-swept water a tail-anchoring, nest-building sea-horse would choose.

behavior.text: If attacked by a larger enemy, it quickly swims to safety by adeptly controlling its dorsal fin.
If the current turns fast it wraps its tail round rocks or coral so it isn't washed away.
Its activity pattern is not stated; the HGSS tables have it at any time.

social.text: When they're in a safe location, they can be seen playfully tangling their tails together.
Tail-tangling in safety reads as social or courtship behaviour between Horsea.
social.analogy: Seahorse pairs link tails and 'dance' each morning as part of their pair bond.

reproduction.text: It makes its nest in the shade of corals.
In Seadra the male raises the young (117.5), so the line's fathers care for the brood.
reproduction.analogy: In real seahorses the male carries the eggs in a brood pouch until they hatch.

reproduction.text: Water 1 and Dragon egg groups, 20 egg cycles, an even sex ratio, medium growth.

defense.text: If it senses danger, it reflexively sprays a dense black ink, or murky ink, and tries to escape.
defense.analogy: Squid and octopuses escape behind a cloud of ink.

defense.text: Smokescreen (Lv 4) is the ink cloud in game form; Agility (Lv 23) the fast escape.

senses.text: It senses danger quickly enough to ink reflexively, and aims ink precisely at flying bugs from under the surface, so it sees well through water and air.
Sniper, one of its abilities, powers up critical hits: the precision of the ink shot in game form.

life_cycle.text: It becomes Seadra at level 32 and Kingdra only by trade while holding a Dragon Scale: 0.4 m and 8.0 kg, then 1.2 m and 25.0 kg, then 1.8 m and 152.0 kg.
Read as development, the line moves from a shallow, ink-squirting forager to a spiny, poisonous predator to a sleeper of the deepest sea floor.

moves_in_the_wild.text: Ink and water: Bubble, Smokescreen, Water Gun, Bubble Beam, Brine, Hydro Pump. Escape: Agility. And the dragon in it: Twister (Lv 26), Dragon Dance (Lv 38) and Dragon Pulse (Lv 42).

ecology.text: A small grazer and insect-eater of rock and coral, low in the web: on the evidence, it eats both small animals and moss or algae.
It flees larger enemies; in Seafoam those would include Gyarados and Golduck, and in the Whirl Islands Tentacruel, but no entry names a predator.
ecology.note: Co-occurrence and size only.

humans.text: Nothing is said about Horsea and people. Its evolved form's fins and bones are prized in traditional medicine (117.4), which makes the whole line a target for harvest.

homestead.text: It would need sea water with rock or coral to anchor to and shade to nest in: not a homestead animal unless a saltwater pool is built for it.
A precise ink shot at flying insects: around a pond, a natural insect control.
homestead.note: Untested in fresh water.

homestead.text: Its ink is a defence, not a mess to clean: give it calm water and it won't use it.
A pair of Horsea with tails tangled in the shade of the dock, the morning the rival comes to visit.

microhabitat: coral and rock in sea caves
niche.foraging: picks small insects and moss off rocks; shoots flying bugs down with ink from the surface

relationships.note: To anchor in currents and to nest in the shade of.

ecotypes.name: Ink archer
ecotypes.reading: The insect-shooting lineage the oldest entry describes: an ink shot and a beam. A Horsea that hunts at the surface for flying bugs. Fits sheltered shallows and mangrove-like edges with insects overhead, not deep caves.
ecotypes.behavior: Hangs just under the surface, aiming upward.

ecotypes.name: Storm-drake
ecotypes.reading: A lineage that leans into the dragon it will become: dragon fire and a wind-blade, in a 0.4 m sea-horse. The line most likely to reach Kingdra. Fits stormy, current-swept caves like the Whirl Islands.
ecotypes.behavior: Bolder than other Horsea; inks less, fights more.

open_questions: What does it eat in sea caves, where there are no flying bugs to shoot?
Is tail-tangling play, courtship or pair-bonding?
Does the male Horsea brood the young, as Seadra's male raises them (117.5)?
Does the 'moss' it eats mean algae on sea rocks?

Houndoom.summary: A black, horned hound of rough country and the rival's FireRed Pokémon. Houndoom lives in packs led by the one whose horns rake sharply back, and the pack chooses its leader by fighting. Its flame is made by toxins burning in its body: it smells pungent, and a burn from it is said to hurt forever. Its eerie howl sends other Pokémon shivering back to their nests, and people long ago imagined it was the call of the grim reaper. Its young, Houndour, are cooperative pack hunters that corner prey with barks only they understand. In HeartGold and SoulSilver, Houndoom is found only in the Johto Safari Zone; Houndour lives on Kanto's Route 7 at night.

anatomy.text: A four-legged hound (Gen 4 shape quadruped), 1.4 m and 35.0 kg, typed Dark and Fire, with horns.
The pungent-smelling flame that shoots from its mouth comes from toxins burning in its body; the flames it breathes when angry contain those toxins.
A flame made by burning toxins means its body makes something combustible and poisonous, an internal chemistry, not an outside fuel.

diet.text: No entry says what Houndoom eats.
Its young hunt as a coordinated pack and corner prey with barks only they understand (228.2, 228.4), so the line is a pack predator.
Bite (Lv 17), Fire Fang (Lv 32) and Crunch (Lv 54) are a hound's bite; Odor Sleuth (Lv 22) the tracking nose.

habitat.text: The Gen 3 Pokédex habitat is rough terrain.

In HeartGold and SoulSilver Houndoom is found only in the Johto Safari Zone, when its peak blocks are placed (10%, Lv 43-44). Houndour is wild on Kanto's Route 7 at night (5%), and in the Safari Zone.
A wild Houndoom of Kanto would be expected near Route 7, between Celadon and Saffron, where its young live; the games show none there.

behavior.text: Upon hearing its eerie howls, other Pokémon get the shivers and head straight back to their nests.
Its young howl at dawn to announce their territory (228.3).
Early Bird, one of its abilities, wakes it quickly from sleep; Houndour is found only at night on Route 7. The line's activity leans to the dark hours and dawn.

social.text: It lives in packs; the one with its horns raked sharply back serves as leader, and they choose their leader by fighting among themselves.
social.analogy: Wolf packs have a breeding pair at their head, though rank is settled more by family than by fighting.

social.text: Its young use a variety of cries to communicate and to corner prey; their teamwork is said to be unparalleled.
Beat Up (Lv 28), a move that calls on every ally to strike, is the pack's attack in game form.

reproduction.text: Field egg group, 20 egg cycles, an even sex ratio, slow growth. Nothing describes breeding or who in the pack breeds.

defense.text: Its flame's burn is said to hurt forever: if you are burned by it, the pain will never go away.
Flash Fire, its other ability, turns fire attacks into power: fire can't hurt it.
Its howl is a defence by fear: it clears other Pokémon from the area.

senses.text: Nothing is said about its own senses. Odor Sleuth and its young's bark-based teamwork suggest a nose and ears for hunting.

life_cycle.text: It evolves from Houndour at level 24, from 0.6 m and 10.8 kg to 1.4 m and 35.0 kg.
Read as development, the young's cries for cornering prey become the adult's howl that empties the hills: the same voice, turned from teamwork to intimidation.

moves_in_the_wild.text: Howl, Smog, Roar (Lv 14), Bite, Odor Sleuth, Beat Up, Fire Fang, Feint Attack, Embargo, Flamethrower, Crunch and Nasty Plot. Smog at level 1 is the toxic smoke of its flame; Howl and Roar its voice.

ecology.text: A pack predator of rough terrain, near the top of any web it lives in; its prey is never named.
Its howl sends other Pokémon back to their nests: the pack shapes when and where other animals move, a landscape of fear.
ecology.analogy: Wolves change where elk feed by making some places riskier: the 'landscape of fear'.

ecology.text: Managed in the Safari Zone, it has no wild Johto or Kanto web of its own.

humans.text: Long ago, people imagined its eerie howls to be the call of the grim reaper.
A burn from its flame is said never to stop hurting.

homestead.text: A guard animal by voice: its howl sends other Pokémon home to their nests, which could keep pests and raiders off at night.
Its flames carry toxins and leave burns that don't heal well: never use it as a cooking fire.
A pack animal that settles rank by fighting: keep only one, or a family, and expect challenges.
The rival's Houndoom, howling once at dusk from the ridge above Blackthorn, and the Swinub running for the Ice Path.

niche.foraging: pack hunting: its young corner prey together using cries
niche.note: The line's pack hunting is from Houndour's entries; Houndoom's own diet is never stated.

relationships.note: They flee to their nests; read as the pack pushing others out of the area.
Both in the Johto Safari Zone.

ecotypes.name: Coursing pack
ecotypes.reading: A lineage that hunts the way the Houndour entries describe: chase the runner, all strike together, feint to break the prey's guard. Fits open, rough country where prey runs.
ecotypes.behavior: Hunts in a tight pack; rarely alone.

ecotypes.name: Hellfire hound
ecotypes.reading: A lineage whose toxic fire lingers: a burn that won't heal, a trapping ring of flame, and a spiteful move. The hound of the grim-reaper stories. Fits dark ravines and old ruins.
ecotypes.behavior: Lets its fire do the work; burns and waits.

open_questions: What does a Houndoom pack hunt?
Where do wild Houndoom live in Kanto or Johto, outside the Safari Zone?
What toxins burn in its body, and where do they come from (229.3)?
Does the leader fight for rank every season, or once?

folklore.text: Long ago, people imagined its eerie howls to be the call of the grim reaper.

Infernape.summary: A fast, fire-crowned primate of high crags that fights with all four limbs. The line starts as Chimchar, which climbs sheer cliffs to live on craggy mountaintops and burns gas made in its belly as a flame at its rear; that flame is a signal as well as a weapon, weakening when the animal is sick and, in Monferno, showing rank in the pack. Infernape carries its fire as a crown and on its hands and feet, and its fire never goes out. Nothing in the Pokédex says what any stage eats, and no game has it in the wild.

anatomy.text: An upright, primate-like animal (1.2 m, 55.0 kg) with a crown of fire on its head and fire on its hands and feet.
In Chimchar the fuel is a gas made in the belly, burned at the rear end.
anatomy.analogy: Mammal guts do make flammable gases (methane and hydrogen from microbial fermentation), though no real animal burns them.

anatomy.text: Whether Infernape's head and limb fires run on the same belly gas is not said.

diet.text: No entry for any stage says what the line eats.
Whatever it eats has to feed both the animal and a fire that never goes out, so its food needs are probably high for its size.

habitat.text: Chimchar climbs sheer cliffs to live on top of craggy mountains.
Monferno uses ceilings and walls to launch attacks from above, which fits overhangs, caves or cliff faces.
It is not found in the wild in any Gen I-IV game. Chimchar is a starter gift at Lake Verity in Diamond and Pearl and on Route 201 in Platinum; no Johto game offers it.
No Gen 3 habitat is given, because the line is from Generation 4.

behavior.text: Extremely fast and agile: beaten by none in quickness, and it throws its enemies around.
Bold to the point of recklessness: it will take on any opponent.
Chimchar puts out its tail flame when it sleeps; Platinum says it does so on purpose, to prevent fires.
No entry gives a time of day for activity.

social.text: Monferno lives in packs with ranks: a bigger tail fire and a brighter blue pattern on the face mean higher rank.
social.analogy: Male mandrills (Mandrillus sphinx) show rank the same way: dominant males have brighter red and blue facial colour.

social.text: A fire that burns weakly when the animal is sick makes the flame an honest signal of condition, which is the kind of signal a ranked pack can rely on.
Whether Infernape still lives in packs is not said; the entries describe it only as a fighter.

reproduction.text: Field and Human-Like egg groups, 20 egg cycles, 87.5% male (the usual starter ratio). Nothing in the Pokédex describes breeding or young.

defense.text: Monferno manages distance with fire: it stretches its tail flame to look bigger and intimidate attackers, and controls the flame's intensity to keep foes at the range it wants.
Infernape's defence is attack: a martial art using all four limbs, with fire on its hands and feet.
Chimchar's fire survives rain.
Blaze, its only ability, strengthens its Fire moves when it is badly hurt.

senses.text: Nothing is said about its senses. Reading rank from flame size and the brightness of a blue face pattern implies good colour vision in Monferno.

life_cycle.text: Chimchar (0.5 m, 6.2 kg, Fire) becomes Monferno at level 14 (0.9 m, 22.0 kg, Fire/Fighting) and Infernape at level 36 (1.2 m, 55.0 kg).
The fire moves through development: at the rear in Chimchar, on the tail in Monferno (as a weapon and a rank badge), then a crown on the head and flames on the hands and feet in Infernape.
The young can put the fire out; the adult cannot, or does not: Chimchar's flame goes out in sleep, Infernape's never goes out.
Read as development, the line shifts from a climber that avoids trouble to a pack animal that displays, to a fighter that seeks out opponents.

moves_in_the_wild.text: No wild Infernape exists in the games, so the level-up list is the species' own repertoire, not observed behaviour. Provocation first: Leer, Taunt (Lv 1 and 9), and in Chimchar, Torment; then speed, with Mach Punch (Lv 14), which matches 'beaten by none in quickness'.
Flame Wheel (Lv 21), a rolling charge wrapped in fire, and Close Combat (Lv 41) fit an animal that fights with all its limbs; Fire Spin (Lv 45) traps an opponent in flame.
Chimchar (Lv 39) and Monferno (Lv 46) learn Slack Off, a rest-and-recover move, which sits well with a young animal that puts its fire out to sleep; Infernape does not learn it.
Fire Punch and Thunder Punch reach this line both as egg moves and as tutor moves; when a trained Infernape uses them, they are more likely taught than inherited.

ecology.text: Its role in a food web is unknown, because its diet is.

A permanent fire on an animal living on dry mountain crags is a wildfire risk; Chimchar's habit of putting out its flame before sleep 'to prevent fires' shows the line's fire can and does ignite its surroundings.

humans.text: Its line reaches people as a Sinnoh starter, handed to new trainers at Lake Verity or on Route 201.
No entry describes a working relationship with people; the record is entirely about fighting.

homestead.text: A heat source that doesn't need fuel from the woodpile: Infernape's fire never goes out, and Chimchar's survives rain.
That same fire needs managing: keep it away from hay, timber and the Glasshouse's dry stores. A young Chimchar puts its flame out to sleep; an adult cannot be relied on to.
A free health check: Chimchar's flame burns weakly when it feels sick.
At home on Blackthorn's crags: the line climbs sheer cliffs and lives on craggy mountains, so steep ground is its habitat, not an obstacle. Rock Climb is a taught move, but the climbing is its own.
A guard that will take on anything, with hands that can grip; whether that boldness can be trained into deterrence rather than picking fights is untested.
homestead.note: Boldness is canon; its usefulness as a guard is a guess.

homestead.text: Hauling and clearing would be taught: Strength, Rock Smash and Cut are machines, not its own moves.
If several are kept, expect a rank order: in Monferno the size of the tail fire and the face pattern decide it.

niche.foraging: unknown; no entry says what any stage eats
niche.note: Guild guessed from the primate-like body plan and Human-Like egg group only. The machine reading's 'thermotroph' comes from the Fire type alone.

relationships.with: gas made in its own belly
relationships.note: Its fuel, at least in Chimchar.

ecotypes.name: Four-limb striker
ecotypes.reading: The canon fighting style made heritable: burning fists, a burning kick, and a two-footed kick. A lineage that commits to close striking with hands and feet rather than flame at range. Fits narrow ledges where there's no room to keep distance.
ecotypes.behavior: Closes in fast and strikes with every limb; uses its fire as a glove, not a torch.

ecotypes.name: Troop helper
ecotypes.reading: A cooperative lineage: Helping Hand strengthens a packmate's attack, Assist borrows a packmate's move, and Fake Out makes an attacker flinch so the group can act first. Fits the ranked packs Monferno lives in, on crags where a troop defends one stretch of cliff together.
ecotypes.behavior: Fights alongside others and covers them; low-ranked animals that make themselves useful.

ecotypes.name: Cliff trickster
ecotypes.reading: A lineage that wins by reading its opponent: Encore locks an attacker into repeating its last move, Counter returns physical blows, and Focus Energy readies a decisive hit. Together they make fights short and predictable. Fits crowded cliff colonies where conflicts are frequent and must not be costly.
ecotypes.behavior: Baits, waits and punishes; rarely the first to commit.

open_questions: What does any stage eat, and what in the diet becomes the belly gas that fuels the fire?
Do Infernape's head, hand and foot fires run on the same gas as Chimchar's rear flame?
Can an Infernape put its fire out at all, or does 'never goes out' (392.1) mean it can't?
Does Infernape still live in a ranked pack, and does its crown fire signal rank as Monferno's tail does?
Where does a wild population live? The games give it only as a Sinnoh starter.
Is it diurnal? Chimchar's sleep habits are described but never their timing.

contradictions.text: Chimchar's flame and sleep: Diamond says its fire is put out when it sleeps, as if passively; Platinum says it puts the flame out itself before sleeping, to prevent fires.
contradictions.note: Probably compatible (a deliberate act that happens at sleep), but the two entries describe different agency.

contradictions.text: Across the line: Chimchar's fire goes out when it sleeps, but Infernape's never goes out.
contradictions.note: Different stages, so this may be development (the adult loses or gives up control of the flame) rather than a true contradiction.

Jolteon.summary: Jolteon is the Thunder Stone form of Eevee, a 0.8 m, 24.5 kg Electric type that makes its own lightning. Its cells give off weak charges, which it concentrates and amplifies through the static of its fur to drop thunderbolts of 10,000 volts. When it is charged, angered or startled every hair stands up into sharp, charged needles that pierce attackers, and Platinum has it launching them in small bunches. A sensitive animal, it charges up with every change of mood, and its fur crackles constantly. Like every Eevee form it is never wild in Gen I–IV.

anatomy.text: A light quadruped of 0.8 m and 24.5 kg, Electric type.
Its cells generate a low level of electricity, which it concentrates into lightning bolts.
anatomy.analogy: Electric eels (Electrophorus) work the same way in principle: thousands of modified muscle cells, each producing a small voltage, discharge together to deliver several hundred volts.

anatomy.text: Its fur amplifies that power with static electricity, and the bristling fur is made of electrically charged needles.
Negatively charged ions generated in its fur make a constant sparking noise.

diet.text: No entry says what Jolteon eats.

It can take in electricity: Volt Absorb heals it when it is hit by an Electric move, and the Red, Blue and LeafGreen entries have it gathering negative ions from the atmosphere. That is energy uptake, but nothing shows it replaces food.
diet.note: The machine reading's 'electrotroph' came from its type; these are the only pieces that bear on it.

habitat.text: Gen 3 Pokédex habitat: urban, the same as every Eevee form, which probably reflects where people get Eevee rather than a wild habitat.

Not found in the wild in any Gen I–IV game. Eevee is a gift in Celadon City, at Bill's house in Goldenrod City, a Game Corner prize in the Johto games, and a gift in Hearthome City; it is wild only in Sinnoh's Trophy Garden after the National Pokédex.

behavior.text: A sensitive animal that easily becomes sad or angry, and every change of mood charges it up.
Its fur sparks audibly all the time.
Its activity pattern is unknown.

social.text: No entry describes how it lives with its own kind.
An animal whose charge rises with its mood would be unpredictable company; close quarters with others of its kind, or with people, may keep it charged.
social.note: An extension of 135.2, not a described behaviour.

reproduction.text: Field egg group, 35 egg cycles, 87.5% male.
Its eggs hatch as Eevee, so Jolteon doesn't breed true; each young takes its own adult form.

defense.text: If angered or startled, the fur all over its body bristles like sharp needles that pierce attackers.
defense.analogy: Porcupine quills are modified hairs that the animal raises when threatened.

defense.text: When agitated it uses electricity to straighten its fur and launch it in small bunches.
defense.analogy: Many New World tarantulas defend themselves by kicking clouds of barbed hairs off the abdomen at an attacker.

defense.text: Every hair stands sharply on end when it becomes charged, so the needle defence and the charge are linked.
Pin Missile (Lv 36), a volley of needles, is its needle fur in move form; Thunder Wave (Lv 57) paralyses, and Volt Absorb turns an opponent's electricity to its own benefit.

senses.text: Nothing is said about its senses. 'Sensitive' in 135.2 refers to its temperament.

life_cycle.text: Eevee (0.3 m, 6.5 kg) becomes Jolteon when exposed to a Thunder Stone; Jolteon is nearly four times Eevee's mass.
Eevee's entries describe this as mutation caused by radiation from evolutionary stones acting on its irregular genetic code.
Unlike Espeon and Umbreon, Jolteon needs no bond with a person to form, only a stone. Like the other stone forms, it could in principle arise wherever an Eevee meets the right mineral.

moves_in_the_wild.text: Electric attacks by level-up: Thunder Shock (Lv 15), Thunder Fang (Lv 43), Thunder (Lv 71) and Discharge (Lv 78).
Speed: Quick Attack (Lv 22) and Agility (Lv 64), with Double Kick (Lv 29) as a hind-leg strike.
These describe what a Jolteon could do on its own; no game has wild ones to observe.

ecology.text: Its role in any wild community is unknown: no diet, no wild population and no predators or prey are named.

humans.text: Its thunderbolts are described at 10,000 volts, enough to make it dangerous to handle when upset.
Almost every Jolteon in these games comes from an Eevee given to someone and a stone a person provides.

homestead.text: An electricity source: it generates charge in its own cells. Whether it could charge a battery steadily, and how often, is untested.
homestead.note: The capability records list battery-charging as gear, not as anything an entry describes.

homestead.text: A deterrent: bristling needle fur, a crackling coat and thunderbolts would keep most wild animals off.
Flash, a taught move, makes it a light source for the Glasshouse or a barn.
Keep it calm and keep it away from hay and kindling: its fur sparks constantly and its charge rises with every upset.
Groom with care: startling it raises the needles, and in Platinum's account it can launch them.

niche.foraging: not described
niche.note: Diet is never stated, so no guild or trophic level is given. It can take in electricity (Volt Absorb, 135.1), but that is not shown to be food.

relationships.note: Only the Red, Blue and LeafGreen entries say this; later entries put the source in its cells (see contradictions).
Needed for Eevee to become Jolteon.

ecotypes.name: Last-spark sprinter
ecotypes.reading: Detect sidesteps an attack, Endure survives one that should fell it, and Flail hits harder the closer the user is to defeat. With Jolteon's speed (Quick Attack, Agility), the set describes a lineage that relies on escape first and a desperate counterattack second. Fits open, exposed ground with little cover.
ecotypes.behavior: Runs at the first sign of trouble; cornered, it is at its most dangerous.

ecotypes.name: Mood-charger
ecotypes.reading: Fake Tears and Charm are both emotional displays, one of distress and one of appeal. If every change of mood charges Jolteon, a lineage that displays its feelings often would also stay charged. Fits life in groups, or close to people, where displays get answered.
ecotypes.behavior: Sulks, pleads and sparks in turn; never quite discharged.

open_questions: Where does its electricity come from: the air, its cells, or its moods? (see contradictions)
What does it eat?
Can it shed or regrow its needle fur, and how quickly after launching it?
Could it charge a battery or light a lamp steadily without harm?
Does the constant sparking make it a fire risk around dry material?
Could Jolteon arise in the wild where Eevee and Thunder Stones occur together?

contradictions.note: Red, Blue and LeafGreen (135.1, 135.9) say it gathers negative ions from the atmosphere; Gold, HeartGold, Ruby, Sapphire and Emerald (135.3, 135.6, 135.7) say its own cells produce weak charges that it concentrates and amplifies; Yellow (135.2) says it charges up with every change of mood. Crystal (135.5) has the ions generated in its fur. These may be parts of one system, but each entry names a different source.

Jynx.summary: A humanoid Ice and Psychic Pokémon, every one of them female, that moves as if dancing and appears to use the dance to communicate. Its cries sound like human speech and come in several patterns that seem to carry different meanings, but nobody has worked out what it says. The dancing is contagious: people who watch it find themselves swaying along without meaning to. Nothing in the Pokédex says what it eats or how a species without males reproduces. In HeartGold and SoulSilver it is an uncommon find on every floor of the Ice Path, met more often by day.

anatomy.text: A humanoid body, 1.4 m and 40.6 kg, typed Ice and Psychic; the games give it no males (0% male).
It rocks its body rhythmically and wiggles its hips as it walks.
In the young form, Smoochum, the lips are the most sensitive part of the body and the first thing used to examine anything; the Jynx entries don't say whether this persists.

diet.text: No entry says what Jynx eats.

Its wild moves are close-contact ones: Pound, Lick (Lv 5), Double Slap (Lv 15), Ice Punch (Lv 18), Body Slam (Lv 39), Wring Out (Lv 44), with Lovely Kiss (Lv 8), which puts a target to sleep, and Mean Look (Lv 21), which stops it escaping. If it takes animal food, the kit fits capture at arm's length.
diet.note: Moves explain biology but don't define a diet; nothing says Jynx hunts.

diet.text: Smoochum tests everything by touching it with its lips, which remember what it likes and dislikes: a taste-led animal that learns its foods.

habitat.text: In HeartGold and SoulSilver it is on all four Ice Path floors (1F, B1F, B2F, B3F): 5% at any time plus another 5% by day, Lv 22-23. It is also on Seafoam Islands B4F (12%, Lv 38-40).

Gold and Silver had the same pattern (10% by day, 5% morning and night); Crystal has it only on B1F-B3F, by day and morning. Platinum puts it in Snowpoint Temple. In Red, Blue, FireRed and LeafGreen it is only an in-game trade in Cerulean City (for a Poliwhirl).
Wherever it is wild, it is inside a cold cave or ice-bound building: the Ice Path, Seafoam Islands' lowest floor, Snowpoint Temple.
Its Gen 3 Pokédex habitat is 'urban', which fits none of its wild locations; it may reflect its humanlike form or the Cerulean trade rather than where it lives.

behavior.text: It moves to a rhythm of its own, sashaying as if it were dancing.
It appears to alter the rhythm depending on how it is feeling.
The Ice Path tables lean to daytime in every Johto game, which hints at a day-active animal.
behavior.note: Time-of-day slots are a weak guide inside a cave.

social.text: It seems to use dancing to communicate.
social.analogy: Honeybees (Apis mellifera) communicate the direction and distance of food with the waggle dance.

social.text: It has several different cry patterns, each of which seems to have its own meaning.
social.analogy: Vervet monkeys give acoustically distinct alarm calls for leopards, eagles and snakes, and listeners respond to each differently.

social.text: Its cries sound like human speech; it is said to speak a language similar to that of humans, but it is impossible to tell what it is trying to say.
Group size is not described.

reproduction.text: Human-Like egg group, 25 egg cycles, and no males. Smoochum, its young form, is a baby Pokémon in the Undiscovered egg group.
How an all-female population reproduces in the wild is not described anywhere.
reproduction.analogy: Some real vertebrates are all-female and reproduce by parthenogenesis, such as several whiptail lizards (Aspidoscelis).

defense.text: Forewarn lets it determine what moves a foe has: an early warning of what it is facing. It also has Oblivious.
Its dancing compels people to dance in unison with it; if that works on would-be attackers too, it is a defence by distraction, as Lovely Kiss is in game terms.
defense.note: The entries describe the effect on people only.

defense.text: Fake Tears (Lv 25) and Perish Song (Lv 49) round out a defence built on display and sound more than strength.

senses.text: Forewarn reads as a sense: it perceives what an opponent can do before the opponent acts.
Smoochum's lips remember what it likes and dislikes; touch and taste are its first senses as a juvenile.

life_cycle.text: It evolves from Smoochum at Lv 30, growing from 0.4 m and 6.0 kg to 1.4 m and 40.6 kg, keeping Ice and Psychic.
Smoochum runs about actively but falls often, and checks its reflection on a lake's surface to see its face isn't dirty: the juvenile lives near still water.
Smoochum has no wild encounters in HeartGold and SoulSilver, so the highlands have no recorded juveniles.

moves_in_the_wild.text: Lovely Kiss (Lv 8) puts others to sleep by contact, and Smoochum examines everything with its lips: the kiss is the line's way of meeting the world, in moves as in entries.
Powder Snow (Lv 11), Avalanche (Lv 33) and Blizzard (Lv 55) are its cold-weather moves; Perish Song (Lv 49) is a song, fitting a vocal animal.

ecology.text: At 40.6 kg it is one of the larger animals in the Ice Path, and nothing records what it eats; it is one of the community's biggest unexplained energy demands.
No predator of Jynx is named. Golbat, which drinks the blood of people and Pokémon, shares every Ice Path floor.
ecology.note: Co-occurrence and Golbat's stated diet only.

humans.text: Its motions are so alluring that people who see it are compelled to shake their hips without noticing, and it can cause people to dance in unison with it.
Research is under way to work out what its humanlike language says.
People trade for it: in the Kanto games it is obtained from a trader in Cerulean City.

homestead.text: A humanoid body with hands; in principle it could handle tools.
homestead.note: Nothing describes Jynx using objects.

homestead.text: Ice-typed, with Powder Snow and Icy Wind: possibly a way to keep a cold store cold in summer.
homestead.note: Untested whether its cold is controllable or lasting.

homestead.text: A hazard to plan for: people near it may be compelled to dance, which matters around tools, ledges and livestock.
Its distinct cries could become shared signals with the household, if their meanings can be learned.
homestead.note: Researchers haven't decoded them (124.8).

homestead.text: At the homestead a Jynx keeps the rhythm for long work days, and nobody can say quite why the hay gets in faster.

niche.foraging: unknown; the level-up moves are close-contact, with a sleep-inducing kiss

relationships.note: Its cries resemble human speech. Resemblance only; nothing says it imitates people deliberately.
Shares every Ice Path floor; Golbat drinks the blood of people and Pokémon. Untested.
SoulSilver only.

ecotypes.name: Mirror troupe
ecotypes.reading: Psych Up copies another's state and Wish sends help to whoever is there a moment later: a social lineage that synchronises with and supports others, the move-level echo of making others dance in unison. Fits the larger chambers of the Ice Path, where several could gather.
ecotypes.behavior: Dances in groups; tends the hurt.

ecotypes.name: Clear-eyed
ecotypes.reading: Miracle Eye sees through evasion and Meditate is focus. A perceptive lineage that finds what hides, on top of Forewarn; fits the dark lower floors of the Ice Path.
ecotypes.behavior: Watches more than it dances; the first to notice an intruder.

ecotypes.name: Cold fist
ecotypes.reading: A contact lineage that strikes first and hits with cold fists. Fits passages it shares with Golbat, where it has to defend itself rather than charm.
ecotypes.behavior: Less dance, more fist.

open_questions: What does Jynx eat?
How does an all-female species reproduce in the wild?
What do the dances and the distinct cries mean? Is the 'language similar to that of humans' (124.4) a language at all?
How does its dancing compel people to move (124.6): a psychic effect, or contagious behaviour?
Where are the young? No wild Smoochum appear in HeartGold or SoulSilver.
Why does the Gen 3 Pokédex give its habitat as urban?

contradictions.text: Silver/SoulSilver says it speaks a language similar to humans' but seems to use dancing to communicate; FireRed says it speaks a language that sounds human and research is under way; Diamond/Pearl/Platinum says only that its cries sound like speech and that it is impossible to tell what it means.
contradictions.reading: The entries differ on whether this is a language or just speech-like sound, and on whether speech or dance is how it communicates. Not resolved here.

Kakuna.summary: The pupa of the Beedrill line. Kakuna clings to or leans against stout trees, or hides under leaves and in the angles of branches, almost unable to move while its body is remade inside a hardening shell. It is not defenceless: it can move a little and push out a poison barb if attacked. The shell grows hot to the touch from the work going on inside. In SoulSilver it is met in Ilex Forest's grass in the morning and by day and in the common Headbutt trees.

anatomy.text: A yellow shell (0.6 m, 10.0 kg) that hardens on the outside while the body within grows softer.
A poison barb or stinger that it can extend from the shell.
The shell becomes hot to the touch.
FireRed calls it 'a temporary stage while making its body'.

diet.text: It doesn't feed. No entry mentions food, and every entry describes it waiting, nearly immobile, for evolution.
diet.analogy: Real insect pupae do not feed; they live on reserves laid down by the larva.

habitat.text: On trees: it clings to a tree or leans against stout trees.
Under leaves and in nooks of branches, where it hides from predators.

In SoulSilver it is in Ilex Forest's grass (30% in the morning and by day, none at night) and common Headbutt trees (10%), on Routes 30 and 31, in National Park, in Route 47's secret Headbutt trees, and in Kanto on Route 2 (including a night record, 11%) and in Viridian Forest. In HeartGold it appears only in the Bug-Catching Contest.

behavior.text: Virtually immobile: almost completely unable to move on its own, though it can move a little.
Still on the outside, extremely busy on the inside as it prepares for evolution.
The time-of-day pattern in its tables reflects where and when pupae are found, not activity.

social.text: Nothing is said about other Kakuna. The machine reading's 'solitary' isn't backed by any entry.

reproduction.text: In the games Kakuna is in the Bug egg group (15 egg cycles) and can breed; a pupa isn't a reproductive stage, so this is a game convention.

defense.text: Hardening its shell is its main protection from predators.
When attacked or endangered it may stick out its stinger and poison the attacker.
defense.analogy: Real pupae aren't always helpless: many wriggle when touched, and some beetle pupae pinch attackers with 'gin traps' between their abdominal segments.

defense.text: Concealment: it hides under leaves and in nooks of branches.
Its only level-up move is Harden, so the barb is described but not given as a move; its ability, Shed Skin, may heal its own status problems.

senses.text: Nothing is said about its senses, though extending its barb 'if it is attacked' and hardening 'when it is in danger' imply it can tell when it is threatened. The capability records turn this into danger sense.

life_cycle.text: From this form it will grow into an adult: Weedle becomes Kakuna at level 7, and Kakuna becomes Beedrill at level 10.
As its body softens the shell hardens: the outside sets while the inside is reorganised.
life_cycle.analogy: Complete metamorphosis: inside a real pupa much of the larval body is broken down and the adult is built from small clusters of cells (imaginal discs) carried over from the larva.

life_cycle.text: If the heat of the shell is metabolic, the pupal stage is expensive and runs on reserves built by Weedle's leaf-eating.
life_cycle.note: The entries give the heat as evidence of activity inside but don't say where it comes from.

moves_in_the_wild.text: Harden is all a wild Kakuna does. Its tutor moves (String Shot, Iron Defense, Bug Bite) are taught by people.

ecology.text: A non-feeding stage that takes nothing from the forest: a store of energy defended by shell, barb and hiding.
It uses trees as anchors and cover: stout trunks to lean on, branch nooks and leaves to hide in.
It has predators: two entries say its defences are against them, though none names one.

humans.text: Anyone handling one will find the shell hot, and it can push out its barb if it feels attacked.

homestead.text: It needs a stout tree or post to lean on, leaf cover, and to be left alone until it emerges.
Not a heater. The capability records list it as a heat source because the shell gets hot, but that heat is a by-product of a few levels' development, not a supply anyone could plan around.
Keep it away from curious hands: it can extend a poison barb when it feels attacked.

niche.foraging: none: a non-feeding pupa living on reserves from the larva
niche.note: No feeding guild applies. Trophic level 2 is its position as food: its body is built from Weedle's leaf-eating.

relationships.note: Trunks to lean on and cling to; branch nooks and leaves for cover.
It hides and hardens against predators; none is named.
Both in Ilex Forest's common Headbutt trees in SoulSilver; Hoothoot pecks (Peck, Lv 9). Shell and barb make it a poor target.
Version counterparts in Ilex Forest; together only in National Park's Bug-Catching Contest.

open_questions: What makes the shell hot, and how hot does it get?
Is the pupa wrapped in silk, as Caterpie's is (10.8)? No Weedle-line entry mentions silk.
Which predators does it hide from (14.1, 14.10)?
How long is the pupal stage in real time?
Can it extend the barb repeatedly, and is its poison Weedle's or Beedrill's?
The line has no HeartGold-SoulSilver egg moves, so no ecotypes can be read from breeding.

contradictions.text: Red/Blue and LeafGreen say it can only harden its shell to protect itself (14.1, 14.9); Yellow and Gold say it can stick out its stinger and poison an enemy (14.2, 14.3).
contradictions.note: The movement claims agree (almost immobile, or able to move a little); the disagreement is over whether hardening is its only defence.

Kingdra.summary: The adult of the Horsea line, and the rival's Crystal Pokémon: a 152 kg sea dragon that sleeps on the deepest sea floor, at depths where nothing else can survive, to build up its energy. When it moves it makes whirlpools, giant enough to swallow ships when it comes to the surface. Much of what is told of it is told as belief: that it hides in underwater caves, that its yawning makes spiralling ocean currents, that it causes tornadoes as it wakes, and that it wakes with storms to wander in search of prey. It is never wild in a Gen I-IV game: it comes only from trading a Seadra that holds a Dragon Scale.

anatomy.text: A large sea animal (Gen 4 shape blob), 1.8 m and 152.0 kg, typed Water and Dragon: the Dragon Pokémon.
It creates giant whirlpools every time it moves.
Its body is never described in its own entries; its spiny young (Seadra) bristle with poison, but Kingdra's abilities (Swift Swim, Sniper) carry no poison.

diet.text: When a storm arrives, it is said to awaken and wander about in search of prey.
diet.note: Told as belief ('is said').

diet.text: Its prey is never named. Its young swallow prey whole after weakening it in whirlpools (117.7); the adult's whirlpools would serve the same.
A sleeper on a lifeless sea floor must feed somewhere else: it stores energy by sleeping, and feeds when it rises.

habitat.text: Extreme ocean depths that are otherwise uninhabited: it sleeps on the seafloor, where no other life forms can survive, and lives in caves on the seafloor.
It is never wild in any Gen I-IV game: it comes only from trading a Seadra holding a Dragon Scale.
Its young live in the Whirl Islands and Seafoam, both sea caves; Kingdra's 'caves on the seafloor' are the deep end of the same world.

behavior.text: It sleeps deep on the ocean floor to build its energy; it sleeps quietly.
When it comes up to the surface it creates a huge whirlpool that can swallow even ships.
It can create whirlpools by yawning.
Its activity is set by sleep and storms, not by day and night: it rests to store energy and rises when a storm comes, by belief.

social.text: Nothing is said about Kingdra together. A sleeper in uninhabited depths is presumably alone.

reproduction.text: Water 1 and Dragon egg groups, 20 egg cycles, an even sex ratio, medium growth. Its line's males raise the young (Seadra, 117.5); nothing says Kingdra does.

defense.text: Nothing is said about how Kingdra defends itself. At depths where nothing else survives, nothing threatens it.
Its Dragon typing leaves it weak only to Dragon moves in the games: few attackers can hurt it much.

senses.text: Nothing is said about its senses. Waking with storms implies it senses them from the sea floor; how is not said.

life_cycle.text: It evolves from Seadra only by trade while holding a Dragon Scale, growing from 1.2 m and 25.0 kg to 1.8 m and 152.0 kg and gaining the Dragon type.
In the games every Kingdra comes through people, by trade with a Dragon Scale; there is no natural route in the data.

moves_in_the_wild.text: Yawn at level 1, the yawn that makes whirlpools in the entries; Twister, Brine, Hydro Pump, Dragon Dance (Lv 48) and Dragon Pulse (Lv 57).
Swift Swim, its ability, speeds it up in rain: the storm-woken hunter in game form.

ecology.text: A deep-sea sleeper that rises to hunt: it links the lifeless deep floor with the life above only through its own feeding trips.
With no wild Kingdra in any game, it has no place in a Johto or Kanto web.

humans.text: Its surfacing whirlpools can swallow ships: a hazard to sailors where it rises.
People long believed its yawn makes spiralling ocean currents and its waking makes tornadoes.

homestead.text: It is a deep-sea animal: Blackthorn's lakes and the Dragon's Den pool are no place for it.
Its whirlpools make any small body of water dangerous.
Swift Swim and Water type: a fast companion for crossing water in rain.
The rival's Kingdra, visiting, asleep at the bottom of the Dragon's Den pool and stirring the water only when the weather turns.

niche.foraging: sleeps to store energy; said to wake with storms and wander in search of prey
niche.note: The prey-seeking is told as belief (230.5); trophic level assumes it eats predators such as other fish.

relationships.note: Said, not stated.

ecotypes.name: Storm-drake
ecotypes.reading: The lineage the entries describe: a dragon that wakes with storms. Dragon fire and a wind-blade, carried down from Horsea. Fits open, stormy seas.
ecotypes.behavior: Rises with every storm.

ecotypes.name: Cold-deep sleeper
ecotypes.reading: A lineage of the coldest, deepest water: an ice beam, and two moves of an animal that thrashes in the shallows. A Kingdra that sleeps longest and rises least. Fits the coldest, deepest water.
ecotypes.behavior: Rarely seen at all; the whirlpools are the only sign.

open_questions: What does Kingdra eat, and how often does it rise to feed?
Does it really wake with storms (230.5), or is that belief?
Where does a Kingdra come from in the wild, when the games make it only by trade?
Does it hide in underwater caves (said, 230.1) or live in them (230.7)?

folklore.text: It is said that it usually hides in underwater caves.
It is said to cause tornadoes as it wakes.
It has long been believed that its yawning creates spiralling ocean currents.
When a storm arrives, it is said to awaken and wander about in search of prey.

Kingler.summary: The adult of Krabby, a crab with one claw grown massively, as hard as steel and said to have 10,000 horsepower of crushing force. The claw is too heavy for its own good: Kingler can hardly lift it, finds it hard to aim, staggers if it raises it too fast, tires quickly, and outside battle the claw just gets in the way. It waves the claw in the air to communicate with others. In HeartGold and SoulSilver it is fished along Johto's coasts and in Kanto it is the commonest Rock Smash find on Sea Route 19; it lives in the Seafoam Islands too.

anatomy.text: A crab (Gen 4 shape armor), 1.3 m and 60.0 kg, typed Water: the Pincer Pokémon.
One claw grew massively and as hard as steel; its pincers grow peculiarly large.
The large pincer has 10,000 horsepower of crushing force.
It is too heavy: unwieldy, hard to lift and difficult to aim.
anatomy.analogy: Male fiddler crabs carry one hugely enlarged claw used for display and fighting, at a real cost in feeding and movement.

diet.text: No entry says what Kingler eats. Its young swallow sand for nutrients when food is short (98.5).
A claw that crushes with great force would crack shellfish and hard prey, but no entry says it does.
diet.note: From the claw only.

habitat.text: The Gen 3 Pokédex habitat is waters-edge; its young live in burrows on sandy beaches (98.6).

In HeartGold and SoulSilver it is fished (Super Rod 10%) at Cherrygrove, Union Cave, Route 34, Olivine, Sea Route 40, Cianwood and the Whirl Islands, is smashed from rocks on Route 47, is the commonest Rock Smash encounter on Kanto's Sea Route 19 (90%), and is fished in the Seafoam Islands, at any time, in both versions.

behavior.text: If it lifts the pincers too fast, it loses its balance and staggers; because the claw is so heavy, it quickly tires.
Outside battle, the oversized claw just gets in the way.
Its activity pattern is not stated.

social.text: It waves its huge claw in the air to communicate with others.
social.analogy: Fiddler crabs wave their big claw to court females and warn rival males.

social.text: A claw that is a burden in daily life but a signal and a weapon reads as a sexually selected trait, but nothing says which sex waves, or why.
social.note: Both sexes are in the tables; the entries don't separate them.

reproduction.text: Water 3 egg group, 20 egg cycles, an even sex ratio, medium growth.

defense.text: The claw is its weapon: very powerful in battle.
Its young's pincers regrow (98.9); nothing says Kingler's great claw does.
Harden, Protect and Shell Armor protect it; Crabhammer (Lv 56) and Guillotine (Lv 37) are the claw's blows.

senses.text: Nothing is said about its senses.

life_cycle.text: It evolves from Krabby at level 28, from 0.4 m and 6.5 kg to 1.3 m and 60.0 kg.
Its pincers grow peculiarly large as it grows.

moves_in_the_wild.text: Krabby's list at later levels: Vise Grip, Leer, Harden, Bubble Beam, Mud Shot, Metal Claw, Stomp, Protect, Guillotine, Slam, Brine, Crabhammer and Flail.

ecology.text: Its diet is unrecorded; by its young, a shore scavenger that has grown a crushing claw, perhaps for hard-shelled food.
ecology.note: From the young and the claw only.

ecology.text: In Seafoam and on Sea Route 19 it shares rocks and water with Krabby, Seel, Tentacool and Staryu.

humans.text: Its strength is measured in an engine's terms, 10,000 horsepower.

homestead.text: Crushing power for breaking stone or cracking nuts, but it tires fast and can't aim well: short jobs only.
homestead.note: Untested.

homestead.text: It staggers if it raises the claw too fast: keep it on level ground.
A shore animal; it would need a sandy margin and salt or fresh water to match the tables.
The Kingler that waves at every boat on the lake, and nobody knows what it is saying.

niche.foraging: unknown; filed with Krabby, which forages on the shore and eats sand when hungry
niche.note: Kingler's own diet is never stated.

relationships.with: detritus washed up on the shore
relationships.note: Its young's habit.
Hard-shelled prey for a crushing claw; never named.

ecotypes.name: Claw-waver
ecotypes.reading: A lineage that makes the claw a display: a dance and a knock. The Kingler that communicates and challenges with its claw more than it crushes. Fits crowded shores with many neighbours.
ecotypes.behavior: Waves first, fights rarely.

ecotypes.name: Fossil-shore digger
ecotypes.reading: A lineage that digs the rocky shore and moves fast for its size: old-rock power, digging and speed. Fits rocky coasts with rubble, like Sea Route 19's rocks.
ecotypes.behavior: Lives under rocks rather than in sand.

open_questions: What does Kingler eat?
What does the claw-waving say (99.6), and to whom?
Does the giant claw regrow, as Krabby's pincers do?
Is the giant claw on one side only, and is it the same side in every Kingler?

Krabby.summary: A small red beach crab that lives in holes dug in the sand. Krabby's pincers are weapons and also its balance when it walks sideways; they break off easily but grow back fast, though one that has lost a pincer somehow can't walk sideways any more. When danger comes it cloaks itself in bubbles to look bigger. On sandy shores with little food Krabby squabble over territory, and one that can't find food will swallow a mouthful of sand for its nutrients. In HeartGold and SoulSilver it is fished all along Johto's coast and Kanto's Sea Route 19, and lives in the Seafoam Islands.

anatomy.text: A small crab (Gen 4 shape armor), 0.4 m and 6.5 kg, typed Water: the River Crab Pokémon.
Its pincers are powerful weapons and are used for balance when it walks sideways.
The pincers break off easily, in battle or when torn out of their sockets, and grow back fast, fully.
anatomy.analogy: Real crabs can shed a claw to escape (autotomy) and regrow it over several moults.

anatomy.text: If it loses a pincer, it somehow becomes incapable of walking sideways.

diet.text: If it can't find food, it absorbs nutrients by swallowing a mouthful of sand.
Its usual food isn't named. On beaches 'with little in the way of food' it squabbles over territory, so food on the beach is what it competes for.
A beach crab that eats sand when hungry is a scavenger and sifter of the shore's detritus and small animals, by inference.
diet.analogy: Sand-bubbler and fiddler crabs sift sand for the organic matter in it.

habitat.text: Sandy beaches near the sea, in burrows dug into the sand. The Gen 3 Pokédex habitat is waters-edge.

In HeartGold and SoulSilver it is fished at Cherrygrove, Union Cave, Route 34, Olivine, Sea Route 40, the Whirl Islands and Cianwood (where Rock Smash finds it too), walks and is smashed out of rocks on Route 47, and in Kanto is fished on Sea Route 19 and in the Seafoam Islands, at any time, in both versions.
Its Rock Smash encounters (Cianwood, Route 47, Sea Route 19) fit a crab that shelters under rocks as well as in sand.

behavior.text: It walks sideways.
Its activity pattern is not stated; the tables have it at any time.

social.text: On sandy shores with little food, Krabby can be seen squabbling with each other over territory.
Territorial fights where food is scarce suggest that where food is plentiful they tolerate each other more.

reproduction.text: Water 3 egg group, 20 egg cycles, an even sex ratio, medium growth. Nothing describes eggs or young.

defense.text: If it senses danger approaching, it cloaks itself with bubbles from its mouth so it will look bigger.
Losing a pincer costs it little: the pincer grows back.
Harden (Lv 11) and Protect (Lv 29), with Shell Armor (no critical hits), are a crab's shell in game form.

senses.text: It senses danger approaching; how is not described.

life_cycle.text: It becomes Kingler at level 28, from 0.4 m and 6.5 kg to 1.3 m and 60.0 kg, and one claw grows massively (99.2).

moves_in_the_wild.text: Mud Sport, Bubble, Vise Grip (Lv 5), Leer, Harden, Bubble Beam, Mud Shot, Metal Claw, Stomp, Protect, Guillotine (Lv 31), Slam, Brine, Crabhammer (Lv 41) and Flail: bubbles, mud and pincers.

ecology.text: A shore scavenger and sand-sifter, close to the bottom of the web, recycling what washes up.
Burrows dug in sand turn over and aerate the beach.
No entry names its predators; in Seafoam it shares the water with Seel, Dewgong and Slowbro.

humans.text: Nothing is said about Krabby and people.

homestead.text: A beach and shore animal: the homestead's lakes have no sand beach for it.
A cleaner of shore detritus, if a sandy margin is made for it.
homestead.note: Its diet is barely recorded.

homestead.text: Lost pincers grow back: a fight costs it little, so it will fight often.
Krabby bubbling up to look bigger every time the homestead's Seel swims past.

niche.foraging: forages on the shore; swallows sand for nutrients when food is short
niche.note: Its usual food is never named.

relationships.with: detritus washed up on the shore

relationships.note: When no other food is found.

ecotypes.name: Burrow digger
ecotypes.reading: A lineage of deep burrows: it digs and slams. The Krabby that holds the best holes on a crowded beach. Fits sandy beaches.
ecotypes.behavior: Wins territory squabbles by digging in.

ecotypes.name: Haze-bubbler
