habitat.text: Grassland by Gen 3 habitat. In HeartGold and SoulSilver it is in Ilex Forest's grass at night (60%), on Routes 5, 6, 24 and 25 at night, and in the Johto Safari Zone at night.
By day it stays quietly underground, in the cold ground, out of the sun.
Its microhabitat is the fertile soil of the forest floor and its clearings: soil it chooses by day, the grass above it at night.

behavior.text: Nocturnal: moonlight wakes it, and it roams actively at night; by day it keeps its face buried and stays quietly underground. HeartGold and SoulSilver meet it in grass only at night.
It roams far and wide at night.
It alternates between a rooted, plant-like day and a mobile night.

social.text: Nothing is said about other Oddish. Its evolved form Bellossom gathers in groups to dance (182.1), but that is the adult, and a different branch of the line.

reproduction.text: It sows seeds as it walks about at night.

In the games it breeds from eggs (Grass egg group, 20 egg cycles). How the seeds relate to the eggs isn't explained: whether a seed grows into an Oddish, an ordinary plant or something else is unknown.

defense.text: By day it buries itself with only its leaves showing, to avoid detection by its enemies, and it can be mistaken for a clump of weeds.
If anyone tries to pull it out of the ground, it shrieks horribly.
defense.analogy: A parallel in folklore rather than biology: the European legend of the mandrake (Mandragora), whose root was said to scream when pulled from the ground.

defense.text: Acid (9), Poison Powder (13), Stun Spore (15) and Sleep Powder (17): a small animal well armed with chemicals.

senses.text: It responds to moonlight: exposure to it starts it moving.
It seeks out fertile soil, so it can sense soil quality somehow; how is not described.

life_cycle.text: Oddish becomes Gloom at level 21; Gloom becomes Vileplume with a Leaf Stone or Bellossom with a Sun Stone.

The line turns carnivorous as it develops: Gloom's sweet, sticky nectar is used to attract prey, and Vileplume lures prey with its huge petals, doses them with toxic spores and eats them. Oddish itself is never described eating animals.
The Sun Stone branch reverses the night habit: Bellossom closes its petals and sleeps at night and dances in sunshine.

moves_in_the_wild.text: Sweet Scent (Lv 5) is a lure. In Gloom the lure is for prey (44.1); in Oddish it might draw animals that carry its seeds, but that is a reading.
Moonlight (Lv 33) heals by moonlight, matching the entries, but Oddish evolves at 21, so a wild Oddish almost never has it.
Its wild repertoire before evolving is drain (Absorb), acid (Acid) and powders (Poison Powder, Stun Spore, Sleep Powder).

ecology.text: A producer, or as near as any regular member of the community comes to one: it draws nutrients from soil and energy from moonlight, which puts it at trophic level 1.
It disperses its own seeds by walking, far and wide each night, spreading its kind across the forest floor.
Digging in by day may loosen and mix the soil, and it selects fertile patches, but nothing says whether it depletes or enriches them.
ecology.note: Untested.

ecology.text: It shares Ilex Forest's grass with the caterpillars in shifts: the larvae in the morning and by day, Oddish at night.

humans.text: People can take it for a clump of weeds and try to pull it up, which sets off its shriek.
FireRed gives it a scientific name, 'Oddium Wanderus', in the same entry as the hearsay about how far it walks (see Folklore).
The capability records list it under light from Gold's 'moon light'. That is a misreading: moonlight wakes it, it doesn't make light.

homestead.text: A night gardener of sorts: it seeks fertile soil, plants itself, and sows seeds wherever it walks. An Oddish loose in the Glasshouse at night would seed its own kind among the Berry rows.
homestead.note: What its seeds grow into is unknown.

homestead.text: A soil test on legs: its leaves grow glossier the more fertile the soil, so a planted Oddish would show where the ground is good.
homestead.note: One entry; untested.

homestead.text: It needs soft, fertile soil to bury itself in by day, darkness and moonlight at night, and cool ground out of the sun.
It chooses the cold underground (43.5), so Blackthorn's cool soils may suit it, though no record puts it in the highlands.
homestead.note: The capability records already file this under cold tolerance; that rests on one entry.

niche.foraging: plants itself in fertile soil by day and absorbs nutrients through its body; absorbs moonlight at night while walking and sowing seeds
niche.note: It takes up soil nutrients as a plant does; the guild names its energy source.

relationships.note: Noctowl catches prey in darkness, and Oddish is the night animal most often met in Ilex Forest's grass (0.5 m against Noctowl's 1.6 m). Against it: Oddish is poisonous and armed with powders, and the enemies it hides from (43.8) are daytime ones.
Hoothoot's grass records are at night, as Oddish's are. Its diet is not stated.
Both draw on what's below ground: Oddish takes soil nutrients, Paras sucks tree roots. Whether they compete for the same nutrients is untested.
Oddish, Zubat and Paras make up the whole of Ilex Forest's night grass table.
Same grass, opposite shifts (HeartGold; Weedle in SoulSilver).

ecotypes.name: Rooted settler
ecotypes.reading: A lineage that leans further into the plant side of its life: it roots in harder and longer (Ingrain) and draws energy from light (Synthesis) instead of wandering. Fits stable, fertile clearings where staying put pays better than seeding new ground.
ecotypes.behavior: Wanders less and stays planted for days, leaves held up to the light.

ecotypes.name: Blade-leaf
ecotypes.reading: A lineage that arms its leaves: sharp-edged leaves thrown or slashed at attackers. Fits grassland and forest edges with more grazers or predators, where the leaves a buried Oddish leaves showing (43.8) are what gets bitten.
ecotypes.behavior: Fights back with its leaves instead of shrieking and staying put.

ecotypes.name: Distraction dancer
ecotypes.reading: A lineage that defuses attackers with behaviour rather than chemistry: a confusing dance, a disarming display, tickling. Fits places with many casual predators, and it foreshadows the line's later dancing (Bellossom).
ecotypes.behavior: Dances and fusses when cornered.

open_questions: What do its seeds grow into, and how do seeds relate to eggs?
Does it photosynthesise with its exposed leaves by day, or only absorb moonlight?
Does it ever take energy from other organisms (Absorb, Mega Drain), or only from soil and light?
Who are the enemies it hides from by day (43.8)?
Does its planting enrich or deplete the soil?
When does the line start eating animals: at Gloom, or earlier?

contradictions.text: How much of it is above ground by day? Crystal says it stays in the cold underground to avoid the sun (43.5) and Red/Blue that it keeps its face buried (43.1); Emerald says it leaves its leaves exposed (43.8).
contradictions.note: Compatible if only the leaves show, but a plant with leaves in the open isn't fully avoiding the sun.

folklore.text: It is said to walk nearly 1,000 feet (about 300 m) a night on its two roots.
folklore.note: Hearsay in the entry itself ('it is said'). The same entry gives its scientific name, cited under People.

Onix.summary: A rock snake nearly nine metres long that bores through the ground at 50 mph, always eating as it burrows: it feeds on large boulders and absorbs the hard objects it digs through, which is what makes its body so solid. As it grows, the stone parts of its body harden like black diamond, and with age it becomes rounder and smoother. A magnet in its brain acts as a compass so it never loses direction underground. Its tunnelling roars and shakes the ground, and the tunnels it leaves become homes for Diglett. In HeartGold and SoulSilver it lives in Union Cave, on Route 47 and Mt. Silver in Johto, and in Rock Tunnel and Victory Road in Kanto.

anatomy.text: A long rock snake (Gen 4 shape squiggle), 8.8 m and 210.0 kg, typed Rock and Ground: the Rock Snake Pokémon.
A massive, rugged body; its stone parts harden as it grows, becoming like black diamond.
It has a magnet in its brain that acts as a compass, so it does not lose direction while tunnelling.
anatomy.analogy: Real birds, sea turtles and some mole rats sense the earth's magnetic field to find their way.

diet.text: It always eats while burrowing, searching for food as it bores through the ground, and feeds on large boulders.
As it digs, it absorbs many hard objects; this is what makes its body so solid.
Its evolved form's body is thought to have changed from iron accumulating inside it from swallowing soil (208.9): the line takes in soil as well as stone.

habitat.text: It usually lives underground; the Gen 3 Pokédex habitat is cave.

In HeartGold and SoulSilver it lives in Union Cave (10%), on Route 47 (10%) and Mt. Silver (30%, Lv 42-48) in Johto, and in Rock Tunnel (20%) and Victory Road (15%) in Kanto, at any time, in both versions; the Johto Safari Zone has it too.

behavior.text: It rapidly bores through the ground at 50 mph by squirming and twisting its massive body.
The thunderous roar of its tunnelling echoes a long way, and it causes rumbling and tremors when it travels underground.
Its activity pattern is not stated; the tables have it at any time.

social.text: Nothing is said about Onix living with other Onix.

reproduction.text: Mineral egg group, 25 egg cycles, an even sex ratio, medium growth. Nothing describes how it breeds.

defense.text: Its size and its solid, diamond-hard body.
Rock Head protects it from recoil and Sturdy from one-hit knockouts; Harden, Bind, Screech and Sandstorm (Lv 22) are in its list.

senses.text: A magnetic sense of direction, from the magnet in its brain.
Its evolved form's eyes can see in the darkness underground (208.8); Onix's own eyes are not described.

life_cycle.text: It becomes Steelix when traded holding a Metal Coat: from 8.8 m and 210.0 kg to 9.2 m and 400.0 kg.
As it grows older, its body becomes steadily rounder and smoother.
It is said that if an Onix lives for over 100 years, its composition changes to become diamond-like, as it evolves into Steelix (208.2, 208.10).

moves_in_the_wild.text: Mud Sport, Tackle, Harden, Bind, Screech, Rock Throw, Rage, Rock Tomb, Sandstorm, Slam, Rock Polish, Dragon Breath, Curse, Iron Tail, Sand Tomb, Double-Edge and Stone Edge.

ecology.text: A rock-eater: it feeds on boulders and absorbs hard objects.
An ecosystem engineer: the tunnels it leaves are used as homes by Diglett.
ecology.analogy: Real burrows dug by one animal, such as an aardvark's, become homes for many others.

ecology.text: In Rock Tunnel it shares the dark with Cubone, Marowak, Geodude and Machop; on Mt. Silver with Steelix, its own adult form.
Eating boulders and rock, it competes with the other rock-eaters it lives beside, Geodude among them.

humans.text: The thunderous roar of its tunnelling echoes a long way; its travel underground causes rumbling and tremors people would feel.

homestead.text: A tunneller at 50 mph that never loses its way: the homestead's road-builder through rock, if it can be steered.
It eats boulders: a way to clear stony fields.
Keep it from tunnelling under buildings: tremors.
The old Onix at the quarry, so smooth now with age that the children slide down its back.

niche.foraging: eats boulders and hard objects while it burrows

relationships.note: Its tunnels become Diglett homes.
Both eat rock where they meet.

ecotypes.name: Boulder-roller
ecotypes.reading: A lineage of the rounder, smoother old Onix (95.6): it curls, rolls and throws stone. Fits open mountain slopes.
ecotypes.behavior: Rolls downhill rather than tunnelling when it can.

ecotypes.name: Tunnel-sealer
ecotypes.reading: A lineage of cave systems: it blocks passages, brings the roof down and, at the last, blows the rock apart. Fits deep cave networks.
ecotypes.behavior: Lies across a tunnel and will not move.

open_questions: Does Onix eat only rock, or soil and anything in it?
How long does it take for an Onix to become 'rounder and smoother'?
Do Onix ever meet in their tunnels?
Does the magnet in its brain respond to Magnemite and Magneton?

folklore.text: It is said that if an Onix lives for over 100 years, its composition changes to become diamond-like.

Paras.summary: A small bug that carries its own parasite. Paras burrows to suck and gnaw tree roots and draws juice from trunks, and the mushrooms on its back, called tochukaso, grow by taking nutrients from it; one entry says they take most of its food, another that they order the bug to feed. The spores reach it at birth, the mushrooms grow as it grows, and in Parasect the mushroom has taken over. In HeartGold and SoulSilver it is met in Ilex Forest's grass at every hour, least often by day.

anatomy.text: A small bug (0.3 m, 5.4 kg) with mushrooms growing on its back.
The mushrooms are called tochukaso and are described as parasitic: they grow large by drawing nutrients from the bug host.
anatomy.analogy: Tochukaso is the Japanese reading of 冬虫夏草 ('winter worm, summer grass'), the name for Ophiocordyceps sinensis and related insect-parasitic fungi; O. sinensis infects ghost-moth caterpillars in the soil of the Tibetan Plateau and fruits from the dead larva.

anatomy.text: The mushrooms grow with the host, sprouting and enlarging as the bug's body grows.
Its two types read as its two partners: Bug for the host, Grass for the mushroom (the games have no fungus type).

diet.text: It burrows to suck tree roots, or burrows under the ground to gnaw on them.
diet.analogy: Cicada nymphs spend years underground feeding on the sap of tree roots.

diet.text: The mushroom orders it to extract juice from tree trunks.
The mushrooms absorb most of the nutrition: the bug does the feeding and the fungus takes most of the food.

habitat.text: Forest, and underground among tree roots.
Its evolved form stays in dark, damp places, a preference not of the bug but of the mushroom.

In HeartGold and SoulSilver it is in Ilex Forest's grass (a 5% slot at every hour, plus 10% more in the morning and at night), National Park's Bug-Catching Contest, Mt. Moon's caves and the Johto Safari Zone.
Its ability Dry Skin (it loses HP in heat; water restores it) fits a damp-loving animal.

behavior.text: It burrows.

It is present in Ilex Forest's grass in the morning, by day and at night, least often by day (5% against 15%). That rests on the time-of-day split in the tables and fits the line's liking for dark, damp places; a table rate isn't abundance.
The fungus directs at least some of what it does: it orders the bug to extract juice from tree trunks.
behavior.analogy: Fungal control of host behaviour is real: Ophiocordyceps unilateralis makes infected carpenter ants climb vegetation and clamp their jaws onto a leaf before the fungus fruits from the ant's body.

social.text: Nothing is said for Paras. As Parasect they infest large trees in numbers and move to another tree all at once, so the adults at least gather.

reproduction.text: It is doused with mushroom spores when it is born.
When nothing is left to extract from the bug, the mushrooms on Parasect's back leave spores on the bug's egg: the fungus passes from parent to offspring at the egg.
reproduction.analogy: Passing a symbiont or parasite from parent to offspring is vertical transmission; it is common in insects, as with the Buchnera bacteria that aphids pass to their young.

reproduction.text: Bug and Grass egg groups, 20 egg cycles, an even sex ratio.

defense.text: No Paras entry describes a defence; what follows comes from its ability and moves.
Effect Spore: contact with it may paralyse, poison or put an attacker to sleep. Read biologically, the mushroom's spores defend the pair.
Stun Spore and Poison Powder (Lv 6) and Spore (Lv 17) make spores its main weapons; Slash (22) and X-Scissor (43) are its claws.

senses.text: Nothing is said about its senses.

life_cycle.text: Paras becomes Parasect at level 24. In Parasect the mushroom has grown larger than the host's body and controls it.
In Parasect the bug host is drained of energy and the mushrooms appear to do all the thinking.

Read in order, the entries trace an infection: spores at birth (46.3), mushrooms growing with the young bug (46.9, 46.10) and taking most of its food (46.2), a mushroom in control of the adult (47.1, 47.9), and spores passed to the next egg once the bug is spent (47.5).
Parasitism or symbiosis? The entries call the mushroom parasitic (46.6 to 46.8) and the adult a host-parasite pair (47.1), and none describes any benefit to the bug. Recorded here as parasitism.
The spores may protect the bug, which would make the young relationship partly mutualistic: Effect Spore and the spore moves are its only described defences.
life_cycle.note: Rests on game mechanics only; no entry says the bug benefits.

moves_in_the_wild.text: Feeding: Scratch (Lv 1), Leech Life (11) and Giga Drain (33). Two draining moves suit a root- and sap-sucker.
Growth (27) and Aromatherapy (38) read as the mushroom's moves, growing and scent. Aromatherapy cures the whole party's status problems, an odd move for a parasite that drains its host.
moves_in_the_wild.note: Assigning moves to host or fungus is a reading, not something the games do.

ecology.text: A root and sap feeder (trophic level 2) carrying a fungus that feeds on it (the fungus is a parasite at level 3).
Hard on trees in numbers: as Parasect they infest large trees en masse, drain the lower trunk and roots, and when the tree dies move on to another all at once. Paras is the first stage of that.
By killing trees, the line would create deadwood and gaps in the canopy, but no member of the community is described eating deadwood.
ecology.note: A gap in the reconstructed web: no decomposer is described.

ecology.text: The tochukaso is the community's only described fungus, and it is a parasite of a living host, not a decomposer.

Spoink, which is in Ilex Forest only through the Hoenn Sound on the radio, loves eating mushrooms that grow underground, which makes it the community's one described fungus-eater. Whether it eats tochukaso is unknown.
ecology.note: No entry links the two.

humans.text: Tochukaso are highly valued as a medicine for extending life (see Folklore for the claim itself).
humans.analogy: Ophiocordyceps sinensis is among the most expensive traditional medicines in China and the Himalaya, sold as a tonic.

humans.text: Parasect's spores are used as herbal medicine in China.
If tochukaso are valued, people would collect Paras; no entry describes this.

homestead.text: A medicinal crop, if the medicine claims hold: tochukaso grow on Paras's back and are valued for long life. Harvesting would need to leave the host alive and the mushroom able to regrow; nobody has described whether it does.
homestead.note: Its medicinal value is claimed, not shown.

homestead.text: Keep it out of the orchard and the Glasshouse: it feeds on tree roots, and its evolved form kills trees in groups.
It needs dark, damp, cool places and water (Dry Skin), so a cellar or cave would suit it better than a sunny yard; it already lives in Mt. Moon's caves as well as forest.

niche.foraging: burrows to suck and gnaw tree roots and extracts juice from trunks; the fungus on its back takes most of the nutrition
niche.note: Activity is read from presence in all three time-of-day tables.

relationships.note: Parasitism: the mushroom draws nutrients from the bug, takes most of its food, and as Parasect controls it.
Described for Parasect, which drains trees until they die; Paras's root-feeding is the start of it.
Spoink loves mushrooms that grow underground; if it eats tochukaso, it eats part of the pair. Spoink is radio-only (Hoenn Sound).
Both draw on what's below ground: roots for Paras, soil nutrients for Oddish.
Ilex Forest's night grass and Mt. Moon's caves.

ecotypes.name: Lure-and-bite
ecotypes.reading: A lineage that adds animal food to root sap: a scent lure to bring small animals close, a bite, and a strike at whatever turns to flee. Fits poor soils where roots yield little.
ecotypes.behavior: Sits scented at a burrow mouth and snaps at visitors.

ecotypes.name: Stone-claw digger
ecotypes.reading: A lineage built for hard ground: hardened claws for burrowing through stony or root-bound soil, and Counter for whatever digs it up. Fits rocky ground and caves such as Mt. Moon, where Paras also lives.
ecotypes.behavior: Digs deeper and hits back when unearthed.

ecotypes.name: Bug-led
ecotypes.reading: A lineage in which the bug keeps the upper hand for longer: fast, with venomous claws, able to forage beyond the dark, damp places the mushroom prefers (47.3). Fits drier, more open woodland.
ecotypes.behavior: Moves about more by day and burrows less.

ecotypes.name: Mind-mushroom
ecotypes.reading: The tochukaso already gives the host orders (46.5) and seems to do the thinking in Parasect (47.2); a psychic attack in the lineage reads as that control turned outward, against attackers. Fits crowded infestations where many Paras share one tree.
ecotypes.behavior: Unsettles attackers instead of fleeing them.

open_questions: Does the bug get anything from the mushroom, such as protection by its spores, or is it pure parasitism?
Is every Paras infected at birth (46.3), or can an uninfected Paras exist?
Does the fungus eventually kill the host (47.5 'nothing's left to extract from the bug')?
Which trees does it feed on, and how much harm does a single Paras do?
Do the medicinal claims hold, and could tochukaso be harvested without harming the host?
Does Spoink eat tochukaso?

contradictions.text: Sucks or gnaws? Red/Blue says it burrows to suck tree roots (46.1); Yellow says it gnaws on them (46.2).
contradictions.note: It may do both; recorded because the feeding mode matters for whether it takes sap or tissue.

folklore.text: Tochukaso are 'highly valued as a medicine for extending life' and 'valued as a medicine for long life'.
folklore.note: A belief the entries record about the mushroom's value; they don't say the medicine works.

Parasect.summary: A bug that has been taken over by the mushroom on its back. In Parasect the mushroom has grown larger than the bug's body and controls it: it drains the bug's energy and appears to do all the thinking, and it is the mushroom, not the bug, that prefers dark, damp places. Parasect infest the roots and lower trunks of large trees in numbers and drain their nutrients, all moving to a new tree when one dies. When there is nothing left to take from the bug, the mushrooms leave spores on the bug's egg. Its spores are toxic, and used as herbal medicine. In HeartGold and SoulSilver it lives in Cerulean Cave, one encounter in four.

anatomy.text: A bug with a mushroom (Gen 4 shape armor), 1.0 m and 29.5 kg, typed Bug and Grass: the Mushroom Pokémon.
A mushroom grown larger than the host's body controls Parasect; it is a host-parasite pair in which the parasite mushroom has taken over the host bug.
anatomy.analogy: Ophiocordyceps fungi take over ants and change their behaviour before fruiting from them; the tochukaso of Paras's entries is the Japanese name for Cordyceps.

anatomy.text: The bug host is drained of energy by the mushrooms on its back; they appear to do all the thinking.

diet.text: Parasect infest large trees en masse and drain nutrients from the lower trunk and roots.
Its young burrow to suck tree roots and draw juice from trunks (46.1, 46.5): the adult keeps the line's diet, in numbers.
Leech Life (Lv 11) and Giga Drain (Lv 39) are draining moves; Growth (Lv 30) the mushroom's own growth.
In Cerulean Cave there are no trees, so there it must live on something else: the cave's moss, roots reaching down from above, or detritus. Nothing says which.
diet.note: The games put it only in a cave in HGSS.

habitat.text: It stays mostly in dark, damp places, the preference not of the bug but of the big mushroom on its back.
Large trees, which it infests, and the Gen 3 Pokédex habitat forest.
In HeartGold and SoulSilver it is wild only in Cerulean Cave (25%, Lv 38-47), at any time, in both versions; the Johto Safari Zone has it too.
Cerulean Cave, dark and full of water, is the darkest, dampest place in Kanto: the mushroom's preference, not a tree's.

behavior.text: When an infested tree dies, they move onto another tree all at once.
Its activity pattern is not stated; the cave tables have it at any time.

social.text: They infest trees en masse and move together, so Parasect live in groups on a shared host tree.

reproduction.text: When nothing's left to extract from the bug, the mushrooms on its back leave spores on the bug's egg.
So the mushroom passes from parent to young: Paras is doused with spores when it is born (46.3). The fungus has its own life cycle riding on the bug's.
Bug and Grass egg groups, 20 egg cycles, an even sex ratio, medium growth.

defense.text: It scatters toxic, poisonous spores from the mushroom cap; the larger the mushroom grows, the stronger the spores.
Effect Spore, its ability, can paralyse, poison or put to sleep anything that touches it; Spore (Lv 17), Stun Spore and Poison Powder are the spores in game form.
Dry Skin, its other ability, hurts it in heat and heals it in water: a damp-loving body in game terms.

senses.text: Nothing is said about its senses; the mushroom 'appears to do all the thinking'.

life_cycle.text: It evolves from Paras at level 24, from 0.3 m and 5.4 kg to 1.0 m and 29.5 kg.

Read as development, the line is the mushroom's growth: spores at the bug's birth, mushrooms sprouting as it grows (Paras), a mushroom larger than the bug that controls it (Parasect), and spores left on the bug's egg when the host is spent.

moves_in_the_wild.text: Cross Poison, Scratch, Stun Spore, Poison Powder, Leech Life, Spore, Slash, Growth, Giga Drain, Aromatherapy and X-Scissor: spores and drains.

ecology.text: A parasite of large trees that kills them, and moves on in a mass when they die: a cause of tree death, and of deadwood.
The mushroom is a parasite of the bug, the bug a parasite of the tree: a chain of parasites, unique in Johto and Kanto's webs.
In Cerulean Cave it shares the dark with Golbat, Kadabra, Machoke, Magneton, Ditto, Electrode and Wobbuffet.

humans.text: In China its spores are used as herbal medicine.

homestead.text: Keep it away from the orchard and any large tree you value: it infests and drains them until they die.
It wants dark, damp quarters: a cellar or a cave, not the sun.
Its spores are medicine but also toxic: handle with care, and never on a living host without a healer's say.
The homestead's one Parasect, kept in the root cellar, which seems to be thinking about something.

microhabitat: roots and lower trunks of large trees
niche.foraging: infests large trees en masse and drains nutrients from roots and trunk
niche.note: Filed with Paras as a sap feeder. Activity from the cave tables (any time).

relationships.with: roots and lower trunks of large trees (non-Pokémon)

relationships.note: It drains them until they die.

relationships.with: the parasitic mushroom on its back (non-Pokémon fungus)

ecotypes.name: Sweet-lure host
ecotypes.reading: A lineage whose mushroom draws others in: a luring scent and a dazzling beam. The mushroom spreading itself by bringing new hosts close. Fits dark forest floors with many bugs.
ecotypes.behavior: Sits still and smells sweet; things come to it.

ecotypes.name: Root-crawler
ecotypes.reading: A lineage in which the bug still matters: claws, speed and a chase. The Parasect that moves fastest from a dying tree to the next. Fits old forest where big trees die often.
ecotypes.behavior: First to leave a dead tree, first to the next.

open_questions: What does Parasect live on in Cerulean Cave, where there are no trees?
How much of the bug is left in a Parasect: does it feel, choose, remember?
Do the spores left on the bug's egg (47.5) always take, or can a Paras be born free of the mushroom?
Which medicine do its spores make, and at what cost to the animal?

folklore.text: It is said to prefer damp places.

Phanpy.summary: The young of Donphan: a small, very strong elephant with a long snout. For its nest Phanpy digs a vertical pit at a river's edge and marks the ground around it with its trunk to tell others the place is taken. In the quiet morning hours it comes ashore to shower with its trunk; when others gather they douse each other thoroughly, then dry off at the water's edge, and in the heat it fans itself with its big ears. It swings its snout around playfully and bumps with it to show affection, but it is so strong it can send you flying, and it can carry an adult on its back. In HeartGold it lives on Route 45 and Mt. Silver; in SoulSilver, Teddiursa has its place.

anatomy.text: A small four-legged animal (Gen 4 shape quadruped), 0.5 m but 33.5 kg, typed Ground: the Long Nose Pokémon.
A long snout, a trunk it uses deftly, and big ears that serve as broad fans.
Strong despite its compact size; even the young are very strong.

diet.text: No entry says what Phanpy eats.
Filed with Donphan as a plant-eater, from its body plan and its line; the machine reading's rock-eater comes from its Ground type alone.
diet.analogy: Real elephants are plant-eaters that use their trunks to gather food and water.
diet.note: No entry gives the line's diet.

habitat.text: River edges, where it digs its nest; it comes ashore, so it spends time in the water too. The Gen 3 Pokédex habitat is rough terrain.
In HeartGold it lives on Route 45 (10%, Lv 20) and Mt. Silver (10%, Lv 43-48), at any time; it is not wild in SoulSilver, where Teddiursa has the same places.

behavior.text: During the deserted morning hours it comes ashore and deftly uses its trunk to take a shower.
When it becomes hot, it flaps its ears busily to cool down.
behavior.analogy: Real African elephants cool their blood by flapping their large ears.

behavior.text: It swings its long snout around playfully, which, because it is so strong, can be dangerous.
Active by day, mornings at least, by 231.3; the tables have it at any time.

social.text: When others gather around, they thoroughly douse each other with water.
It marks the area around its nest with its trunk to let the others know the area has been claimed.
As a sign of affection, it bumps with its snout.
Social at the water and territorial at the nest: a group animal that keeps its own nest site.

reproduction.text: For its nest, it digs a vertical pit in the ground at the edge of a river.
Field egg group, 20 egg cycles, an even sex ratio, medium growth.

defense.text: Its strength: its snout can send you flying.
Defense Curl and Rollout (Lv 15), the curled roll its adult attacks with; Endure (Lv 28) and Take Down (Lv 10) too.

senses.text: Odor Sleuth, a scenting move, is in its list; the entries say nothing of its senses.

life_cycle.text: It becomes Donphan at level 25: from 0.5 m and 33.5 kg to 1.1 m and 120.0 kg.
A riverbank youngster that becomes a tusked herd animal of rough mountain country, as Donphan's dossier reads its adult entries.

moves_in_the_wild.text: Odor Sleuth, Tackle, Growl, Defense Curl, Flail, Take Down, Rollout, Natural Gift, Slam, Endure, Charm, Last Resort and Double-Edge.

ecology.text: A digger of nest pits at river edges: it shapes the banks it lives on.
On Route 45 it shares the slopes with Geodude, Graveler, Gligar, Spearow and the Aipom and Heracross of the trees; on Mt. Silver with Donphan, its adult.

humans.text: It can easily pick up and carry an adult human on its back.
Its affectionate bump may send you flying.

homestead.text: Carries an adult on its back: a pack animal and a ride for short distances.
Strong for its size: hauling.
Give it water to shower in, and stand clear of its playful snout.
Morning at the creek: two Phanpy soaking each other, and the washing on the line soaked too.

niche.foraging: not described
niche.note: Diet never stated; filed with Donphan as a herbivore. Diurnal from 231.3's morning showers.

relationships.note: Its nest pits.

ecotypes.name: Rockfall ram
ecotypes.reading: The young of Donphan's head-down lineage: a crushing head blow, a gathering of strength and a body slam. Fits rocky slopes.
ecotypes.behavior: Its playful snout-swinging turns into charges early.

ecotypes.name: Crevasse walker
ecotypes.reading: The young of Donphan's high-country lineage: ground-splitting, ice and old stone power. Fits cold, broken ground like Mt. Silver.
ecotypes.behavior: Digs its nest pits in hard, cold banks.

open_questions: What does Phanpy eat?
Where is the river on Route 45 or Mt. Silver that it nests by?
How many Phanpy gather to shower together?
Why is it in HeartGold's wild and not SoulSilver's?

Pichu.summary: The young of Pikachu, a tiny electric mouse (0.3 m, 2.0 kg) that hasn't yet learned to hold its charge. Its cheek pouches are small and can't store much, so any shock, fright or even amusement makes it discharge, and the jolt surprises Pichu as much as anyone; it gets better at holding power as it grows. Young Pichu play by touching tails and setting off sparks, a test of courage that can end in tears when the sparks flash. It charges more easily in thundery or very dry weather. In HeartGold and SoulSilver it is never wild; Crystal gives it as an egg, and only Sinnoh's Trophy Garden has it wild.

anatomy.text: A tiny four-legged animal (Gen 4 shape quadruped), 0.3 m and 2.0 kg, typed Electric.
The electric pouches or sacs in its cheeks are still small and can't store much electricity yet.
Static crackles off it: you can hear it.

diet.text: No entry says what Pichu eats.
The adult gathers Berries and softens hard ones with electricity (Pikachu's dossier), so the young most likely eats fruit too, but this is the adult's diet, not Pichu's.
It takes in electricity from the weather: it charges more easily on days with thunderclouds or when the air is very dry. That is a charge, not a food.

habitat.text: The Gen 3 Pokédex habitat is forest.
Wild only in Sinnoh's Trophy Garden (Diamond and Pearl 5%, more in the morning; Platinum 25%). Crystal gives one as an egg on Route 34. HeartGold and SoulSilver have no wild Pichu.
Its parents' range in Johto and Kanto is Viridian Forest and the forest edges (Pikachu), so a wild Pichu would be expected there; the games show none.

behavior.text: It may send out a jolt if amused or startled; any kind of shock makes it discharge spontaneously.
If even a little electricity leaks, it becomes shocked, and when it zaps someone it surprises itself.
It plays with others, touching tails and setting off sparks; this appears to be a test of courage.
Its activity pattern is not stated; Diamond and Pearl's Trophy Garden has it more often in the morning.

social.text: Young Pichu play together. When one shorts out its electricity with another, it makes a shower of sparks and the Pichu begins to cry, startled by the flash.
Tail-touching play that tests courage reads as practice: young learning to handle charge, and each other, before they can store it.
social.analogy: Play-fighting in young mammals rehearses adult skills in a safe setting.

social.text: Pikachu live in groups (its dossier), so playmates would be the group's young.

reproduction.text: A baby Pokémon: Undiscovered egg group, so it can't breed; it hatches from a Pikachu or Raichu egg. 10 egg cycles (short), an even sex ratio, medium growth.

defense.text: Its electricity is a defence it can't yet control: it zaps when startled, even adult humans, despite its size.
Static, its ability, can paralyse anything that touches it, and Thunder Wave (Lv 10) does it on purpose.
Its other early moves are disarming rather than fierce: Charm (Lv 1), Tail Whip (Lv 5), Sweet Kiss (Lv 13). A small animal that wins by being harmless and then nasty (Nasty Plot, Lv 18).

senses.text: Nothing is said about its senses. It is startled by flashes of its own sparks, so it sees them.

life_cycle.text: It evolves into Pikachu with high friendship, and Pikachu into Raichu with a Thunder Stone: 0.3 m and 2.0 kg, then 0.4 m and 6.0 kg, then 0.8 m and 30.0 kg.
It gets better at holding power as it grows older.
Read as development, the cheek pouches grow and the control comes with them: Pichu leaks, Pikachu stores and uses, and Raichu's long tail grounds it against its own high voltage (26.1).

moves_in_the_wild.text: Its level-up list is short: Thunder Shock, Charm, Tail Whip, Thunder Wave, Sweet Kiss and Nasty Plot. Everything else comes from its parents (egg moves), a tutor or a machine.

ecology.text: Its role is the adult's in miniature, a small forest fruit-eater, if it eats what Pikachu eats.
ecology.note: Pichu's diet is unrecorded.

ecology.text: A 2 kg animal that can't help discharging when startled is a poor target for a predator: whatever grabs it gets shocked.

humans.text: Despite its small size, it can zap even adult humans, and then it is surprised itself.
Crystal gives a Pichu egg to the player on Route 34, so people breed and pass them on.

homestead.text: Expect shocks: it discharges when startled or amused, so warn visitors and keep it away from wiring and stored seed.
Calm, steady handling will help it grow out of the leaks: its control improves as it ages, and friendship is what makes it a Pikachu.
Storms and very dry air charge it faster: on such days, give it space.
A pair of homestead Pichu daring each other to touch tails by the fence, and both bursting into tears at the spark.

niche.foraging: unrecorded; read from the adult, which gathers Berries
niche.note: Filed as a frugivore with Pikachu; Pichu's own entries never say what it eats.

ecotypes.name: Kin keeper
ecotypes.reading: Pikachu's group-keeping lineage, in the young: a healing move given to another, a gift, and a move that keeps a partner doing something. A Pichu that plays and shares rather than sparks. Fits forest edges where Pikachu groups live together.
ecotypes.behavior: Plays gently, shares food, rarely shocks a playmate.

ecotypes.name: Storm capacitor
ecotypes.reading: A lineage that stores more than most: Charge builds up power for the next blow. In a Pichu, the young that leak least and learn control first. Fits open, stormy ground where thunderclouds come often.
ecotypes.behavior: Quiet in a storm while the others crackle; the first of its litter to become a Pikachu.

open_questions: What does a Pichu eat? Its entries say nothing.
Where are Pichu born and raised in Johto and Kanto? The HGSS tables have none.
Does storm weather charge it as food, or only as charge?
Do adults teach control, or does it come with age alone (172.6)?

Pidgeotto.summary: A territorial raptor of forest and grass. Pidgeotto claims a large territory and patrols it, flying slow circles with a sharp lookout; its vision is so good that however high it flies it can see its prey move. It downs prey with well-developed claws and carries it more than 60 miles to its nest, an Exeggcute for example, and it shows no mercy to anything that violates its territory. It is the one named predator of Magikarp, which it catches mid-jump. In HeartGold and SoulSilver it hunts by day on Routes 37 and 43 in Johto and Routes 2, 8, 13, 14, 15 and 25 and Viridian Forest in Kanto.

anatomy.text: A bird (Gen 4 shape wings), 1.1 m and 30.0 kg, typed Normal and Flying.
The claws on its feet are well developed: it immobilises prey with them and carries it.

diet.text: It flies over its wide territory in search of prey and downs it with its highly developed claws.
It can carry prey such as an Exeggcute to its nest over 60 miles away.
Predators like Pidgeotto catch Magikarp mid-jump (Magikarp's own entry).
An Exeggcute (2.5 kg) carried 60 miles by a 30 kg bird is a plausible load; prey much heavier than that would be eaten where it falls.

habitat.text: Forest, and the open sky over its territory; the Gen 3 Pokédex habitat is forest.
In HeartGold and SoulSilver it lives on Routes 37 (day only, 5%) and 43 in Johto, and on Routes 2, 8 (65%), 13, 14, 15 and 25 and in Viridian Forest in Kanto, by day and morning, in both versions.
Its prey Exeggcute lives on Route 43 with it, and Magikarp is in the water of Route 25: the tables put it beside the prey its entries name.

behavior.text: It claims a large area as its own territory and flies around patrolling it.
It slowly flies in a circular pattern, keeping a sharp lookout for prey.
behavior.analogy: Buzzards and other soaring hawks circle on rising air while they scan the ground.

behavior.text: It is full of vitality and constantly flies around its large territory.
Diurnal: every HeartGold and SoulSilver table has it by day and morning only.

social.text: Territorial: very protective of its sprawling territory, it fiercely pecks at any intruder.
A territorial predator lives spaced out, one bird (or pair) per territory; nothing says whether it pairs.

reproduction.text: It has a nest it carries prey back to, more than 60 miles from where it hunts.
Flying egg group, 15 egg cycles, an even sex ratio, medium-slow growth.
Carrying prey to a nest is how many birds feed nestlings; the entries don't say the prey is for young.
reproduction.note: The nest is stated, the chicks are not.

defense.text: If its territory is violated it shows no mercy in thoroughly punishing the foe with its sharp claws.
Its moves keep Pidgey's sand and wind (Sand Attack, Gust, Whirlwind) and add speed (Agility, Lv 32) and a rest (Roost, Lv 42).

senses.text: It has outstanding vision: however high it flies, it can distinguish the movements of its prey.
Keen Eye keeps its accuracy from being lowered.

life_cycle.text: It evolves from Pidgey at level 18 and into Pidgeot at 36, from 1.1 m and 30.0 kg to 1.5 m and 39.5 kg.
It is where the line becomes a predator of vertebrates: Pidgey eats small bugs (16.8), Pidgeotto carries off an Exeggcute.

moves_in_the_wild.text: Gust, Quick Attack, Whirlwind, Twister, Feather Dance, Agility, Wing Attack, Roost, Tailwind, Mirror Move and Air Slash: speed and wind. No claw move is in its list; the claws are the entries'.

ecology.text: A top daytime aerial predator wherever it lives, with named prey: Exeggcute and Magikarp.
Carrying prey 60 miles moves nutrients from hunting grounds to nest sites far away.
In Viridian Forest it would take what it can carry from the bug community: Caterpie, Weedle, Metapod, Kakuna and the small birds; no entry says it eats bugs.
ecology.note: Size and co-occurrence only.

humans.text: Nothing is said about Pidgeotto and people. Trespassing in its territory invites its claws.

homestead.text: A sentinel over the fields: outstanding vision from great height, and a territory it patrols.
Pest control from the air, but it will also take small Pokémon: keep young stock covered.
It will defend its territory hard; one Pidgeotto per stretch of country, and give it a high perch.
The Pidgeotto that circles the lake below Blackthorn every morning and has never once let a Magikarp jump in peace.

microhabitat: open sky over forest and grassland
niche.foraging: circles high, spots prey by its movement, downs it with its claws and carries it to its nest

relationships.note: Viridian Forest by day; size and co-occurrence only.
Viridian Forest by day (SoulSilver); size and co-occurrence only.

ecotypes.name: Stoop hunter
ecotypes.reading: A lineage that kills on the dive: a full-body stoop, a chase and a hard wing strike. The Pidgeotto that drops from its circling height onto prey. Fits open grassland and lakes.
ecotypes.behavior: Circles high, stoops hard.

ecotypes.name: Wind-cutter
ecotypes.reading: A lineage that works the wind and its voice: cutting gusts and a loud call to drive intruders off its territory without a fight. Fits windy uplands.
ecotypes.behavior: Screams at trespassers before it strikes.

open_questions: What else does Pidgeotto hunt besides Exeggcute and Magikarp?
Why carry prey 60 miles to a nest? Is it feeding young?
How large is a territory, and does it hold it alone or as a pair?
Does it take the Bug Pokémon of Viridian Forest?

Pidgey.summary: The small, docile ground bird of every forest edge and grassy route. Pidgey hides in tall grass, forages for small bugs, and has a clever trick: it flaps its wings rapidly in the grass to raise a dust cloud that drives insect prey into the open. The same dust is its defence; it would rather kick up blinding sand than fight, though if disturbed it can strike back ferociously. It has an extremely sharp sense of direction and finds its way home to its nest from however far away. In HeartGold and SoulSilver it is one of the commonest daytime birds of Johto and Kanto, Viridian Forest among them.

anatomy.text: A tiny bird (Gen 4 shape wings), 0.3 m and 1.8 kg, typed Normal and Flying: the Tiny Bird Pokémon.
It flaps its wings at ground level to kick up blinding sand.

diet.text: It hides in tall grass and forages for food such as small bugs.
It rapidly flaps its wings in the grass, stirring up a dust cloud that drives insect prey out into the open.
diet.analogy: Cattle egrets and some other birds catch insects flushed from the grass, though by following grazers, not by fanning dust themselves.

diet.text: 'Food such as small bugs' leaves room for other food; seeds are likely for a ground bird but never stated.
diet.note: The wording is open-ended.

diet.text: Sand Attack (Lv 5) and Gust (Lv 9) are the dust-raising wingbeats in game form.

habitat.text: Forests, woods and grassy areas: a common sight in forests and woods, it usually hides in tall grass. The Gen 3 Pokédex habitat is forest.

In HeartGold and SoulSilver it lives on Routes 29, 30, 31, 35, 36 and 37 and in the National Park in Johto, and on Routes 1, 2, 5, 6 and 25 and in Viridian Forest in Kanto, always by day and morning only, in both versions.
In Viridian Forest it is 15% of daytime encounters, among Caterpie or Weedle, Metapod or Kakuna, and Pikachu; at night Hoothoot and Noctowl take its slots.

behavior.text: Very docile; it dislikes fighting and prefers to avoid conflict.
If disturbed, however, it can ferociously strike back.
Diurnal: every HeartGold and SoulSilver table has it by day and morning only, and the owls take its place at night.

social.text: Nothing is said about flocks or pairs.

reproduction.text: It has a nest it can unerringly return to, however far it is taken from home.
Flying egg group, 15 egg cycles (short), an even sex ratio, medium-slow growth.

defense.text: If attacked, it often kicks up sand to protect itself rather than fight back; it chases off enemies by flapping up sand.
One trick does two jobs: the dust that flushes insects is the dust that blinds attackers.
Its predators aren't named; Pidgeotto and the owls are larger birds in the same places.
defense.note: Co-occurrence and size only; Noctowl hunts at night when Pidgey isn't out.

senses.text: It has an extremely sharp sense of direction.
senses.analogy: Homing pigeons find their way back over hundreds of kilometres using the sun, the earth's magnetic field and smell.

senses.text: Keen Eye, one of its abilities, keeps its accuracy from being lowered: good eyes in game terms.

life_cycle.text: It becomes Pidgeotto at level 18 and Pidgeot at 36: 0.3 m and 1.8 kg, then 1.1 m and 30.0 kg, then 1.5 m and 39.5 kg.
Read as development, a docile insect-eater that hides in grass becomes a territorial raptor that carries prey to its nest (Pidgeotto, 17.4): the line climbs from trophic level 2-3 to the top.

moves_in_the_wild.text: Tackle, Sand Attack, Gust, Quick Attack (Lv 13), Whirlwind, Twister, Feather Dance, Agility, Wing Attack, Roost, Tailwind, Mirror Move and Air Slash: a bird that kicks up dust, outpaces and out-turns, and roosts to rest.

ecology.text: A small daytime insectivore of grass and forest edges, active when the owls are not: Pidgey by day and Hoothoot or Noctowl by night share the same slots in the tables.
By flushing insects into the open with its dust, it may make prey available to other insect-eaters nearby.
ecology.note: Untested.

humans.text: Its homing is the kind people have used birds for: it returns to its nest from any distance.
Docile and common on the routes out of every early town, it is the first wild bird most Trainers meet.

homestead.text: A messenger: a bird that finds its way home from anywhere could carry notes between the homestead and town.
homestead.note: Homing is stated; carrying messages is untested.

homestead.text: Insect control in the garden and fields: it flushes and eats small bugs.
Docile around people, but it can strike back if disturbed: don't corner it.
Pidgey kicking dust in the vegetable rows each morning, and the beetle population in steep decline.

niche.foraging: flushes insects from the grass with a dust cloud raised by its wings, then eats them

relationships.note: The same grass by day (Pidgey) and night (Hoothoot).

ecotypes.name: Dust-flusher
ecotypes.reading: A lineage that hunts harder than the docile entries suggest: a move to find what hides, a chase, and a cutting wind. The Pidgey that runs down what its dust drives out. Fits open grassland.
ecotypes.behavior: Follows the flushed insects instead of waiting for them.

ecotypes.name: Steel-wing defender
ecotypes.reading: The 'ferociously strike back' side of Pidgey as a lineage: a hard wing and a full-body dive. Nest-defenders. Fits crowded forest edges where nests are raided.
ecotypes.behavior: Docile until its nest is threatened, then fearless.

open_questions: Does Pidgey eat anything besides small bugs?
How does it find its way home: sun, magnetism, landmarks?
Where does it nest: on the ground in tall grass, or in trees?
Does it live in flocks?

Pikachu.summary: A small forest mouse that stores electricity in pouches on its cheeks and uses it for almost everything. It lives in groups, monitors its surroundings with its tail raised, and when several gather their combined charge can build into a lightning storm. The Gold and HeartGold Pokédex call it intelligent enough to roast hard Berries with electricity until they are tender, and Ruby notes the blackened Berries left when it overdoes it. One Platinum entry has it recharging a weakened companion with a shock, and the young, Pichu, play at touching tails to set off sparks.

anatomy.text: A small quadruped (0.4 m, 6.0 kg) with electricity-storing pouches or sacs on both cheeks.
The stored charge can be released in a single burst equal to a lightning bolt.
anatomy.analogy: The strongest real electric animal, the electric eel (Electrophorus), produces up to several hundred volts from stacks of modified muscle cells; a lightning bolt is many orders of magnitude beyond that.

anatomy.text: The tail is held up as a monitoring organ, and is sometimes struck by lightning in that pose.

diet.text: It eats Berries, and roasts hard ones with electricity to make them tender enough to eat.
diet.analogy: No wild animal cooks. The nearest real behaviour is food processing, such as bearded capuchins (Sapajus libidinosus) cracking hard nuts open with stone hammers.

diet.text: It sometimes misjudges: a blackened Berry is evidence of a Pikachu that overdid its charge.
Whether it also feeds on electricity, as Magnemite does, is not said; its charge is described as generated or gathered, not eaten.

habitat.text: A forest animal that lives with others of its kind; its Gen 3 Pokédex habitat is forest.
In HeartGold and SoulSilver its only wild home is Kanto's Viridian Forest, uncommon at any hour (5%) with an extra rare daytime slot (1%); Johto has none. Gold and Silver put it on Kanto's Route 2.
In Red, Blue, FireRed and LeafGreen it is common in Kanto's Power Plant (25%), alongside Magnemite, Magneton, Voltorb and Electabuzz: an electrical habitat as well as a forest one.
Pichu is found wild only in Sinnoh's Trophy Garden, where Diamond and Pearl add a morning slot; in Crystal it comes as an egg on Route 34.

behavior.text: Vigilant: it keeps its tail raised to check its surroundings.
It tests new things with electricity: whenever it comes across something new it blasts it with a jolt.
Its cheek pouches seem to charge at night while it sleeps, and it may discharge when drowsy after waking, so it sleeps at night.
Sleeping at night implies a day-active animal.
Intelligent, by the Gold and HeartGold entries.

social.text: It lives in groups in the forest, and several together can build up enough electricity to cause lightning storms.
It helps its own kind: it occasionally recharges a weakened fellow Pikachu with an electric shock.
Crackling from the cheek pouches signals wariness, a warning others can hear.
social.analogy: A warning display before attack, comparable in function to a rattlesnake's rattle.

social.text: Pichu play together by touching tails to set off sparks, which seems to be a test of courage; shorting out with another Pichu makes it cry.

reproduction.text: Field and Fairy egg groups, an even sex ratio, 10 egg cycles (short), medium growth. Pichu is a baby Pokémon in the Undiscovered group and can't breed.
Short incubation and a small, common animal suggest a fast-breeding species, but nothing in the Pokédex describes breeding.

defense.text: Electric defence: threatened, it looses charges from its cheek sacs; angered, it discharges its stored energy at once.
It bites if its tail is yanked.
Static, its ability, may paralyse anything that touches it.
Its own level-up list adds Double Team (Lv 18) and Agility (Lv 34), evasion and speed: a small animal that dodges first.

senses.text: The raised tail monitors its surroundings; what it detects is not said.
Raichu's ears stand straight up when its pouches are fully charged, so the line's ears respond to charge state.

life_cycle.text: Pichu (0.3 m, 2.0 kg) becomes Pikachu when it levels up with high friendship; Pikachu becomes Raichu (0.8 m, 30.0 kg, upright) on exposure to a Thunder Stone.
Storage is learned with age: Pichu's cheek pouches are small, it can't hold much electricity, discharges when startled or amused, and shocks itself; it gets better at holding power as it grows older.
Raichu manages a larger charge: it grows aggressive as charge builds and calms itself by discharging through its tail into the ground, leaving scorched patches near its nest.
Read as development, the line goes from leaking charge, to storing and using it deliberately, to having to vent it to stay calm.

moves_in_the_wild.text: Its level-up repertoire is electrical and evasive: Thunder Shock (Lv 1), Thunder Wave (Lv 10), Quick Attack, Double Team, Thunderbolt (Lv 26), Agility, Discharge (Lv 37), Light Screen and Thunder (Lv 45).
Discharge, which hits everything around it, is the closest move to the uncontrolled release of a startled or angry animal.
Tail Whip (Lv 5) and Slam (Lv 21) both use the tail it otherwise holds up as a monitor.

ecology.text: A forest frugivore (trophic level about 2), and possibly a minor disperser of Berry seeds, though roasting would probably kill them.
Groups can trigger lightning storms, and a raised tail draws lightning: a fire and disturbance risk to the forest it lives in.
Raichu leaves scorched patches near its nest, small disturbances in the ground cover.

humans.text: Pichu can zap even adult humans, and surprises itself when it does.
In HeartGold and SoulSilver a Pikachu is offered in trade in Saffron City; in Crystal a Pikachu is a Game Corner prize in Celadon City; in Yellow it is the starter.

homestead.text: Cooking help in the kitchen: it softens hard Berries with electricity. Expect some to come out blackened.
Small-scale electricity: it stores charge in its cheeks and can recharge another Pikachu; whether it can be persuaded to charge a battery is untested.
homestead.note: Recharging a companion is canon; charging equipment is the capability record's guess.

homestead.text: Lightning risk on the highland: a group can build a lightning storm, and a raised tail can be struck. Don't house many together near the Glasshouse or timber buildings.
Introduce new tools and equipment carefully: it jolts anything new it comes across.
Pichu in the nursery will shock carers, and itself, when startled; Blackthorn's dry winter air makes that worse, since Pichu charge more easily when the air is very dry.
A small, alert lookout: its raised tail monitors its surroundings and its crackling warns of trouble.
Needs: company of its own kind, Berries, and somewhere to sleep undisturbed at night while its pouches recharge.

niche.foraging: gathers Berries and softens hard ones with electricity before eating
niche.note: Activity is read from its sleeping at night (25.7); encounter tables give it at all hours.

relationships.note: Its tail is struck by lightning (25.4); Raichu gathers electricity from the air (26.5); Pichu charge more easily under thunderclouds (172.4).
Kanto Power Plant in Red, Blue, FireRed and LeafGreen; an electrical community.
By Thunder Stone, an object people supply.

ecotypes.name: Storm capacitor
ecotypes.reading: A store-and-release lineage: Charge builds up power for the next electric move, Bide absorbs punishment and returns it doubled, and Reversal hits hardest when it is nearly beaten. It is the cheek-pouch canon (pent-up energy released in one burst) made into a fighting style. Fits exposed ridges and hilltops with frequent thunderstorms, where charge comes easily.
ecotypes.behavior: Holds back, soaks up, then releases everything at once.

ecotypes.name: Kin keeper
ecotypes.reading: A caring lineage built on the Platinum canon of recharging a weakened companion: Wish heals whoever is in its place next turn, Present can heal or harm, and Encore holds an attacker to one move while others act. Fits dense forest groups where weak members are kept going rather than left.
ecotypes.behavior: Stays close to injured groupmates; tends rather than flees.

ecotypes.name: Spark-sparrer
ecotypes.reading: Play-fighting kept into adulthood: Fake Out startles, Double Slap is a contact contest of quick light blows, and Tickle weakens without injuring. Low-harm moves that settle disputes, like Pichu's tail-touching tests of courage. Fits large, crowded groups where real fights would be costly.
ecotypes.behavior: Settles rank with sparring rather than shocks.

open_questions: Where does its electricity come from? Generated in sleep (25.7), gathered from storms (172.4) or from the air (26.5), or all three?
Does it eat anything besides Berries?
How does recharging a weakened Pikachu (25.13) work, and is it common or rare?
What does the raised tail actually sense?
Is there a wild population anywhere in Johto? The HeartGold tables have none.
Is it ever killed by the lightning its tail attracts (25.4)?

contradictions.text: Group lightning storms: Red and Blue say several Pikachu together 'could' cause lightning storms; LeafGreen, with the same sentence, says they 'can'.
contradictions.note: Minor: possibility versus fact.

contradictions.text: What Raichu's grounded tail does: Ruby, Diamond and Platinum say it discharges excess electricity into the ground; Sapphire says Raichu plants its tail in the ground to search for electricity.
contradictions.note: Venting versus gathering through the same posture.

Piloswine.summary: The shaggy middle stage of the Swinub line: a short-legged, long-haired swine built for freezing cold, with rugged hooves that don't slip on ice and tusks it uses to dig up food buried under ice. Its coat covers its eyes, so it finds its way by a sensitive nose and very sensitive hearing, and when it charges it simply keeps charging, hair standing up on its back. Its tusks of ice thicken when it snows. In HeartGold and SoulSilver it is never wild: it comes only from raising a Swinub, which lives in the Ice Path.

anatomy.text: A four-legged animal (Gen 4 shape quadruped), 1.1 m and 55.8 kg, typed Ice and Ground.
It is covered by a thick coat of long hair that lets it endure freezing cold.
Its legs are short, but its rugged hooves keep it from slipping, even on icy ground.
It has tusks of ice, which thicken when it snows.
Tusks that grow with snowfall are built from the weather itself, a body part the environment adds to, which ties the animal's armament to cold places.

diet.text: It uses its tusks to dig up food that has been buried under ice.
What the buried food is isn't said. Swinub's favourite food is a mushroom that grows under dead grass, so the line most likely digs up fungi and plant matter buried by snow.
Odor Sleuth (Lv 1) and Mud-Slap, Mud Bomb and Earthquake are the nose and the digging in game form.

habitat.text: Cold places: its coat endures freezing cold, its hooves grip ice, and the Gen 3 Pokédex habitat is cave.
It is wild in only one Gen I-IV game: Platinum, on Route 217 with the Poké Radar. In HeartGold and SoulSilver it comes only from evolving a Swinub, whose home is the Ice Path.
A Piloswine of the highlands would be expected in and around the Ice Path, where its young live, but the games never place one there.
habitat.note: Range inferred from the young's range only.

behavior.text: Because the long hair all over its body obscures its sight, it just keeps charging repeatedly.
When it charges, the hairs on its back stand up straight.
Its activity pattern is not stated, and there are no HGSS tables to read it from.

social.text: Nothing is said about herds, pairs or how it treats its own kind.
Oblivious, one of its abilities, keeps it from becoming infatuated: in game terms it is hard to charm.

reproduction.text: Field egg group, 20 egg cycles, an even sex ratio, slow growth. Nothing in the Pokédex describes breeding or young.

defense.text: Its defence is the charge: it keeps charging, hair raised, at whatever threatens it.
Raised back hair during a charge makes it look bigger, a display as well as an attack.
defense.analogy: Many mammals raise their hackles (piloerection) when threatened, which makes them look larger.

defense.text: Snow Cloak raises its evasion in a hailstorm, Mist (Lv 48) shrouds it, and Endure (Lv 16) lets it survive a blow: a blizzard animal's defences.

senses.text: Its shaggy coat leaves it unable to see; it checks its surroundings with its sensitive nose instead.
It is very sensitive to sound.
A nose-and-ear animal, as its young are: Swinub finds food by smell too.

life_cycle.text: It evolves from Swinub at level 33, and into Mamoswine by levelling up while knowing Ancient Power, growing from 1.1 m and 55.8 kg to 2.5 m and 291.0 kg.
Ancient Power is in its own level-up list (Lv 1), so the move that unlocks the ice-age adult is one it already has.
Read as development, Piloswine is where the ice tusks appear: Swinub roots with its nose, Piloswine digs with tusks, Mamoswine's tusks are huge and made of ice.

moves_in_the_wild.text: Feeding and digging: Odor Sleuth, Mud Sport, Mud-Slap, Mud Bomb, Earthquake. Cold: Powder Snow, Icy Wind (Lv 25), Ice Fang (Lv 28), Mist, Blizzard (Lv 56). The charge: Take Down (Lv 32) and Fury Attack (Lv 33), a repeated jabbing that fits 'keeps charging repeatedly'.
Peck at level 1 is odd for a swine; it is the tusk jab, read generously.
moves_in_the_wild.note: A game convention, not a biological statement.

ecology.text: A digger of buried food: by breaking ice and frozen ground with its tusks it opens food for itself, and possibly for smaller animals that follow it.
ecology.analogy: Wild boar rooting turns over soil and leaf litter, and birds follow them for the exposed invertebrates.

ecology.text: Likely a primary consumer of fungi and plants under snow, as its young are.

humans.text: Nothing is said about Piloswine and people.

homestead.text: A winter worker for the highlands: endures freezing cold and walks on ice without slipping.
It could find and dig up food stores under snow, or clear iced-over ground, with its tusks and nose.
homestead.note: Untested whether it will dig where asked.

homestead.text: It can't see through its coat: approach it from where it can hear or smell you, never silently, or it may charge.
A Piloswine that clears the Ice Path entrance after each snowfall, tusks a little thicker every time.

microhabitat: ice caves and frozen ground (from the line's range)
niche.foraging: digs up food buried under ice with its tusks, finding it by smell
niche.note: Its own entries never name the food; filed as a fungivore with Swinub and Mamoswine, whose food is a mushroom under dead grass.

relationships.with: food buried under ice (fungi and plant matter)
relationships.note: Swinub's mushroom, read into the buried food.

ecotypes.name: Charging herd
ecotypes.reading: The line's charging lineage at the stage the charge belongs to: Piloswine is the one whose entries say it keeps charging, hackles up. Three full-body charges carried as egg moves. Fits open snowfields where a half-blind animal meets threats head-on.
ecotypes.behavior: Charges at any sound it doesn't like, again and again.

ecotypes.name: Ice-tusk line
ecotypes.reading: Swinub's ice-tusk lineage, in the stage that grows the tusks: Ancient Power is what turns a Piloswine into Mamoswine, and Icicle Spear matches tusks of ice that thicken in snow. Fits the coldest, snowiest ground.
ecotypes.behavior: Tusks that grow fast in snow; the Piloswine most likely to become Mamoswine.

open_questions: What is the food it digs from under the ice?
Where do wild Piloswine live in Johto? HeartGold and SoulSilver never show one.
Does it live in herds, as its charging habit and mammoth-like adult might suggest?
Do its tusks thin again when the snow stops (221.7)?

Pineco.summary: A sit-and-wait predator of the forest canopy that builds its own armour. Pineco hangs from a branch inside a case of tree bark it glues on with a fluid that sets in air, waits for flying insects to come close, and barely moves otherwise. It passes for a pinecone, which keeps birds from treating it as food; if its tree is shaken while it feeds it drops and explodes. In Johto it lives in the trees themselves: every wild Pineco in the Johto games is found by shaking a tree.

anatomy.text: A small, rounded body (0.6 m, 7.2 kg) wrapped in a case it builds and thickens itself from layers of tree bark.
It secretes a fluid that it spits out to glue bark to its body; the fluid hardens on contact with air.
anatomy.analogy: Bagworm moth caterpillars (Psychidae), whose name this Pokémon's category borrows, bind plant fragments into a portable case with silk that likewise sets once it is spun.

anatomy.text: The case is heavy relative to the animal, and the weight doesn't hinder it; the armour costs it mobility rather than effort, which fits an animal that hardly moves.

diet.text: It eats flying insects, which it waits for rather than chases.
It feeds from a hanging position on a branch and is exposed to disturbance while eating.
Its prey are most likely small, non-Pokémon insects: the flying Bug Pokémon it shares trees with in Ilex Forest (Butterfree 1.1 m, Beedrill 1.0 m) are larger than Pineco itself.
Bug Bite, which it learns early (Lv 9), is a biting attack and the most plausible reading of how it takes prey.

habitat.text: A forest animal that lives in trees, hanging from branches.

In HeartGold and SoulSilver it is found only by Headbutting trees, and the tree tables put it almost everywhere in Johto with trees, from New Bark Town to Ecruteak City; in Ilex Forest it is on the rarer tree table.

In Sinnoh (Diamond, Pearl, Platinum) it appears in Eterna Forest and on Routes 203, 204, 210 and 229 only when Pokémon Emerald is in the second slot, so it is not a native Sinnoh animal in the games' own terms.
Its microhabitat is the canopy and branches rather than the trunk or ground; it reaches the ground only when it falls.

behavior.text: Sedentary: it doesn't move about much on its own.
An ambush (sit-and-wait) forager: it hangs patiently and lets prey come to it.
behavior.analogy: The same strategy as orb-weavers and ambush bugs: low energy spent, low encounter rate, long waits.

behavior.text: Activity pattern isn't stated anywhere; HeartGold's tree tables don't split it by time of day.

social.text: No entry describes groups, pairs or interaction with its own kind; the sedentary ambush life suggests it lives alone on its branch.

reproduction.text: Bug egg group, 20 egg cycles, an even sex ratio; nothing in the Pokédex describes how it breeds or where it lays.

defense.text: Masquerade: it looks just like a pinecone, and its shell protects it from bird Pokémon that peck it by mistake.
defense.analogy: Masquerade (resembling an inedible object) rather than camouflage (blending into the background), as in caterpillars that pass for twigs or bird droppings.

defense.text: Last-resort defence: if its tree is shaken while it eats, it drops to the ground and explodes without warning.
defense.analogy: Comparable to autothysis in exploding ants (Colobopsis), where a worker ruptures its own body to defend the colony; Pineco's explosion is not described as fatal to it.

defense.text: Its moves line up with the canon: Protect at Lv 1 and Iron Defense later (withdrawing into armour), Self-Destruct from Lv 6 and Explosion at Lv 34 (the drop-and-explode defence), and Sturdy (it can't be knocked out in one blow).

senses.text: Nothing is said about its senses. An ambush predator of flying insects must detect prey approaching through the air, so vision or vibration sense is implied but not described; as Forretress its eyes are the only part visible through the shell.

life_cycle.text: It becomes Forretress at level 31, and the bark case becomes a steel-hard shell: the type changes from Bug to Bug/Steel.
The adult is even more sedentary, immovably rooted to its tree, usually on a fat trunk; it opens the shell only to catch prey, too fast for the inside to be seen.

Read as development, the move from layered bark to a steel shell suggests the case is mineralised or replaced as the animal matures, and the adult trades the juvenile's branch-hanging life for trunk-clinging.
life_cycle.note: No entry describes the change itself.

moves_in_the_wild.text: Feeding: Bug Bite. Defence: Protect, Iron Defense, Self-Destruct, Explosion. Rapid Spin (Lv 17) and Gyro Ball (Lv 42) fit a round body that falls and rolls; Spikes (Lv 28) matches the adult scattering pieces of its shell to drive enemies away.
Natural Gift (Lv 23) needs a held Berry, which hints that it handles fruit, but nothing in the Pokédex says it eats or stores Berries.
moves_in_the_wild.note: A level-up move, so it's the wild form's own repertoire; treat as a lead, not a diet item.

ecology.text: A canopy insectivore (trophic level about 3: it eats insects, which mostly eat plants), probably a minor control on flying insects in the trees it occupies.
It strips or collects tree bark for its case, so it uses the trees as a building material as well as a perch; whether it takes living bark (harming the tree) or shed bark is unknown.
Its explosion when a tree is shaken makes it a hazard to anything that shakes trees for food, such as foragers using Headbutt.

humans.text: People meet it by shaking trees, which is exactly the disturbance that the Ruby, Sapphire and Emerald entries say makes it explode. The Johto games' only way of finding it is the way most likely to set it off.

homestead.text: A natural perimeter deterrent: as Forretress it scatters shell fragments to drive enemies away, and Spikes is the game form of that.
Free insect control in an orchard or around the Glasshouse, if it will settle in the trees there; it needs trees to hang from and flying insects to eat.
homestead.note: Untested: whether it targets pest insects or just whatever flies past.

homestead.text: Don't put it in trees people shake for fruit or Apricorns, and keep it away from Headbutt foraging: a shaken tree is the trigger for its explosion.
Its bark-glue fluid, which sets in air, is an interesting material for repairs if it can be collected without stressing the animal.

niche.foraging: sit-and-wait ambush of flying insects from a hanging position

relationships.note: Birds peck it by mistake, taking it for food or for a cone; the shell protects it. Attempted predation, not a successful one.
Same Ilex Forest headbutt trees in HeartGold and SoulSilver; Hoothoot and Noctowl are the forest's bird Pokémon and the likely mistaken peckers.

ecotypes.name: Barbed bark
ecotypes.reading: A lineage whose defence is chemical and projectile rather than explosive: barbs in the bark case and a toxic litter of shed fragments beneath its tree. Fits dense woods where predators approach from below.
ecotypes.behavior: Explodes less, sheds more; leaves a poisoned ring of debris under its roost.

ecotypes.name: Ground-fall brawler
ecotypes.reading: A lineage that turns the drop from the branch into a fight: retaliation moves (Counter, Revenge) for the animal that shook its tree, and Sand Tomb for burying in sand or leaf litter once down. Fits dry, sandy woodland edges where falling is common and climbing back is slow.
ecotypes.behavior: Falls, digs in and hits back rather than exploding.

ecotypes.name: Mirror shell
ecotypes.reading: A lineage that leans into the armour: a defensive screen, and Power Trick, which swaps attack and defence, as the habit of turning that heavy case into the weapon (rolling and ramming).
ecotypes.behavior: Rolls into attackers with its case; the most Forretress-like juvenile.

open_questions: What is inside the shell? The Forretress entries call it a total mystery (205.1, 205.7).
Does it take bark from living trees, harming them, or gather shed bark?
What, if anything, does it eat besides flying insects? Natural Gift hints at Berries.
Does it survive its own explosion, and how often can it do it?
How does it breed, and where are eggs laid: in the canopy, in the case?
Is it diurnal or nocturnal? Ilex Forest's tree tables don't say.

Piplup.summary: A small, proud penguin of northern shores. Piplup is a skilled swimmer that dives for over ten minutes to hunt, wears thick down against the cold, and walks so badly it often falls over, then puffs up its chest as if nothing happened. Its pride runs through every entry: it hates accepting food from people, doesn't like being looked after, and won't listen to its Trainer. It is the first stage of SoulSilver's Empoleon. In the Gen I-IV games it is only ever a Sinnoh starter; no Johto game has one.

anatomy.text: A small two-legged bird (Gen 4 shape humanoid), 0.4 m and 5.2 kg, typed Water: the Penguin Pokémon.
Its thick down guards it from cold.
It is a poor walker and often falls down: a body built for water, not land.
anatomy.analogy: Real penguins walk awkwardly too, because their legs are set far back for steering in water.

diet.text: It dives for over 10 minutes to hunt.
Its prey isn't named. Prinplup searches for prey in icy seas (394.2), so the line hunts marine animals; fish are likely but never stated.
Because it is very proud, it hates accepting food from people.
Peck (Lv 15), Fury Attack (Lv 25) and Drill Peck (Lv 39) are a bill used for striking, the beak a diving hunter catches prey with.

habitat.text: It lives along shores in northern countries.
It is never wild in any Gen I-IV game: a starter gift at Lake Verity (Diamond, Pearl) or on Route 201 (Platinum). HeartGold and SoulSilver have it only by trade.
No Gen 3 habitat is given (the line is from Generation 4).

Cold northern shores in the Blackthorn world would be the coasts of Seafoam and the Whirl Islands, where the sea is coldest by the games' encounters (Seel, Dewgong, Jynx); the games put no Piplup there.
habitat.note: A habitat match only, from other species' presence.

behavior.text: A poor walker that often falls down, yet its strong pride makes it puff up its chest without a care.
A skilled swimmer that stays under for more than ten minutes at a time.
Its activity pattern isn't stated.

social.text: Its pride is the social trait the entries return to: it doesn't like to be taken care of, and it won't listen to its Trainer.

The line becomes solitary as Prinplup, which can never form groups because each one thinks it is the most important (394.3); Empoleon groups have a leader with the biggest horns (395.1). So the line goes from independent young, to loners, to led groups.

reproduction.text: Water 1 and Field egg groups, 20 egg cycles, 87.5% male (the starter ratio), medium-slow growth. Nothing describes nesting or care of chicks.
A chick that refuses care and food from others is odd for a bird; whether its parents feed it is unknown.

defense.text: Nothing describes how it defends itself. Bide (Lv 22), which stores up damage and returns it, and Mist (Lv 36) are its defensive moves.
Puffing up its chest after a fall is a display: it doesn't show weakness.

senses.text: Nothing is said about its senses. Hunting on dives of ten minutes means it finds prey underwater, but how is not described.

life_cycle.text: It becomes Prinplup at level 16 and Empoleon at 36: 0.4 m and 5.2 kg, then 0.8 m and 23.0 kg, then 1.7 m and 84.5 kg. Empoleon adds the Steel type.
Pride is the constant: Piplup won't take care, Prinplup won't group, Empoleon will destroy anything that threatens its pride (395.4).

moves_in_the_wild.text: Water and bill: Bubble, Water Sport, Bubble Beam, Brine (Lv 29), Whirlpool (Lv 32) and Hydro Pump (Lv 43); Peck, Fury Attack and Drill Peck. A diving hunter's set, with Growl (Lv 4) as its one display.

ecology.text: A small diving predator of cold coastal seas, eating marine animals it catches underwater; its exact prey and trophic level are unrecorded.
Nothing names its predators. A 5 kg chick that falls over on land would be easy prey on the shore.
ecology.note: From its clumsiness only.

humans.text: It hates accepting food from people and is hard to bond with because it won't listen to its Trainer.
It reaches people as a Sinnoh starter.

homestead.text: It won't take food from people: give it water to hunt in rather than a bowl.
Thick down for the cold, so it would be at home in the highland winter and in the cold lakes.
A long-diving swimmer: it could search the bottom of the Dragon's Den pool or the lake below Blackthorn, if it can be persuaded to.
homestead.note: It won't listen to its Trainer (393.4); persuasion is the hard part.

homestead.text: Expect a bond to take time and patience; the entries say outright that it is difficult.
The Piplup that falls flat on the ice outside the kitchen every morning and struts off as if it meant to.

niche.foraging: pursuit-diving: dives for over ten minutes to hunt
niche.note: Predator, as for Empoleon; prey never named, so trophic level assumes small marine animals.

relationships.note: Hunts on long dives; fish are likely but never named.

ecotypes.name: Long-dive hunter
ecotypes.reading: Empoleon's diving lineage in the chick: endurance in water, speed and force. The Piplup that stays under longest. Fits deep, cold coastal water.
ecotypes.behavior: Spends more time under the water than on the shore.

ecotypes.name: Tideflat prober
ecotypes.reading: A shore-foraging lineage: mud moves and a quick double jab, a chick that probes mud and shallows instead of diving deep. Fits flat, muddy shores and estuaries.
ecotypes.behavior: Pecks along the tideline; dives only when it must.

open_questions: What does it hunt on its dives?
Do its parents feed it, given that it refuses food from people?
Where would it live in Johto or Kanto, if anywhere? The games give only Sinnoh's shores.
Does it live in groups before the solitary Prinplup stage?

Poliwag.summary: A tadpole that has just grown legs and can't use them yet.
