Poliwag's skin is thin, damp and so transparent that its coiled insides show through as the swirl on its belly, clearer after it has eaten; yet the skin is so flexible that sharp fangs bounce off it. It lives in water and swims rather than walks. In Ilex Forest it is caught only by fishing, and it lives in Blackthorn City's water too. The direction of the belly spiral is said to differ from region to region.

anatomy.text: A tadpole (0.6 m, 12.4 kg) with newly grown legs.
anatomy.analogy: Real tadpoles grow their hind legs first and their forelegs later, then absorb the tail at metamorphosis; a two-legged tadpole like Poliwag is at the hind-leg stage.

anatomy.text: Very thin, slick, damp black skin through which its internal organs can be seen.
The swirl on its belly is its insides showing through the skin: part of its internal organs, seen as a spiral.
anatomy.analogy: Many real tadpoles have a long, coiled gut that shows through the belly skin; it is long because they digest plant food.

diet.text: It eats, and its belly swirl looks clearer afterwards.
What it eats isn't stated. A long, coiled gut points to plant food or detritus rather than prey.
diet.note: An inference from gut shape that leans on real tadpoles; the entries don't say the spiral is the gut, only 'insides' and 'internal organs'.
diet.analogy: Most real tadpoles graze algae and detritus, and carnivorous tadpoles, such as the meat-eating form of spadefoot toad tadpoles, have shorter guts.

habitat.text: Water: because it is inept at walking on its new legs, it always swims around in water.

In HeartGold and SoulSilver it is fished from Ilex Forest's pond (15% on the Old Rod, 60% Good Rod, 80% Super Rod) and never surfed there; it is fished from ponds and rivers across Johto, including Blackthorn City and Routes 43 to 45, and surfed on Routes 30, 31 and 44 and in Violet and Ecruteak Cities.
Being caught by rod rather than met surfing in Ilex Forest suggests it stays below the surface.

behavior.text: It prefers swimming to standing or walking, and is more adept at it.
Its activity pattern is unknown: Ilex Forest's fishing tables have no time of day.

social.text: Poliwag gather from far and wide when they hear Politoed's echoing cry, and Politoed's cries make them obey: the line's adult leads groups of young.
So Poliwag live within earshot of, and respond to, adults of their own line; whether they form groups without one isn't stated.

reproduction.text: Water 1 egg group, 20 egg cycles, an even sex ratio, medium-slow growth. As a tadpole it is the line's juvenile; nothing says where eggs are laid.

defense.text: Its skin, though thin, is so flexible that even sharp fangs bounce off it.
Hypnosis (Lv 8) is the belly spiral in game form: in its evolved form the spiral puts a foe to sleep so it can escape, and staring at it causes drowsiness.
Its abilities are Water Absorb (water attacks heal it) and Damp.

senses.text: Nothing is said about its senses.

life_cycle.text: Poliwag becomes Poliwhirl at level 25; Poliwhirl becomes Poliwrath with a Water Stone, or Politoed if traded holding a King's Rock.
Read as tadpole to frog: the new legs become Poliwhirl's well-developed legs, and Poliwhirl can live in or out of water, though it prefers water.
life_cycle.analogy: Amphibian metamorphosis: an aquatic, tailed larva becomes a semi-aquatic or land-living adult.

life_cycle.text: The two adult forms divide: Poliwrath is a powerful swimmer that nonetheless lives on dry land, and Politoed is a leader whose cry gathers Poliwag.

moves_in_the_wild.text: Water Sport (Lv 1), Bubble (5), Water Gun (11), Bubble Beam (25), Hydro Pump (38): water. Mud Shot (28) and Mud Bomb (41): mud.
Hypnosis (8) is the spiral; Rain Dance (18) calls rain. A wild Poliwag evolves at 25, so its working repertoire stops at Body Slam (21).

ecology.text: If it grazes, it is a primary consumer of the pond (trophic level 2), and food for larger pond animals.
ecology.note: Its diet is undescribed.

ecology.text: Its fang-proof skin is a defence against biting predators, which implies they exist.
In Ilex Forest it shares the fishing tables with Magikarp, and the share shifts by rod: mostly Magikarp on the Old Rod, mostly Poliwag on the Super Rod.

humans.text: Easy to catch (catch rate 255) and fished all over Johto.
People have noticed that the spiral's direction varies by area and have a theory about why (see Folklore).

homestead.text: Local: it lives in Blackthorn City's water and on Routes 43 to 45, so it is at home in the highland ponds.
If it grazes algae, a Poliwag in a cistern or garden pond might help keep the water clear.
homestead.note: Untested; rests on the grazing hypothesis.

homestead.text: Water Gun (Lv 11) is in its wild repertoire, so it can spray water on plants.
homestead.note: A move, read as a practical ability.

homestead.text: It needs clean water to live in: its thin, damp skin means it can't stay out of water for long.

microhabitat: pond and slow water, below the surface
niche.foraging: unknown; probably grazing, judging by its coiled gut
niche.note: No entry gives its diet.

relationships.note: From gut shape; no entry gives its diet.
Same water; Golduck is the pond's fastest and largest animal. Poliwag's fang-proof skin argues against.

ecotypes.name: Cold-water
ecotypes.reading: Three Ice-type egg moves: a lineage at home in cold, high water. Fits highland ponds and streams like Blackthorn City's and Route 44's, where Poliwag is in fact found.
ecotypes.behavior: Stays active in cold water and under thin ice.

ecotypes.name: Mud-bottom
ecotypes.reading: A lineage of silty, shallow ponds: mud as weapon and cover, and resistance to the infections and fouling of stagnant water (Refresh cures status problems).
ecotypes.behavior: Lives on and in the muddy bottom.

ecotypes.name: Splash-escape
ecotypes.reading: A lineage that leaps clear of the water to escape, and fights hardest when badly hurt. Fits ponds with many fast predators, where a last-ditch escape matters.
ecotypes.behavior: Jumps when chased; turns on an attacker when cornered.

open_questions: What does it eat?
Does the belly spiral really differ by area, and if it does, why?
Where are its eggs laid, and how long is the tadpole stage?
Does it hatch with legs, or grow them later?
Does it ever come onto land?

folklore.text: The direction of its belly spiral differs by area, and the equator is thought to have an effect on this.
folklore.note: The regional difference is stated as fact; the equator explanation is given as a belief ('is thought to').
folklore.analogy: The popular idea that water drains swirl opposite ways in the two hemispheres is a myth at the scale of a basin. And in real tadpoles the gut coils the same way in nearly every individual, as part of the body's fixed left-right asymmetry.

Prinplup.summary: The solitary middle stage of the Empoleon line. Every Prinplup believes it is the most important, so they can never form a group and each lives alone, away from the others. It searches for prey in icy seas, and its wings deliver blows that snap even the thickest trees. Between the proud, care-refusing chick and the adults that follow a leader, Prinplup is the loner stage. It is never wild in any Gen I-IV game.

anatomy.text: An upright bird (Gen 4 shape upright), 0.8 m and 23.0 kg, typed Water.
Its wings deliver wicked blows that snap even the thickest of trees.
Flippers strong enough to snap trees are flippers built for power in water; the strength is a swimmer's.

diet.text: It searches for prey in icy seas.
The prey is never named; Piplup dives for over ten minutes to hunt (393.2). Fish are likely but unrecorded.
Metal Claw (Lv 16, learned on evolving) and Drill Peck (Lv 46) are its striking moves.

habitat.text: Icy seas, where it hunts; its young live along shores in northern countries (393.2).
It is never wild in any Gen I-IV game.
It lives alone, away from others: each animal needs its own stretch of coast.

behavior.text: It lives a solitary life.
Its activity pattern isn't stated.

social.text: It lives alone, away from others; apparently every one of them believes it is the most important.
Because every Prinplup considers itself the most important, they can never form a group.
The adults have a leader with the biggest horns (395.1), so the line regroups at the last stage: the loner phase sits between a care-refusing chick and a led adult society.
social.analogy: Young males of many social mammals spend a solitary or bachelor phase between leaving their birth group and joining or leading a new one.

reproduction.text: Water 1 and Field egg groups, 20 egg cycles, 87.5% male, medium-slow growth. A stage that can never form a group is probably not the breeding stage; that is unknown.

defense.text: Its wing blows, strong enough to snap the thickest trees, are its defence as well as its weapon.
Bide and Mist carry over from Piplup as its defensive moves.

senses.text: Nothing is said about its senses.

life_cycle.text: It evolves from Piplup at level 16 and into Empoleon at 36, from 0.8 m and 23.0 kg to 1.7 m and 84.5 kg, gaining the Steel type.
Metal Claw is learned on evolving into Prinplup, the first hint of the Steel the adult will have.

moves_in_the_wild.text: Its list is Piplup's with Metal Claw added and later levels: Bubble Beam, Bide, Fury Attack, Brine, Whirlpool, Mist, Drill Peck and Hydro Pump (Lv 51).

ecology.text: A solitary diving predator of icy seas; spacing out on its own suggests each one claims its own hunting water.
Its prey and predators are unrecorded.

humans.text: Nothing is said about Prinplup and people; its chick won't listen to its Trainer (393.4), and a loner that thinks itself most important is unlikely to be easier.

homestead.text: Keep one at a time: two Prinplup can't share, by their own entries.
Its wing strikes could split firewood or clear fallen trunks, if it will work.
homestead.note: Whether a proud loner will do work is the open question.

homestead.text: Give it its own stretch of cold water to hunt in.
The Prinplup on the far rock of the lake, who has decided the lake is his.

microhabitat: a solitary stretch of cold coast
niche.foraging: hunts prey in icy seas, alone
niche.note: Predator, as for Piplup and Empoleon; prey unnamed.

ecotypes.name: Shore peacemaker
ecotypes.reading: Empoleon's calming lineage, in the stage that most needs it: moves that soften or confuse a rival without a fight. A Prinplup that can share a shore after all. Fits crowded coasts where loners can't spread out.
ecotypes.behavior: Tolerates neighbours; the first of its age to join a group.

ecotypes.name: Long-dive hunter
ecotypes.reading: The line's diving lineage at its solitary stage: stamina, speed and force underwater. Fits deep, icy seas.
ecotypes.behavior: Rarely seen on land; hunts alone and far out.

open_questions: What does it hunt in icy seas?
How does a loner that can't form groups become an adult that follows a leader?
Does Prinplup breed, or only Empoleon?
How much coast does one Prinplup claim?

Psyduck.summary: A pond duck with a constant headache and powers it can't remember using. When the headache peaks, Psyduck shows psychic or telekinetic power, apparently in an altered state like deep sleep, and afterwards it has no memory of it, which is why it always looks puzzled. Not one entry says what it eats or where it lives. HeartGold and SoulSilver put it on the water: it is 90% of what is met surfing Ilex Forest's pond.

anatomy.text: A yellow duck (0.8 m, 19.6 kg) that stands upright.
When it uses its power it produces brain waves otherwise seen only in sleepers, a discovery that caused controversy among scholars.
It can use its psychic power only when its sleeping brain cells happen to wake.

diet.text: Not stated in any entry.

Its moves suggest a scratching, splashing forager (Scratch at Lv 1, Water Gun 9, Fury Swipes 27), and a duck at the water's edge suggests water plants and small animals; but that is a guess from its body plan.
diet.note: No entry or capability record gives a diet.
diet.analogy: Real dabbling ducks eat a mix of water plants, seeds and invertebrates.

habitat.text: Water's edge by Gen 3 habitat. In HeartGold and SoulSilver it is surfed on Ilex Forest's pond (90%), Route 35 and Route 6, walks in Seafoam Islands, surfs in Cerulean Cave, and is in the Johto Safari Zone.
Golduck's entries put the line on lakes and quiet, slow rivers.
In Crystal it also walked Ilex Forest's grass at night (10%); HeartGold and SoulSilver keep it on the water.

behavior.text: It is constantly tormented by headaches, and when a headache peaks or worsens it starts using strange powers.
It can't remember using its powers, so it always looks puzzled and tilts its head.
During an episode it goes into an altered state much like deep sleep, and so forms no memory of it.
Activity is unknown: surfing tables have no time of day, and its land records (Crystal's Ilex Forest, HeartGold-SoulSilver's Safari Zone) are at night only.

social.text: Nothing is said about other Psyduck.

reproduction.text: Water 1 and Field egg groups, 20 egg cycles, an even sex ratio. Nothing in the Pokédex describes nesting or young.

defense.text: It lulls enemies with its vacant look while it uses psychokinetic powers: a 'wily' animal, in the oldest entry.
Its abilities are Damp (no one can self-destruct near it) and Cloud Nine (weather has no effect); Disable (14), Confusion (18) and Screech (31) are its disruptive moves.

senses.text: Nothing is said about its senses.

life_cycle.text: Psyduck becomes Golduck at level 33: the yellow, puzzled duck becomes a blue, fast, graceful swimmer whose forehead glows when it uses its power.
The headaches and forgetting belong to Psyduck alone; Golduck's entries describe its power as tied to a glowing forehead, not to pain or blackouts.

moves_in_the_wild.text: Water Sport (Lv 1), Water Gun (9), Water Pulse (22) and Hydro Pump (48): water used with growing force.
Confusion (18) and Zen Headbutt (40) are its psychic episodes in game form; Psych Up (35) and Amnesia (44) are status moves with no counterpart in the entries.

ecology.text: By surfing rate the pond's commonest surface animal, so probably its main large consumer, whatever it eats.
With no described diet, the pond's commonest surface animal has no food link at all; water plants, invertebrates, and the smaller Poliwag and Magikarp are the candidates.
ecology.note: A gap in the reconstructed web.

ecology.text: Damp stops anything near it from self-destructing, and Pineco, which explodes when its tree is shaken, lives in the same forest. The interaction is a game mechanic only.

humans.text: Its psychic episodes interest scholars: the sleep-like brain waves caused controversy.
The capability records say it could use hand tools and garden tools, because of its upright, handed body; that rests on body shape, not on any entry.

homestead.text: Watering: Water Gun is in its wild repertoire from level 9, and the capability records credit its upright body with handling objects, so it could carry water too. It could water the Glasshouse rows, which need heavy watering.
homestead.note: Untested; depends on it being calm enough for routine work.

homestead.text: Its headaches and the powers that come with them are unpredictable; keep it away from eggs and fragile equipment when it is visibly suffering.
homestead.note: No entry says its episodes are dangerous, only that they happen and it can't remember them.

homestead.text: It needs water to live by: a pond, a stream, or at least a large tub.
Damp is an odd but real benefit near anything that self-destructs, such as Pineco.

niche.foraging: unknown; probably dabbling and scratching at the pond margin
niche.note: No entry gives its diet; the guild is a guess from a duck body at the water's edge.

relationships.note: A guess from body plan and habitat; no entry gives its diet.
Ilex Forest's surfing table is Psyduck (90%) and Golduck (10%).

ecotypes.name: Seer
ecotypes.reading: A lineage in which the power is stronger and steadier, with a flavour of anticipation (Future Sight, Foresight). Fits waters with many threats, where early warning pays.
ecotypes.behavior: Fewer blackouts, more deliberate use of its power.

ecotypes.name: Drowsy lure
ecotypes.reading: A lineage that disarms threats by making them sleepy or confused, turning the 'vacant look' that lulls enemies (54.1) into a real tactic. Fits ponds with many predators and few hiding places.
ecotypes.behavior: Stares, yawns, and lets attackers lose interest.

ecotypes.name: Mud-bank brawler
ecotypes.reading: A physical lineage of muddy pond margins, flinging mud and striking with its arms, using its upright body. Fits shallow, silty ponds and marsh.
ecotypes.behavior: Fights on the bank rather than retreating to open water.

open_questions: What does it eat?
Where does it live, by the entries? None say; its habitat comes from game data and from Golduck.
What causes the headaches, and are the powers involuntary or deliberate?
Is it active by day or by night?
Does it nest at the pond margin?

contradictions.text: Deliberate or involuntary? Red/Blue calls it wily and has it lull enemies before using its power (54.1); Yellow says no one knows whether it means to use it (54.2), and later entries say it can't even remember using it (54.3, 54.7).

Pupitar.summary: The pupa of the Tyranitar line, and a pupa that won't keep still. Pupitar's shell is as hard as sheet rock or bedrock, and inside it the animal already has arms and legs and can move freely. It makes a gas in its body, compresses it and blasts it out to launch itself like a jet or a rocket, and its body can hit solid steel without harm. Its thrashing can topple a mountain. In HeartGold and SoulSilver it lives only on Mt. Silver's third floor, one encounter in twenty.

anatomy.text: A heavy, limbless-looking body (Gen 4 shape squiggle), 1.2 m and 152.0 kg, typed Rock and Ground: the Hard Shell Pokémon.
Its shell is as hard as sheet rock, its body as hard as bedrock, and it can hit solid steel without being damaged.
Under the shell it already has arms and legs, and even sealed in, it can move freely.
It makes a gas inside its body, compresses it, and ejects it to propel itself like a jet.
Where the gas comes from is not said. A pupa that doesn't eat would have to make it from its own stores, the soil it ate as a larva.
anatomy.note: Joins the pupa's gas with the larva's diet; no entry links them.

diet.text: No entry says Pupitar eats. The line's entries put all the eating in the larva, which sleeps once it has eaten enough to make a mountain.
Whether a Pupitar feeds at all is unknown.

habitat.text: Mountains: the Gen 3 Pokédex habitat is mountain, and its thrashing can topple one.
In HeartGold and SoulSilver it is found only on Mt. Silver's 3F, 5% at any time (Lv 45 in HeartGold, Lv 30 in SoulSilver). Crystal had it at the top of Mt. Silver by day and morning, 1%.
Being met inside the mountain, deeper than where Larvitar is commonest (the top), fits a pupa that rests in caves or burrows, but the tables can't show where it pupates.

behavior.text: It will not stay still, even while it is a pupa.
Hard and fast, it has outstanding destructive power; its thrashing can topple a mountain.
It travels by jet: venting pressurised gas launches it like a rocket.
Its activity pattern isn't stated; the HGSS tables list it at any time of day.

social.text: Nothing is said about pupae together or with adults.

reproduction.text: As a pupa it doesn't breed in its own right; the egg group (Monster), 40 egg cycles and an even sex ratio are the line's.

defense.text: Armour: a shell as hard as bedrock that survives a collision with solid steel.
Shed Skin, its ability, lets it heal its own status problems: a pupa that sloughs off what ails it.
Unlike most pupae it is not defenceless: it can move, thrash and launch itself, which turns the vulnerable stage of the life cycle into a dangerous one to approach.
defense.analogy: Most insect pupae can only wriggle; some, like mosquito pupae ('tumblers'), can swim away, but none fight back.

senses.text: Nothing is said about its senses.

life_cycle.text: It evolves from Larvitar at level 30 and into Tyranitar at 55, growing from 1.2 m and 152.0 kg to 2.0 m and 202.0 kg.
The line's own words call it a pupa (Crystal: 'even while it's a pupa'; Larvitar 'becomes a pupa'), and the limbs under the shell are the adult's, already formed.
Read as development, Pupitar is where the adult's body is built inside a shell: arms and legs form, the mass grows by half again, and the type will change from Ground to Dark.

moves_in_the_wild.text: Its level-up list is Larvitar's with later levels: Sandstorm, Screech, Rock Slide, Scary Face, Thrash (Lv 23, the 'thrashing' that topples a mountain), Dark Pulse, Payback, Crunch, Earthquake (Lv 47), Stone Edge (Lv 54).
No move is a jet or a launch; the gas-propelled travel is described only by the entries.

ecology.text: A non-feeding stage, if it truly doesn't eat: it takes nothing from the food web, but its thrashing and launches break rock and soil, so it reshapes the ground it rests in.
ecology.note: The diet is unstated, not stated to be nothing.

ecology.text: On Mt. Silver's 3F it shares the cave with Golbat, Graveler, Onix, Steelix and Sneasel; nothing is said to prey on it, and a bedrock shell leaves little to try.

humans.text: Nothing is said about Pupitar and people. A rock pupa that launches itself like a rocket is a hazard to anyone climbing Mt. Silver.

homestead.text: It may need nothing for a long stretch: if it doesn't eat, a sheltered, quiet cave and time are what it wants.
homestead.note: Depends on whether a pupa feeds.

homestead.text: Keep it away from anything breakable: it doesn't stay still, its thrashing breaks rock, and it can launch itself without warning.
Its strength could break rock for building stone if it can be set to thrash where it is wanted.
homestead.note: Untested: whether a Pupitar's thrashing can be directed.

homestead.text: The Ice Path's echo, some winters, of a Pupitar going off like a cork.

niche.foraging: none recorded; the line's eating is the larva's
niche.note: Filed with the line as a lithovore so the line reads as one guild; a pupa may not feed at all. Trophic level left null.

relationships.note: Its thrashing can topple a mountain.

ecotypes.name: Ridge rampager
ecotypes.reading: Tyranitar's rampaging lineage, seen in the pupa: a display, a frenzy and a heavy stamp. A Pupitar of this lineage thrashes more and rests less, the one whose thrashing topples mountains. Fits high, broken ridges.
ecotypes.behavior: Restless even for a Pupitar; leaves rockfalls behind it.

ecotypes.name: Iron-head jet
ecotypes.reading: A lineage whose shell is the weapon: launched by its gas jet, head first, into whatever is in the way, and braced for the impact. The entries already say its body survives hitting steel. Fits narrow caves where the only way out is through.
ecotypes.behavior: Rockets into walls and rivals and comes out unhurt.

open_questions: Does a Pupitar eat anything?
What gas does it make, and from what?
Where does a Larvitar go to pupate, and does it move about the mountain as a pupa?
How long is the pupal stage? Larvitar 'falls asleep so it can grow' (246.7): is Pupitar asleep inside the shell while it thrashes?

Quilava.summary: The nimble middle stage of the Typhlosion line: a four-legged animal covered in nonflammable fur that keeps enemies off with the heat of its flames and gusts of superheated air, and dodges while it scorches. Before a fight it turns its back to show how fiercely its fire blazes, and a turned back is a warning that it is about to attack with that fire. Where Cyndaquil hides its fire until frightened, Quilava uses it on purpose. Nothing says what it eats, and it is never wild in any Gen I-IV game.

anatomy.text: A four-legged animal (Gen 4 body shape quadruped), 0.9 m and 19.0 kg, typed Fire.
It is fully covered by nonflammable fur and can withstand any kind of fire attack.
Its fire is on its back, as in Cyndaquil: it attacks with the fire on its back and turns its back to display it.
Fireproof fur is what lets an animal carry flames on its own body without burning itself; the fur is the adaptation that makes the fire usable.

diet.text: No entry for any stage of the line says what it eats.
The machine reading's thermotroph comes from its Fire type alone; the Pokédex never says it takes in heat.
diet.note: Left out of the niche.

habitat.text: The Gen 3 Pokédex habitat is grassland. It is never found in the wild in any Gen I-IV game: it comes only from raising a Cyndaquil.
Where a wild Quilava would live is unknown.

behavior.text: Before battle, it turns its back on its opponent to demonstrate how ferociously its fire blazes.
A turned back during battle means it will attack with the fire on its back.
The fire burns more strongly when it readies to fight.
Turning the back is a threat display that also aims the weapon: the same move warns and attacks. It is a signal an opponent can learn to read, as the entries tell people to.
behavior.analogy: Many venomous or armed animals give an honest warning before attacking, like a skunk's handstand before it sprays.

social.text: Nothing is said about groups or how it treats its own kind.

reproduction.text: Field egg group, 20 egg cycles, 87.5% male, medium-slow growth; nothing in the Pokédex describes breeding.

defense.text: It keeps its foes at bay with the intensity of its flames and gusts of superheated air.
It uses its outstanding nimbleness to dodge attacks even while it scorches the foe.
It intimidates foes with the heat of its flames.
Its fur makes it safe from fire, so other fire-users have little to threaten it with.

senses.text: Nothing is said about its senses.

life_cycle.text: It evolves from Cyndaquil at level 14 (the archive also lists 17) and into Typhlosion at 36, growing from 0.9 m and 19.0 kg to 1.7 m and 79.5 kg.
It is where the line's fire changes use: the juvenile flares only when frightened (155.1), Quilava flares on purpose and dodges while it burns, and the adult hides inside its own heat haze (157.4).
Its body shape goes from Cyndaquil's two legs to four, and stays four-legged in Typhlosion.

moves_in_the_wild.text: Its level-up moves are Cyndaquil's, a little later: Smokescreen, Ember, Quick Attack, Flame Wheel (Lv 20), Defense Curl (Lv 24), Swift, Lava Plume (Lv 35), Flamethrower (Lv 42), Rollout, Double-Edge and Eruption (Lv 57). Quick Attack and Flame Wheel fit the nimble animal that scorches while it moves.
Lava Plume and Heat Wave (a tutor move) are spreading fire and hot air, the 'gusts of superheated air' in game form.

ecology.text: Its role in a food web can't be set: its diet is unknown and it has no wild range.
A fire-user that dodges as it burns would be a fire risk in dry grassland, its listed habitat.
ecology.note: Follows from the flames and the habitat only.

humans.text: The entries speak to Trainers: 'be careful if it turns its back during battle', a warning about how to read it.
It reaches people only by raising Professor Elm's Cyndaquil from New Bark Town.

homestead.text: A heat source with fireproof fur, easier to keep near people than a bare flame: its own coat doesn't catch.
Read its back: turned towards you, it is about to use its fire. Teach visitors that sign.
Fire attacks don't hurt it, so it could work close to a forge or a burn pile.
Quilava as the homestead's lamplighter, trotting along the paths at dusk with its back alight.

niche.foraging: unknown; no entry says what any stage eats
niche.note: Guild left empty, as for Cyndaquil and Typhlosion.

ecotypes.name: Wildfire charger
ecotypes.reading: Typhlosion's charging lineage in its nimble stage: a rallying call, a full-body fire charge and a rampage. In Quilava it would show as the back-turned display followed by a rush. Fits open grassland where there is room to charge.
ecotypes.behavior: Displays, howls, then charges through the grass on fire.

ecotypes.name: Side-step kicker
ecotypes.reading: Speed and footwork: a lineage that fights with its legs and its timing, matching the entries' 'outstanding nimbleness'. Fits broken ground where a dodge matters more than a charge.
ecotypes.behavior: Dodges, kicks and scorches, never standing still to take a hit.

open_questions: What does it eat, and what does its fire burn?
Where would a wild Quilava live?
Does the nonflammable fur also keep it warm, or cool?
How hot are the 'gusts of superheated air' (156.4), and how far do they reach?

Roserade.summary: A small, flower-handed predator that lures with scent and kills with poison. Roserade attracts prey with a sweet aroma, then strikes with poison-thorned whips hidden in its arms; HeartGold and SoulSilver add that the more toxic it is, the sweeter it smells. Its line starts as Budew, a bud that waits out winter closed and opens in spring sun beside clear pools, and passes through Roselia, whose scent relaxes people and whose flowers carry poisoned thorns. Roserade itself is never found in the wild; it is made by touching a Roselia with a Shiny Stone.

anatomy.text: A small upright animal (0.9 m, 14.5 kg) with a flower on each hand and thorny whips hidden in its arms; the whips are densely lined with poison thorns.
Each hand carries a different toxin, and both can jab with near-fatal power.
It also spews poison, a third delivery route beside whips and jabs.
Two separate toxins in two hands suggests either two glands or two sources of toxin; nothing says which, or what the toxins do.

diet.text: A predator: it draws prey in with a sweet aroma, then downs it with its whips or poison.
diet.analogy: Carnivorous plants such as pitcher plants (Sarracenia, Nepenthes) also lure prey with scent and nectar, while still photosynthesising; prey mainly supplies nitrogen and phosphorus.

diet.text: The prey is never named. A lure based on sweet scent suggests insects or other nectar seekers, but that is a guess.
diet.note: Sweet-scent lures attract nectar feeders in real systems; nothing in the entries says what Roserade catches.

diet.text: As a Grass type with Mega Drain at Lv 1 (and Synthesis and Giga Drain in the line), it probably also lives partly on sunlight and drains what it catches.
Roselia's flowers respond to the water it drinks: nutritionally rich springwater or clean water gives lovely, vivid blooms.

habitat.text: Roserade is not found in the wild in any Gen I-IV game, and no entry says where it lives.
Budew lives alongside clear ponds and pools; Roselia's Gen 3 habitat is grassland.

In HeartGold and SoulSilver the line is barely present: Budew only through the Sinnoh Sound radio in Ilex and Viridian Forests, and Budew and Roselia only in the Johto Safari Zone once enough plains or forest blocks are placed. It is common in Sinnoh (Eterna Forest, Routes 204 and 212, Trophy Garden, Great Marsh).
Water quality matters to the line: Budew picks clear water, and Roselia's flowers show what it drinks.

behavior.text: It fights with the movements of a dancer.
A lure-and-strike forager: it lets scent do the searching and the prey come to it.
Probably day-active: Budew opens in the sun's warmth and evolves by day, and Sinnoh tables add day and morning slots for Budew and Roselia. Nothing is said about Roserade's own hours.

social.text: No entry describes groups, pairs or interactions with its own kind.

reproduction.text: Roselia and Roserade are in the Fairy and Grass egg groups, with an even sex ratio and 20 egg cycles; Budew is a baby Pokémon in the Undiscovered group and can't breed.
Budew's bud opens in spring to release pollen, which in a plant is reproductive. Oddly, the stage that releases pollen is the one the games say cannot breed.
reproduction.note: Pollen is described only as an irritant and a seasonal release; no entry ties it to breeding.

defense.text: Chemical and mechanical at once: poison-thorned whips, toxic jabs, sprayed poison, and Poison Point (contact may poison an attacker).
Roselia defends its flowers: it shoots sharp thorns at anything trying to steal them, the thorns on its head carry a vicious poison, and its arm flowers have toxic thorns.
Roselia's fragrance makes its foes careless, a softer defence that disarms rather than injures.
Natural Cure, its other possible ability, clears its status problems when it withdraws from a fight.

senses.text: Budew is sensitive to temperature and opens its bud when it feels the sun's warmth.
senses.note: Platinum (406.3) hedges the same thing as 'said to'; see folklore.

senses.text: Nothing is said about how Roserade detects prey that its scent has drawn in.

life_cycle.text: Budew (0.2 m, 1.2 kg) becomes Roselia (0.3 m, 2.0 kg) when it levels up with high friendship by day, and Roselia becomes Roserade (0.9 m, 14.5 kg) when exposed to a Shiny Stone. The archive lists the line as Roselia, Budew, Roserade, but Budew is the first stage.
Budew spends winter as a closed bud enduring the cold, and opens in spring to release pollen.
The line goes from a bud, to flowers on the arms, to a bouquet on each hand with whips inside the arms; the defensive thorns of Roselia become the predatory weapons of Roserade.
The scent changes meaning: in Roselia a stronger aroma means a healthier animal; in Roserade a sweeter aroma means a more toxic one. Both may be the same thing, if a healthy animal makes more toxin.

moves_in_the_wild.text: Roserade's own level-up list in HeartGold is short, all at Lv 1: Sweet Scent (the lure), Poison Sting (the thorns), Mega Drain and Magical Leaf. Sweet Scent is the canon hunting method in move form.

Roselia's level-up list holds most of the line's natural repertoire: Stun Spore, Leech Seed, Grass Whistle, Toxic Spikes, Ingrain, Toxic, Aromatherapy and Synthesis, which together read as a plant that drugs, drains and poisons rather than chases.
Budew learns Water Sport (Lv 7), which fits a pond-edge animal.

ecology.text: A small ambush predator using scent as bait (trophic level about 3 if its prey are herbivores or nectar feeders).
Budew's pollen goes into the air in spring and causes harsh sneezing and runny noses, so the line affects the animals around clear ponds as an allergen source.
ecology.analogy: Hay fever in people is mostly caused by wind-dispersed pollen, from grasses, birch and the like.

ecology.text: Because Roselia's flowers track water quality, the line could serve as a living indicator of clean water.
ecology.note: The entries say water changes the flowers; whether poor water dulls them is not stated.

humans.text: Its flowers tempt people, which is dangerous: 'Don't even think about picking those flowers.'
Roselia's scent deeply relaxes people and brings serenity to living things.
People make Roserade: it comes only from a Roselia exposed to a Shiny Stone.

homestead.text: A handling hazard: near-fatal toxins in both hands, poison-lined whips and Poison Point. Keep it away from children, grazing animals and the nursery, and handle with gloves.
A possible pest trap for the Glasshouse: it lures and kills small animals with scent. Whether it takes pests rather than pollinators is untested and important.
homestead.note: Prey identity is unknown; a lure that works on pollinators would harm the berry beds.

homestead.text: Keep Budew out of the house and the Glasshouse in spring: its pollen causes harsh sneezing.
Budew survives winter by closing up, which suits Blackthorn's cold season without heated housing; whether Roserade is as hardy is not said.
A Roselia's flowers as a check on the water it is drinking.
homestead.note: Unproven as an indicator.

homestead.text: Sweet Scent, its own move, draws wild Pokémon out, which a forager can use and a guard should know about.
Needs: clean water, sun, and a pond edge for the young.

niche.foraging: sit-and-wait lure predator: draws prey with a sweet scent and strikes with poison-thorned whips; probably also photosynthetic
niche.note: Prey never named; activity read from Budew and Roselia, not Roserade.

ecotypes.name: Thorn thicket
ecotypes.reading: Roselia's thorn-shooting made heritable and extended: Pin Missile fires a volley of thorns, Spikes scatters barbs on the ground. A lineage that defends a fixed patch, like a dense flowerbed, from browsers and flower thieves rather than hunting. Fits crowded meadow and garden edges where its blooms draw trouble.
ecotypes.behavior: Holds a patch, fires at anything that reaches for a flower, and litters the approach with barbs.

ecotypes.name: Sleeping lure
ecotypes.reading: The scent lure with a sedative behind it: Sleep Powder puts the animal it has drawn in to sleep, Cotton Spore slows anything that tries to leave, and Mind Reader makes the next strike certain. A sit-and-wait trap that needs no venom to work. Fits sheltered pond margins where prey come to drink.
ecotypes.behavior: Lures, drugs and only then strikes; rarely needs to chase.

ecotypes.name: Sun-fed bloom
ecotypes.reading: A lineage that leans on sunlight rather than prey: Synthesis for recovery in the sun, Razor Leaf for everyday defence, Leaf Storm as a single all-out burst that costs it afterwards. Fits open, sunny grassland where prey is scarce and light is not.
ecotypes.behavior: Basks more and lures less; hits hard once when threatened, then retreats to recover.

open_questions: What does Roserade catch? Its prey is never named.
What are the two toxins in its two hands (407.3), and does it choose between them?
If sweeter means more toxic (407.4), what tells prey to keep coming? Is the scent a lure, a warning, or both?
Is Budew's spring pollen reproductive, given that Budew itself cannot breed in the games?
Where does a wild Roserade live? Shiny Stones are the only route the games give.
Does Roserade keep Budew's winter dormancy?

contradictions.text: Water and flower colour: Diamond states as known fact that Roselia raised on clean drinking water grow vividly coloured flowers; HeartGold and SoulSilver say only that Roselia drinking rich springwater are 'said to' reveal rare coloration; Emerald states that springwater gives lovely flowers.
contradictions.note: Vivid versus rare colour, and fact versus report. The rare-colour version is filed as folklore.

contradictions.text: Budew's bloom on the sun's warmth: HeartGold and SoulSilver state it plainly; Platinum says the bud is 'said to' bloom that way.

folklore.text: On extremely rare occasions a Roselia is said to appear with its flowers in unusual colours.
folklore.note: Reported as hearsay. Likely the games' rare colour variants described in-world.

folklore.text: Roselia that drink nutritionally rich springwater are said to show rare colouring when they bloom.
Budew's bud is said to bloom when it feels the sun's warm touch.
folklore.note: Hedged in Platinum, stated as fact in HeartGold and SoulSilver (406.4).

Salamence.summary: The winged adult of the Bagon line, and the rival's SoulSilver Pokémon. Its whole line is a story about wanting to fly: Bagon throws itself off cliffs every day and grows a steel-hard head from the falls, Shelgon shuts itself in an iron shell while its cells rebuild its body, and Salamence is what grows when, after many long years, a sudden mutation gives it wings. It wheels across the sky spouting flame for joy, and when it is enraged it loses all thought and rampages out of control, scorching fields and mountains. It is never wild in a Gen I-IV game; in HeartGold and SoulSilver Bagon is only in the Johto Safari Zone.

anatomy.text: A four-legged winged dragon (Gen 4 shape quadruped), 1.5 m and 102.6 kg, typed Dragon and Flying.
It has wings, which grew when its cellular structure underwent a sudden mutation.
It spouts flames from its mouth and has shredding claws.

diet.text: No entry for any stage says what Salamence eats. Shelgon hardly eats while it waits to evolve (372.3).
Bite, Crunch (Lv 53) and Dragon Claw (Lv 61) are its biting and clawing moves; none names a food.
The machine reading's 'predator' comes from the Dragon type only.
diet.note: Guild left empty.

habitat.text: The sky over fields and mountains, which it scorches; the Gen 3 Pokédex habitat is rough terrain. Its young leap off cliffs (371.5) and Shelgon hides in caverns while it waits to evolve (372.2).
It is never wild in any Gen I-IV game. In HeartGold and SoulSilver, Bagon is found only in the Johto Safari Zone, when its blocks are placed.

behavior.text: To express its joy at having wings, it flies and wheels all over the sky while spouting flames.
It becomes uncontrollable if enraged: it loses all thought, rampages, and destroys everything with shredding claws and fire, scorching fields and mountains.
Its activity pattern isn't stated.

social.text: Nothing is said about groups or pairs.

reproduction.text: Dragon egg group, 40 egg cycles (twice the usual), an even sex ratio, slow growth.

defense.text: Intimidate, its ability, lowers an opponent's Attack. Nothing in the Pokédex describes anything attacking a Salamence.
Protect (Lv 30) is the shell-stage defence carried into the adult.

senses.text: Nothing is said about its senses.

life_cycle.text: Bagon becomes Shelgon at level 30 and Salamence at 50: 0.6 m and 42.1 kg, then 1.1 m and 110.5 kg, then 1.5 m and 102.6 kg.
Salamence came about from a strong, long-held dream of growing wings; by evolving, it finally realises that dream.

Read as development, the line is a metamorphosis with a resting stage: Shelgon's cells transform inside an armour-like shell that peels off when it evolves (372.1, 372.5), much as a pupa's body is rebuilt.
life_cycle.analogy: Insect pupae rebuild the larval body into the winged adult inside a case.

life_cycle.text: Wings arriving by 'a sudden mutation' after 'many long years' is the entries' own explanation; biologically a mutation doesn't happen on purpose, so the 'dream' is best read as the line's story about itself.
life_cycle.note: The dream-caused mutation is told as 'it is said' in Ruby (C373.2).

moves_in_the_wild.text: Its list joins the line's earlier moves (Bite, Leer, Headbutt, Focus Energy, Ember, Protect, Dragon Breath, Zen Headbutt, Scary Face) to Fly at level 50, the level it gains its wings, then Crunch, Dragon Claw and Double-Edge.

ecology.text: Its role can't be set: its diet is unknown and it is never wild.
An enraged Salamence scorching fields and mountains would be a fire-starter on the scale of a wildfire.

humans.text: It becomes uncontrollable if enraged: the entries warn of it as they do of Gyarados.

homestead.text: Flight for a rider, if it will carry one: it gained its wings on purpose and loves to use them.
homestead.note: Carrying a rider is untested.

homestead.text: Never let it lose its temper near the homestead: an enraged Salamence scorches fields.
It needs open sky and cliffs; a Bagon needs cliffs to jump from.
The rival's Salamence wheeling over the Ice Path on a clear morning, flames streaming, for no reason but joy.

microhabitat: open sky over fields and mountains
niche.foraging: unknown; no entry says what any stage eats
niche.note: Guild left empty: the machine reading's predator comes from the Dragon type alone.

relationships.note: By scorching them when enraged.

ecotypes.name: Sky-joy flier
ecotypes.reading: The wheeling, flame-spouting flight the entries describe as joy: a dance and a whirlwind. A lineage that flies for display as much as travel. Fits open skies over mountains.
ecotypes.behavior: Wheels and loops over its range on clear days.

ecotypes.name: Cliff-diver
ecotypes.reading: A lineage of the Bagon that never stopped hurling itself off cliffs: a full-body dragon charge, a rampage and a fiery bite. The most likely to lose all thought when angered. Fits sheer cliffs and ravines.
ecotypes.behavior: Dives from height at whatever angers it.

open_questions: What does Salamence eat?
Does every Bagon reach Salamence, or only those that 'dream' hardest?
Where do wild Salamence live? No game has them wild.
How long does a Shelgon spend in its shell before the wings come?

folklore.text: It is said that its powerful desire to fly triggered a sudden mutation in its cells, causing it to sprout wings.

Sandshrew.summary: A small desert burrower with a very dry, extremely tough hide. Sandshrew lives in deep burrows in arid places far from water, which it dislikes, and its body absorbs water without waste. It only comes out to hunt. Its defence is a ball: it rolls itself instantly into one, and attacks bounce off it; rolled up, it could even survive a fall from a great height by bouncing. In HeartGold and SoulSilver it is HeartGold's, in Union Cave and Mt. Moon, the dry inside of mountains rather than a desert.

anatomy.text: A small upright animal (Gen 4 shape upright), 0.6 m and 12.0 kg, typed Ground: the Mouse Pokémon.
Its hide is very dry and extremely tough, turned tough and solid by life in the desert.
Its body is configured to absorb water without waste, so it survives in arid desert.
anatomy.analogy: Desert rodents such as kangaroo rats get almost all their water from food and lose very little.

diet.text: It only emerges to hunt for food, or for prey.
Its prey isn't named. Scratch, Fury Swipes (Lv 19) and Slash (Lv 31) are claw moves, and Poison Sting (Lv 9) a sting; a 12 kg burrower would take insects and small animals.
When it gets cold at night its hide is said to become coated with fine dew: perhaps a way of getting water in a dry place.
diet.note: The dew is told as 'said'; using it for water is a reading.

habitat.text: Deep burrows in arid places far from water: it dislikes water and prefers dry, sandy places. The Gen 3 Pokédex habitat is rough terrain.
In HeartGold and SoulSilver it is HeartGold's: Union Cave (30%) and Mt. Moon (20%), at any time; the Johto Safari Zone has it in both versions.
Caves are not deserts, but the dry, sandy floors of caves suit an animal that burrows and avoids water.

behavior.text: At night it burrows into the desert sand to sleep.
So it sleeps at night and hunts by day, by Sapphire's entry; the HGSS cave tables have it at all hours.

social.text: Nothing is said about groups or pairs.

reproduction.text: Field egg group, 20 egg cycles, an even sex ratio, medium growth. Nothing describes breeding.

defense.text: It rolls itself instantly into a ball when threatened, and in a ball it makes any attack bounce off harmlessly.
It uses sand to protect itself when threatened, which is why it prefers sandy places.
If it fell from a great height, it could save itself by rolling into a ball and bouncing.
defense.analogy: Armadillos and pangolins roll into armoured balls for the same reason.

defense.text: Defense Curl (Lv 3), Sand Attack (Lv 7), Rollout (Lv 21), Sand Tomb and Sandstorm are the ball and the sand in game form; Sand Veil helps it dodge in a sandstorm.

senses.text: Nothing is said about its senses.

life_cycle.text: It becomes Sandslash at level 22 (the archive also lists an Ice Stone, a later games' route), from 0.6 m and 12.0 kg to 1.0 m and 29.5 kg.
Read as development, the smooth tough hide becomes Sandslash's spikes, which are hardened sections of hide (28.6).

moves_in_the_wild.text: Scratch, Defense Curl, Sand Attack, Poison Sting, Rapid Spin, Swift, Fury Swipes, Rollout, Fury Cutter, Sand Tomb, Slash, Gyro Ball and Sandstorm: the ball, the sand and the claws.

ecology.text: A small burrowing hunter; burrows in sandy ground move soil and make shelter others can use.
In Mt. Moon it shares the cave with Zubat, Geodude, Paras and Clefairy; in Union Cave with Wooper, Quagsire, Onix and Rattata.

humans.text: Nothing is said about Sandshrew and people.

homestead.text: It wants dry, sandy ground and no water: a sandy bank or a dry barn floor, not the lakeside.
A digger of deep burrows: it could dig, if the burrows go where they are wanted.
Its water thrift would suit dry summers but not the highland wet.
Sandshrew rolling down the homestead's scree slope for fun, bouncing at the bottom and doing it again.

microhabitat: deep burrows in dry, sandy ground
dry cave floors (Mt. Moon, Union Cave)
niche.foraging: emerges from its burrow only to hunt
niche.note: Prey never named; trophic level assumes insects and small animals. Day activity from its sleeping in sand at night (27.7).

relationships.note: What a 12 kg burrower would mostly find; never named.
To protect itself, and to sleep in.

ecotypes.name: Night-slash digger
ecotypes.reading: A claw lineage: three strong claw strikes carried by the line. A Sandshrew that digs and hunts with its claws more than it rolls. Fits hard, stony ground.
ecotypes.behavior: Digs faster and deeper; stands and fights.

ecotypes.name: Rockslide roller
ecotypes.reading: A lineage of slopes: rock thrown down, a spinning ball, and mud. A Sandshrew that rolls and brings the slope with it. Fits scree and cave ramps like Mt. Moon's.
ecotypes.behavior: Rolls downhill at threats in a shower of stones.

open_questions: What does Sandshrew hunt?
Why does HeartGold have it in caves when its entries say desert?
What fills Sandshrew's slot in SoulSilver's Mt. Moon and Union Cave?
Does the night dew on its hide (27.2) give it water?

folklore.text: When it gets cold at night, its hide is said to become coated with a fine dew.

Sandslash.summary: The spiny adult of Sandshrew. Sandslash's back is covered in tough spikes, hardened sections of its hide, which fall out once a year as new ones grow beneath; spikes and claws that snap off when it digs too fast grow back in a day. It curls into a spiny ball to protect itself, and to avoid heatstroke on hot days, and rolls into foes back first; in a fight it jabs with its spines to make the foe flinch, then leaps at it and tears with its claws. It climbs trees to attack from above, and kicks up a blinding dust storm to hide. In HeartGold and SoulSilver it is HeartGold's: Route 26, Route 27 and Mt. Moon.

anatomy.text: An upright animal (Gen 4 shape upright), 1.0 m and 29.5 kg, typed Ground: the Mouse Pokémon.
Its body is covered by tough spikes, which are hardened sections of its hide.
anatomy.analogy: Porcupine quills and hedgehog spines are modified hairs, a similar hardening of the skin's growths.

anatomy.text: It has sharp claws.

diet.text: No entry says what Sandslash eats. Its young emerges only to hunt (27.10), so the line is a hunter.
Crush Claw (Lv 22, learned on evolving), Fury Swipes and Slash are its claw attacks.

habitat.text: The Gen 3 Pokédex habitat is rough terrain; it is adept at climbing trees.
In HeartGold and SoulSilver it is HeartGold's: Route 26 (30%, Lv 28), Route 27 (5%) and Mt. Moon (5%), at any time; the Johto Safari Zone has it in both versions.
Its HeartGold range, two roads below Victory Road and a mountain cave, matches the rough terrain of its listed habitat.

behavior.text: It curls up to prevent heatstroke during the daytime when temperatures rise sharply.
To hide, it runs around at top speed to kick up a blinding dust storm.
If it digs at an incredible pace, it may snap off its spikes and claws.
Its activity pattern isn't stated; curling up against midday heat suggests it rests in the heat of the day.

social.text: Nothing is said about groups or pairs.

reproduction.text: Field egg group, 20 egg cycles, an even sex ratio, medium growth.

defense.text: It curls up into a spiny ball when threatened, and can roll while curled up to attack or escape.
In battle it jabs the foe with its spines to make it flinch, then leaps at the stunned foe to tear wildly with its claws.
It curls up, then rolls into foes with its back, and its sharp spines inflict severe damage.
Adept at climbing trees, it rolls into a spiny ball and attacks its enemies from above.

senses.text: Nothing is said about its senses.

life_cycle.text: It evolves from Sandshrew at level 22, from 0.6 m and 12.0 kg to 1.0 m and 29.5 kg.
Once a year its old spikes fall out and new ones grow from beneath; broken spikes and claws grow back within a day.
life_cycle.analogy: Animals that moult once a year, like many birds, replace worn armour or feathers on a cycle.

moves_in_the_wild.text: Sandshrew's list with Crush Claw added: Defense Curl, Sand Attack, Poison Sting, Rapid Spin, Swift, Fury Swipes, Rollout, Fury Cutter, Sand Tomb, Slash, Gyro Ball and Sandstorm (Lv 52). Sand Attack and Sandstorm are its dust storm.

ecology.text: A spiny hunter of rough country, by its young's habit; its prey and predators are unnamed.
Its shed spikes, falling once a year, would litter its range.

humans.text: Nothing is said about Sandslash and people.

homestead.text: A fast digger that regrows its claws in a day: trenching and post holes, if it will dig where asked.
Its shed spikes, once a year, could be collected as tough points or awls.
homestead.note: Untested.

homestead.text: Handle with care; it rolls into foes spines first.
A Sandslash curled in the shade of the porch through every summer noon, uncurling at dusk.

niche.foraging: unknown; its young emerges from burrows to hunt
niche.note: Filed as a predator with Sandshrew; Sandslash's own diet is never stated.

relationships.note: Its young hunts from a burrow; prey never named.
To climb and attack from.
Mt. Moon, HeartGold.

ecotypes.name: Tree-drop ambusher
ecotypes.reading: The tree-climbing attacker of Crystal's entry as a lineage: it readies its claws, drops, slashes and hits back. Fits wooded rough ground with trees to climb.
ecotypes.behavior: Waits in trees and drops onto what passes.

ecotypes.name: Dust-storm runner
ecotypes.reading: A lineage that hides in its own dust: spinning, throwing mud and thrashing. Fits open, dry ground where a dust cloud can hide it.
ecotypes.behavior: Vanishes in dust when threatened.

open_questions: What does Sandslash eat?
Why is it HeartGold's only, and what holds its slot in SoulSilver?
When in the year do its spikes fall, and what happens to them?
Is it active by day, given it curls up against midday heat?

Scizor.summary: A steel-hard, red insect that has traded its parent's camouflage and flight for armour and a bluff. Scizor's pincers carry eye-like markings that it raises to make itself look three-headed, and they contain steel enough to crush any hard object. Its wings no longer fly; it flaps them fast to regulate its body temperature. It develops from Scyther, a green, grass-hiding ambusher with scythes that cut logs, and in the games only a Scyther traded while holding a Metal Coat becomes one.

anatomy.text: A heavy, winged insect (1.8 m, 118.0 kg) with a body as hard as steel.
Two pincers that contain steel and can crush any hard object they grip; they carry eye-like markings.
Its wings are not used for flying; they are flapped at high speed to adjust body temperature.
anatomy.analogy: Bumblebees and many moths warm up by shivering their flight muscles before they can fly; whether Scizor's flapping warms it or cools it is not said.

anatomy.text: If its steel-hard body conducts heat the way metal does, it would warm and cool quickly, which may be why it needs the wing-flapping.
anatomy.note: A physical guess linking two canon facts; no entry connects them.

diet.text: No entry says what Scizor eats.
Scyther is a predator: it leaps out of tall grass to slice prey, and tears and shreds it with its scythes.
diet.analogy: Praying mantises (Mantodea), which Scyther's category names, are sit-and-wait predators that seize prey with raptorial forelegs.

diet.text: Crushing pincers suit hard-shelled prey, which Scyther's slicing scythes would not; Scizor may take different food from its parent.
diet.note: Built on anatomy alone.

habitat.text: Its Gen 3 Pokédex habitat is grassland; Scyther hides in tall grass.
Scizor is not found in the wild in any Gen I-IV game.

In HeartGold and SoulSilver, Scyther appears only during the National Park Bug-Catching Contest (5%), and after the National Pokédex only on Tuesday, Thursday and Saturday contests. In Platinum it is on Routes 210 and 215, commoner in the morning; in Kanto, in the Safari Zone or as a Game Corner prize.

behavior.text: Threat display: it raises its eye-patterned pincers to intimidate, which makes it look three-headed, and it can swing them down dangerously.
Scyther relies on speed: too fast for the eye, leaving only a blur, so fast its opponent doesn't know what hit it, and very proud of it.
Scyther rarely flies; Scizor doesn't fly at all.
Platinum's Scyther are commoner in the morning; no activity pattern is stated for Scizor.

social.text: No entry describes groups. Scyther's speed can create the illusion of more than one, which is a solitary animal looking like many, not a group.

reproduction.text: Bug egg group, even sex ratio, 25 egg cycles (a little longer than most). Nothing is said about breeding or young.

defense.text: A deimatic bluff: the eyespots on its raised pincers make it look like a three-headed animal.
defense.analogy: The peacock butterfly (Aglais io) flashes large eyespots on its wings when disturbed, which experiments show deters small birds.

defense.text: Armour: its steel-hard body is not easily fazed by ordinary attacks.
Scyther's defence was concealment instead: its protective colouring makes it invisible in grass.
Iron Defense (Lv 37) is in Scizor's own level-up list; Swarm or Technician are its abilities.

senses.text: Nothing is said about Scizor's senses. An eyespot display only works on predators that see well, so its enemies are probably visual hunters.

life_cycle.text: Scyther (1.5 m, 56.0 kg, Bug/Flying, green) becomes Scizor (1.8 m, 118.0 kg, Bug/Steel, red) when traded holding a Metal Coat.
The change swaps strategies: from camouflage, speed and slicing scythes to bright colour, a bluff display, crushing pincers and armour; from rare flight to wings used only for heat.
The weight doubles while the height grows only 0.3 m, which fits a body that becomes metal-hard.
Scyther's scythes grow sharper by cutting hard objects; whether that habit feeds into Scizor's steel is not said.

moves_in_the_wild.text: Scizor's level-up list mixes speed and steel: Quick Attack and Bullet Punch (Lv 1), Agility, Metal Claw (Lv 21), Iron Defense (Lv 37), Iron Head (Lv 53).
The cutting moves (Fury Cutter, Slash, X-Scissor, Night Slash) are shared with Scyther and match the scythe canon; in Scizor they come from pincers.
Pursuit (Lv 9) and False Swipe (Lv 13) suit a predator that chases down and holds prey rather than killing at once.
Steel Wing and Roost are machine moves: taught, and of little use to an animal that doesn't fly.

ecology.text: A large insect predator of grassland (trophic level about 3-3.5), if Scizor hunts as Scyther does.
In HeartGold's Bug-Catching Contest, Scyther shares the National Park grass with Butterfree, Beedrill, Caterpie and other contest bugs, only on contest days.

humans.text: People make Scizor: it evolves only by trade, holding a Metal Coat.
Scyther's attacks are nearly impossible to parry, and its scythes cut thick logs in one stroke: dangerous at close quarters.

homestead.text: Breaking hard material: its pincers crush any hard object, useful for stone, nuts or scrap metal at the Works.
Timber and brush clearing is Scyther's job rather than Scizor's: Scyther's scythes slice thick logs in one stroke and cut through grass.
A deterrent at the gate: its three-headed pincer display is built to frighten.
Watch it in Blackthorn's cold: it manages its body temperature by flapping its wings, and how well that works in a highland winter is unknown.
Its size is in the rider range, but it cannot fly and no entry says it carries anyone.
Keep people clear when it swings its pincers down; the display can turn into a strike.

niche.foraging: Scyther: ambush from tall grass and high-speed slashing; Scizor: unknown, perhaps crushing hard prey
niche.note: Scizor's own diet is never stated; the machine reading's herbivore comes from the Bug type alone.

relationships.note: Stated for Scyther.
Cover for Scyther's ambush.
National Park Bug-Catching Contest, HeartGold and SoulSilver (Scyther).

ecotypes.name: Tall-grass reaper
ecotypes.reading: A patient ambusher: Razor Wind takes a turn to charge before it cuts, and Night Slash is a high-critical strike from cover. A lineage that waits in grass and lands one decisive blow, the Yellow canon of leaping out of tall grass in heritable form. Fits dense tall-grass meadow.
ecotypes.behavior: Waits motionless in long grass; one strike, rarely two.

ecotypes.name: Last-stand fencer
ecotypes.reading: A lineage that fights through injury: Endure survives a blow that would knock it out, Reversal hits hardest when it is nearly beaten, and Counter returns physical attacks double. It suits Scizor's armour-and-bluff life, where it holds its ground instead of fleeing. Fits contested open ground where it can't hide.
ecotypes.behavior: Never runs; most dangerous when hurt.

ecotypes.name: Wing-singer
ecotypes.reading: Wings used for sound and wind rather than flight: Bug Buzz is a damaging vibration, Silver Wind a gust of wing scales that can boost all its stats. A lineage that turns Scizor's non-flying, fast-flapping wings into a weapon and display. Fits open meadow where sound carries.
ecotypes.behavior: Buzzes loudly when threatened, before any display of the pincers.

open_questions: What does Scizor eat, and does it still hunt as Scyther does?
Does wing-flapping warm it, cool it, or both (212.2, 212.4)?
How does a Scyther become steel? The games require a held Metal Coat and a trade, neither of which has a wild equivalent.
Is there a wild Scizor population anywhere?
Are the pincer eyespots a bluff against particular predators, and which?
How does it cope with Blackthorn's cold, as a steel-bodied insect that relies on its wings for temperature control?

Scyther.summary: A green mantis-like hunter of tall grass. Scyther hides in the grass, where its colours make it invisible, then leaps out and slices prey with twin scythes on its forearms, moving too fast for the eye to follow; its speed adds to the scythes' sharpness, and cutting hard things makes them sharper still. It can cut thick logs in one stroke, and it very rarely spreads its wings to fly. It is the young of SoulSilver's Scizor. In HeartGold and SoulSilver it appears only in the Bug-Catching Contest at the National Park, which stocks it, so Johto has no resident population.

anatomy.text: A winged insect (Gen 4 shape bug-wings), 1.5 m and 56.0 kg, typed Bug and Flying: the Mantis Pokémon.
Twin scythes on its forearms, sharp enough to slice through thick logs in one stroke.
The scythes become sharper by cutting through hard objects.
It has wings but very rarely spreads them to fly.
Its colours are protective: hiding in grass, it becomes invisible.
anatomy.analogy: Praying mantises are green or brown like the plants they wait in, a camouflage for an ambush predator.

diet.text: It leaps out of tall grass and slices prey with its scythes; it tears and shreds prey.
Its prey is never named. A 56 kg ambusher that can cut logs could take large animals, but nothing says it does.
The machine reading's 'omnivore' comes from 'tall grass' being read as plant food; the entries only hide it in grass.
diet.note: Filed as a predator.

diet.text: Pursuit (Lv 9), Fury Cutter (Lv 25), Slash (Lv 29), X-Scissor (Lv 41) and Night Slash (Lv 45) are the scythe strikes in game form.

habitat.text: Tall grass, which it hides in and leaps out of; the Gen 3 Pokédex habitat is grassland.
In HeartGold and SoulSilver it appears only in the Bug-Catching Contest at the National Park (5%; on Tuesday, Thursday and Saturday after the National Pokédex), in both versions.
The Contest stocks the park with bugs, so a Contest Scyther says nothing about a native population: Johto and Kanto have no wild Scyther outside it.

behavior.text: It slashes through grass with its scythes, moving too fast for the human eye to track; when it moves it leaves only a blur.
With ninja-like agility and speed it can create the illusion that there is more than one of itself; its movements are like a ninja's.
It is very proud of its speed, and moves so fast its opponent doesn't know what knocked it down.
Its activity pattern isn't stated; the Contest runs by day.

social.text: Nothing is said about groups; every entry describes a lone ambusher.

reproduction.text: Bug egg group, 25 egg cycles, an even sex ratio, medium growth. Nothing describes eggs or young.

defense.text: Camouflage in grass, and speed: it hides, and when seen it is a blur.
Its attacking scythes are nearly impossible to parry.
Double Team (Lv 37), an illusion of copies, matches the entries' 'more than one of itself'.

senses.text: Nothing is said about its senses. An ambusher that strikes too fast to be seen must judge distance well, but how is not described.

life_cycle.text: It becomes Scizor only by trade while holding a Metal Coat; Scizor is Bug and Steel and its wings are no longer used for flying (212.2).
Read as development, the change trades camouflage and speed for armour and a bluff (Scizor's eye-marked pincers), as Scizor's dossier says; it happens only through people, in the games.

moves_in_the_wild.text: Its level-up list is the ambush in order: Quick Attack and Vacuum Wave at level 1, Focus Energy, Pursuit, False Swipe, Agility, Wing Attack, Fury Cutter, Slash, Razor Wind, Double Team, X-Scissor, Night Slash, Double Hit, Air Slash, Swords Dance and Feint.
Technician, its second ability, powers up weak moves: many quick, light cuts rather than one heavy blow.

ecology.text: A top ambush predator of tall grass, by its own entries. With no wild Johto population, it has no place in a Johto or Kanto web.
Cutting through grass and logs as it moves, a Scyther changes the grass it hunts in, opening paths.
ecology.note: Follows from its slashing only.

humans.text: It moves too fast for the human eye to track.
People meet it in the National Park's Bug-Catching Contest, which stocks the park.

homestead.text: It cuts thick logs in one stroke: firewood and clearing, if it can be trusted to cut only what it is asked.
Its scythes sharpen as they cut hard things; it will want hard things to cut.
Keep tall grass for it to hide in, away from paths where people walk: it strikes from cover.
The homestead's Scyther as the hay-mower, and the blur at the edge of the meadow.

niche.foraging: ambush from tall grass, then high-speed slashing with twin scythes
niche.note: Predator, as for Scizor; prey never named.

relationships.note: Cover for the ambush.

ecotypes.name: Tall-grass reaper
ecotypes.reading: Scizor's grass-hunting lineage at the stage that hunts in grass: a critical slash and a wind-blade. The archetypal Scyther. Fits tall, dense grassland.
ecotypes.behavior: Never leaves the long grass; strikes from it.

ecotypes.name: Wing-singer
ecotypes.reading: A lineage that uses its wings, which most Scyther rarely spread: a gust of scales and a buzzing sound. A Scyther that flies more and signals with sound. Fits open woodland edges where flight pays.
ecotypes.behavior: Seen in the air more than others; buzzes at rivals.

ecotypes.name: Last-stand fencer
ecotypes.reading: A lineage that turns a losing fight: it endures, then hits back hardest when nearly beaten. Fits contested grassland where rivals are many.
ecotypes.behavior: Rarely flees; most dangerous when hurt.

open_questions: What does Scyther hunt?
Where are the wild populations the Contest stocks from?
Does it ever fly, and why so rarely (123.8)?
Is it solitary?

Seadra.summary: The spiny, poisonous middle stage of the Kingdra line. Seadra's body bristles with poison barbs and spikes that can make a careless person faint; it sleeps wedged between coral branches with its tail hooked on, and it spins its body to make whirlpools strong enough to swallow fishing boats, weakening prey in the current and then swallowing it whole. The male raises the young and shows no mercy to anything approaching the nest. Its fins and bones are prized in traditional medicine. In HeartGold and SoulSilver it lives in the Whirl Islands and on the Seafoam Islands' deepest floor.

anatomy.text: A water animal (Gen 4 shape blob), 1.2 m and 25.0 kg, typed Water: the Dragon Pokémon.
Its body bristles with sharp, poisonous spikes and barbs; its fin-tips leak poison, and touching the back fin causes numbness.
It swims backwards by rapidly flapping its wing-like pectoral fins and stout tail.
An examination of its cells found a gene not found in Horsea, which became a hot topic.

diet.text: It generates whirlpools by spinning its body, weakens prey with the currents, then swallows it whole.
Its prey isn't named. Swallowed whole by a 25 kg animal, it would be small: fish and small invertebrates are the likely food.
The whirlpools are strong enough to swallow even fishing boats.
Whirlpool isn't in its own list; Twister (Lv 26) and Brine (Lv 30) are its current-making and prey-finishing moves.

habitat.text: Coral reefs: it sleeps between coral branches, and coral harvesters get stung when they fail to notice it. The Gen 3 Pokédex habitat is sea.
In HeartGold and SoulSilver it lives in the Whirl Islands (Super Rod 10%; surf 10% on B2F) and on the Seafoam Islands' B4F (Super Rod 15%), at any time, in both versions.

behavior.text: It sleeps after wriggling itself between the branches of coral, hooking its tail to coral to stay in place.
It shows no mercy to anything approaching its nest.
Its activity pattern is not stated; the tables have it at any time.

social.text: The male raises the young; if approached, it fends off the intruder with its toxic spikes.
social.analogy: In real seahorses and pipefish, males brood the young.

social.text: Whether the female takes part, and how long the young stay, is not said.

reproduction.text: It keeps a nest, and the male raises the young there.
Water 1 and Dragon egg groups, 20 egg cycles, an even sex ratio, medium growth.

defense.text: Its spines provide protection; carelessly touching it can cause fainting from the spikes.
Poison Point, its ability, poisons what touches it.
Horsea flees and inks; Seadra stays and stings. The line's defence changes from escape to armament.

senses.text: Nothing is said about its senses.

life_cycle.text: It evolves from Horsea at level 32 and into Kingdra only by trade while holding a Dragon Scale, from 1.2 m and 25.0 kg to 1.8 m and 152.0 kg; Kingdra adds the Dragon type.
A gene not found in Horsea appears in Seadra's cells: the entries treat evolution as a change in the genes, not only the body.

moves_in_the_wild.text: Its list is Horsea's with later levels: Smokescreen, Water Gun, Focus Energy, Bubble Beam, Agility, Twister, Brine, Hydro Pump (Lv 40), Dragon Dance (Lv 48), Dragon Pulse (Lv 57).

ecology.text: A reef predator that swallows its prey whole, above Horsea in the web.
Its whirlpools would stir sediment and carry small animals; on the scale of fishing boats, they would reshape the water around a reef.
ecology.note: From the entry's scale only.

ecology.text: In Seafoam it shares the deepest floor with Seel, Dewgong, Krabby, Kingler, Horsea and Gyarados.

humans.text: Its fins and bones are highly valued as ingredients in traditional herbal medicine.
People harvesting coral are sometimes stung by its poison barbs when they fail to notice it.
Being prized for medicine is pressure from harvest, as the line's entries hint and as Lapras's decline from hunting shows for another sea animal.
humans.note: No entry says Seadra is declining.

homestead.text: Handle with care, or not at all: its spikes can make a person faint.
Never take fins or bones from a living Seadra; if the homestead ever needs the medicine, it should come from one that has died naturally.
A nesting male will defend its young without mercy: give a breeding pair its own water.
Its whirlpools could stir and aerate a large saltwater pool, if one were ever built.
homestead.note: Speculative.

niche.foraging: spins whirlpools to weaken prey in the current, then swallows it whole
niche.note: Prey never named; trophic level assumes small fish and invertebrates.

relationships.note: It swallows its prey whole; the prey is never named.
To sleep in and hook its tail to.

ecotypes.name: Murk guardian
ecotypes.reading: A lineage of nest fathers that fouls the water and stops an intruder's attack: muddy water and a move that disables a move. Fits silty sea-cave floors where nests are hard to see.
ecotypes.behavior: Clouds the water around its nest when anything comes near.

ecotypes.name: Storm-drake
ecotypes.reading: The line's dragon-leaning lineage at its spiny stage: the Seadra most likely to become a Kingdra that wakes with storms. Fits stormy, current-swept water.
ecotypes.behavior: Most active when the sea is rough.

open_questions: What prey does it swallow whole?
Does the male raise the young alone? For how long?
What is the gene found in Seadra but not Horsea (117.3)?
Are wild Seadra harvested for medicine in Johto, and does it threaten them?

Seaking.summary: The adult of the Goldeen line, a horned river fish whose life centres on its nest. In autumn Seaking gather from all over to spawn, turning the rivers red; the male bores a hole in a riverbed boulder with his drill-like horn, and the pair take turns guarding the eggs for over a month. It defends its eggs with its life. In the highlands it is a rare Super Rod catch in Dark Cave's water, where there are no riverbed boulders to nest in.

anatomy.text: A fish, 1.3 m and 39.0 kg, typed Water.
The horn on its head is sharp like a drill.
In autumn its body becomes fattier and its colours are at their most beautiful, before it courts a mate.

diet.text: No entry says what Seaking eats.
It fattens before the autumn courtship, so it must feed heavily in the months before spawning.
Its level-up moves start with Poison Jab and Peck (Lv 1); like Goldeen's, they are strikes that might double as feeding, but nothing says so.
diet.note: A reading of moves only.

habitat.text: Rivers, creeks and stream beds; it lives in hollowed rocks in streams.

In the highlands in HeartGold and SoulSilver it is only in Dark Cave's water, both ends, by Super Rod 10% (Lv 40). It is widespread elsewhere: Union Cave, Slowpoke Well, Route 42, Mt. Mortar (also surfing 10%), Tohjo Falls, the Kanto routes and the Johto Safari Zone, and it is the main surfing encounter on Mt. Silver (about 90%). The Gen 3 Pokédex habitat is waters-edge.
A boulder-nesting river fish recorded in a cave pool: Dark Cave Seaking presumably feed there and spawn somewhere with current and boulders.
habitat.note: Nothing records where Dark Cave's fish breed.

behavior.text: In the autumn spawning season they swim powerfully up rivers and creeks.
Males perform courtship dances in riverbeds to woo females.
Males patrol the area around their nests in autumn to protect their offspring.

social.text: During spawning season Seaking gather from all over, colouring the rivers a brilliant red.
social.analogy: Sockeye salmon (Oncorhynchus nerka) turn bright red at spawning, and their mass runs colour whole rivers.

social.text: The male and female take turns patrolling around their nest and eggs.

reproduction.text: The male makes the nest by carving out a boulder in the stream with his horn.
reproduction.analogy: Male three-spined sticklebacks (Gasterosteus aculeatus) build the nest, take on red breeding colours and guard the eggs and young.

reproduction.text: The hole stops the eggs from washing away in the current or being attacked.
It is very protective: the guarding of eggs goes on for over a month, and it defends them with its life.
Water 2 egg group, 20 egg cycles, even sex ratio; the line's egg moves sit on Goldeen.

defense.text: To protect its family it will fight with its drill-sharp horn.
Swift Swim and Water Veil, as Goldeen; Agility (Lv 56) and Aqua Ring (Lv 27).

senses.text: Nothing is said about its senses.

life_cycle.text: It evolves from Goldeen at Lv 33.
Both stages are described spawning, Goldeen in schools running upstream and Seaking at nests, so the line may breed before it reaches full size.

moves_in_the_wild.text: Horn Drill (Lv 47) is the nest-borer in game form; Horn Attack, Fury Attack and Megahorn (Lv 63) are the horn as a weapon. Waterfall (Lv 40) is a natural move, matching the runs upstream.

ecology.text: An engineer: it bores holes in riverbed boulders, and empty nest holes would shelter other small stream animals.
ecology.note: The boring is canon; later use of the holes by others is not recorded.

ecology.text: A mass autumn gathering of large fish is a seasonal food pulse for predators; none is recorded in the highlands.
ecology.note: Untested.

ecology.text: Its diet, and so its trophic level, is unknown.

humans.text: Its autumn spawning is a spectacle: rivers turn a brilliant red.
Anyone working a stream in autumn should leave nest boulders alone: the guarding parent will fight.

homestead.text: To breed it needs a real stream with boulders; a pond will not do.
Expect it to be aggressive near its nest for over a month each autumn; keep people and stock out of that stretch of stream.
Its horn bores holes in stone; whether it would do so anywhere but at a nest is unknown.
homestead.note: Untested.

homestead.text: A pair of Seaking in the homestead's stream, with the autumn red run as the household's marker of the year turning.

niche.foraging: unknown; nothing records what it eats

relationships.note: Nest sites, bored with the horn.
Empty nest holes as shelter; not recorded.
Dark Cave water.

ecotypes.name: Torrent spawner
ecotypes.reading: Two powerful water attacks in a lineage built for the autumn run up steep, fast streams. Fits highland streams with falls, where the strongest swimmers reach the best nest boulders.
ecotypes.behavior: Nests highest up the stream.

ecotypes.name: Silt nester
ecotypes.reading: Mud moves in a lineage that nests where boulders are scarce, digging into silt and gravel instead of boring rock. Fits slow, muddy reaches and cave pools such as Dark Cave's.
ecotypes.behavior: Digs a hollow rather than drilling one.

ecotypes.name: Heavy guardian
ecotypes.reading: Weight and a tail strike in a nest-guarding lineage that drives intruders off by force. Fits crowded spawning reaches where many pairs nest close together, as when Seaking gather from all over.
ecotypes.behavior: Guards longer and fights harder at the nest.

open_questions: What does Seaking eat, especially to fatten in autumn (119.13)?
Where do Dark Cave's Seaking spawn? A cave pool has no riverbed boulders.
Which season: spring for Goldeen (118.8), autumn for Seaking?
Who guards: the males (119.5) or both parents in turn (119.7)?
What uses the bored nest holes after the young leave?
What eats Seaking or its eggs? Nothing is recorded.

contradictions.text: Crystal says the males patrol the nests in autumn; Sapphire says the male and female take turns patrolling.
contradictions.reading: Male-only versus shared guarding. Possibly both happen; not resolved here.

contradictions.text: Emerald puts Goldeen's spawning runs in spring; the Seaking entries put spawning in autumn.
contradictions.reading: The two stages may spawn in different seasons, or the entries disagree.

Seel.summary: A white-and-blue sea lion of frigid, ice-covered seas. Seel loves the cold, relishing water around -10 °C and staying active at -40 °F, and wears light blue fur and a thick, tough hide against it. It hunts prey under sheets of ice and, when it needs to breathe, punches a hole through the ice with the hard, sharply protruding horn on its head. Clumsy on land, it is a graceful swimmer; by day it is often found asleep on the seabed in shallow water, nostrils closed.
