In HeartGold and SoulSilver it is the commonest animal of the Seafoam Islands, and lives in the Whirl Islands and off Route 47 too.

anatomy.text: A sea-lion body (Gen 4 shape fish), 1.1 m and 90.0 kg, typed Water: the Sea Lion Pokémon.
The protruding horn on its head is very hard, used for bashing through thick ice or icebergs.
Light blue fur covers it and keeps it protected against the cold; its hide is thick and tough.
Its nostrils close while it swims.
anatomy.analogy: Seals close their nostrils when they dive, too.

anatomy.text: Thick Fat, one of its abilities, resists fire and ice: a blubber layer in game terms.

diet.text: It hunts for prey in the frigid sea underneath sheets of ice.
The prey is never named; a 90 kg sea lion hunting under ice would most likely take fish and invertebrates.
diet.analogy: Ringed seals hunt fish and crustaceans under sea ice and keep breathing holes open with their claws.

diet.text: Lick, Stockpile, Spit Up and Swallow are egg moves of the line: some lineages may store and swallow food in bulk.

habitat.text: Frigid, iceberg-filled seas; it lives on icebergs. The Gen 3 Pokédex habitat is sea.
In HeartGold and SoulSilver it lives in the Seafoam Islands (60%: walking and surfing, Lv 30-40), the Whirl Islands (15%) and off Route 47 (surf 30%), at any time, in both versions.
The games have no iceberg seas in Johto or Kanto; Seel's places are sea caves, the coldest, most sheltered water the regions have.

behavior.text: In the daytime it is often found asleep on the seabed in shallow waters.
It relishes swimming in a frigid climate of around 14 °F and is active in a bitter cold of -40 °F.
Although it can't walk well on land, it is a graceful swimmer.
Asleep by day suggests it hunts at night, as Dewgong does (87.5).

social.text: Nothing is said about groups or colonies.

reproduction.text: Water 1 and Field egg groups, 20 egg cycles, an even sex ratio, medium growth. Nothing describes pups.

defense.text: Nothing in its entries describes defence; a thick hide and the cold it can bear are its protection.
Rest (Lv 21) and Aqua Ring (Lv 23) are its recovery; Safeguard (Lv 51) protects against status.

senses.text: Nothing is said about its senses. Finding prey under ice, and the way back to its breathing hole, implies good underwater senses.

life_cycle.text: It becomes Dewgong at level 34, from 1.1 m and 90.0 kg to 1.7 m and 120.0 kg, gaining the Ice type.
Read as development, light blue fur becomes Dewgong's pure white coat, which hides it in snow (87.10).

moves_in_the_wild.text: Headbutt at level 1, the ice-breaking horn; then Growl, Water Sport, Icy Wind, Encore, Ice Shard, Rest, Aqua Ring, Aurora Beam, Aqua Jet, Brine, Take Down, Dive, Aqua Tail, Ice Beam and Safeguard.

ecology.text: A cold-water predator, likely of fish and invertebrates, in the sea-cave webs.
By punching breathing holes in ice, it would open the water to other air-breathers in a frozen sea.
ecology.note: From the habit only.

ecology.text: In Seafoam it shares the caves with Dewgong, Horsea, Seadra, Krabby, Kingler, Slowbro, Jynx and Gyarados.

humans.text: Nothing is said about Seel and people.

homestead.text: A cold-water worker for the highland lakes in winter: it breaks ice with its head.
It loves bitter cold and swims in it: a companion for the Blackthorn winter.
Poor on land: give it water to live in, not a pen.
Seel keeping a hole open in the lake ice below Blackthorn all winter, for itself and anyone fishing.

niche.foraging: hunts prey under ice, punching breathing holes with its head
niche.note: Prey never named. Night activity read from its sleeping on the seabed by day (86.4).

relationships.note: Its prey is never named.
Lives on icebergs and breathes through holes it punches.

ecotypes.name: Ice-hole driller
ecotypes.reading: A lineage that is all horn: a drilling horn, icicle spears and a body slam. The Seel that keeps breathing holes open through the thickest ice. Fits seas that freeze over.
ecotypes.behavior: Breaks more ice than others; a hole-keeper for its neighbours.

ecotypes.name: Hoarding diver
ecotypes.reading: A lineage that eats big and stores it: three moves of storing and swallowing. A Seel that gorges on rare good hunts in cold water where food comes and goes. Fits ice seas with long lean spells.
ecotypes.behavior: Feeds heavily, then sleeps on the seabed for days.

open_questions: What does Seel hunt under the ice?
Is it nocturnal, given it sleeps on the seabed by day?
Does it live in colonies?
Johto and Kanto have no iceberg seas: is Seafoam cold enough for it?

Shellder.summary: A small bivalve in a two-piece shell harder than diamond, tender inside, with a large tongue it always keeps hanging out. Shellder swims backward, surprisingly fast, by opening and closing its shell; at night it burrows a hole in the seafloor sand with its broad tongue and sleeps in it, shell shut and tongue out. Sand caught in its shell becomes beautiful pearls. It is the Shellder that bites a Slowpoke's tail or head that makes Slowbro and Slowking, and that Shellder is said to feed on the host's leftover scraps and on the tasty flavour oozing from its tail. In HeartGold and SoulSilver it is hooked on the good and super rods along both regions' coasts, beside Chinchou.

anatomy.text: A small shelled animal (Gen 4 shape ball), 0.3 m and 4.0 kg, typed Water: the Bivalve Pokémon.
A two-piece shell, harder than diamond, that repels any kind of attack; inside, it is surprisingly tender.
A large, broad tongue, always kept hanging out.

diet.text: No entry of its own says what Shellder eats.
The Shellder latched onto a Slowpoke's tail is said to feed on the host's leftover scraps, and won't let go because of the tasty flavour that oozes out of the tail (Slowbro's entries).
diet.note: 'Said to': hearsay in the entries themselves, and only of an attached Shellder.

diet.text: Free-living, a small bivalve on sandy sea floors most likely eats small particles and scraps it can reach with its tongue; nothing says so.
diet.analogy: Real clams and scallops filter food particles from the water through their shells' gape.

habitat.text: The sea floor, where it burrows in the sand at night; the Gen 3 Pokédex habitat is sea.

In HeartGold and SoulSilver it is hooked on the good and super rods (Lv 20-40) at New Bark Town, Sea Route 41 and Route 47 in Johto, and Routes 26 and 27, Pallet Town, Vermilion City, Cinnabar Island and Sea Routes 20 and 21 in Kanto, at any time, in both versions.
Some live on Slowpoke instead: on the tail of a Slowbro, on the head of a Slowking.

behavior.text: It swims facing backward by opening and closing its two-piece shell, and is surprisingly fast.
behavior.analogy: Real scallops swim by clapping their two shells together, jetting water out.

behavior.text: At night it uses its broad tongue to burrow a hole in the seafloor sand and sleeps in it, shell closed and tongue hanging out.
Active by day and asleep in the sand at night, by those entries; the rods hook it at any time.

social.text: Nothing is said about Shellder living with other Shellder.
Its one recorded partnership is with Slowpoke: it bites a Slowpoke's tail and holds on, making Slowbro; on a Slowpoke's head, Slowking.

reproduction.text: Water 3 egg group, 20 egg cycles, an even sex ratio, slow growth. Nothing describes how it breeds.

defense.text: Its hard shell can withstand any attack; it is vulnerable only when the shell is open and the tender body exposed.
Clamping on to an opponent reveals its vulnerable parts, so it uses that only as a last resort.
Withdraw (Lv 4), Protect (Lv 16), Iron Defense (Lv 40) and Shell Armor: shutting in, in game form. Clamp (Lv 25) is the last-resort bite.

senses.text: Nothing is said about its senses. Its tongue, always out, is the obvious organ to taste and feel with; the entries don't say it is.

life_cycle.text: It becomes Cloyster with a Water Stone: from 0.3 m and 4.0 kg to 1.5 m and 132.5 kg.
Cloyster that live in seas with harsh tidal currents grow large, sharp spikes on their shells (91.4): the adult's form depends on where it lives.
Grains of sand trapped in its shells mix with its body fluids to form beautiful pearls.
life_cycle.analogy: Real oysters coat an irritant with nacre to make a pearl.

moves_in_the_wild.text: Tackle, Withdraw, Supersonic, Icicle Spear, Protect, Leer, Clamp, Ice Shard, Aurora Beam, Whirlpool, Iron Defense, Brine and Ice Beam. Skill Link makes its multi-strike moves land in full.

ecology.text: A small bottom-dweller of sandy sea floors, and, attached to Slowpoke, a partner whose bite turns its host into a different animal.
With Slowbro, Shellder gets food (scraps and the tail's ooze) and the Slowbro gets a poison that numbs pain (80.4); whether that is mutualism or parasitism is open.
Where the rods hook it, it shares the water with Chinchou, Lanturn, Tentacool and Tentacruel.

humans.text: Its pearls are beautiful.
Nothing says people collect them; the pearls a Shellder makes would be worth something to people who do.

homestead.text: Not a highland animal: a sea-floor bivalve. Met only on coastal trips.
Keep fingers away from an open shell: Clamp is its last resort, and it holds on.
A Shellder in a bucket of seawater on the kitchen table, tongue out, and the pearl someone hopes is in it.

microhabitat: on a Slowpoke's tail or head
niche.foraging: unknown when free; attached to Slowpoke, said to eat the host's leftover scraps and the tail's ooze
niche.note: Filed as a scavenger from the Slowbro entries; the machine reading's grazer comes from its Water type alone. Diurnal from 90.6 (sleeps at night).

relationships.with: leftover food remains of its Slowpoke host
relationships.note: Said of the Shellder on a Slowbro's tail.
It lives on the tail and eats the scraps; the host's gain (numbed pain, 80.4) or loss (no fishing tail, 80.6) is open.

ecotypes.name: Sand-burrower
ecotypes.reading: A lineage of soft bottoms: it throws up mud, spins itself into the sand and shuts in. The night burrower of 90.6. Fits sandy and silty sea floors.
ecotypes.behavior: Digs in at dusk and barely shows by day.

ecotypes.name: Spike-volley
ecotypes.reading: A lineage of rough water: volleys of spikes and stones, and a charge. Cloyster in seas with harsh tidal currents grow large, sharp spikes (91.4); these are the Shellder that become them. Fits rocky coasts with strong tides.
ecotypes.behavior: Fires back from inside its shell rather than clamping.

open_questions: What does a free-living Shellder eat?
How does a Shellder choose a Slowpoke, and does the Slowpoke ever choose it?
Does a Shellder that comes off a Slowbro (80.2) go back to the sea floor?
Do Shellder that become Cloyster in rough seas differ before they evolve?

folklore.text: The Shellder on a Slowpoke's tail is said to feed on the host's leftover scraps.

Skarmory.summary: An armoured bird with a body and wings of steel. Its sturdy wings look heavy but its bones are hollow and light, and it flies at over 180 mph, slashing foes with wings that have sword-like cutting edges. It nests in bramble bushes, and its chicks' wings grow hard from the scratches of the thorns. Its wings are battered by battles and grow back completely once a year. The feathers it sheds are very sharp: people in the past made swords and knives from them. In SoulSilver it lives on Route 45, the mountain road below Blackthorn, rarely; in HeartGold, Gligar has its place.

anatomy.text: A winged bird (Gen 4 shape wings), 1.7 m and 50.5 kg, typed Steel and Flying: the Armor Bird Pokémon.
A body and wings of steel, entirely encased in hard, protective armour.
Its wings look heavy, but its bones are hollow and light, allowing it to fly freely.
anatomy.analogy: Real birds have hollow, air-filled bones that keep them light.

anatomy.text: Its wings have sword-like cutting edges; the feathers it sheds are very sharp.

diet.text: No entry says what Skarmory eats.
The machine reading's metal-eater comes from its Steel type alone; nothing supports it.
Peck, Fury Attack (Lv 17) and Slash: a bird that strikes with beak and blade, but not said to hunt.

habitat.text: It nests in bramble bushes; the Gen 3 Pokédex habitat is rough terrain.
In SoulSilver it lives on Route 45 (5%, Lv 27), at any time; it is not wild in HeartGold, where Gligar has that place in the table.

behavior.text: It flies at close to 190 mph, over 180 mph by another entry, despite its armour.
Its activity pattern is not stated; the table has it at any time.

social.text: Nothing is said about Skarmory living together. It raises chicks in a nest.

reproduction.text: It nests in bramble bushes, and raises chicks there; the thorns' scratches harden their wings.
Flying egg group, 25 egg cycles, an even sex ratio, slow growth.
Choosing a thorny nest site keeps predators from the chicks as well as hardening them.
reproduction.analogy: Real shrikes and many small birds nest in thorn bushes for protection.

defense.text: Its armour, and wings that cut like swords.
Keen Eye keeps its aim true and Sturdy guards against one-hit knockouts; Spikes (Lv 28) and Metal Sound (Lv 31) are its defences.

senses.text: Nothing is said about its senses. Keen Eye, its ability, is a game reading of sharp sight.

life_cycle.text: It does not evolve: 1.7 m and 50.5 kg as an adult.
Its steel wings become tattered and bashed in from repeated battles; once a year the battered wings grow back completely, restoring their edges.
life_cycle.analogy: Real birds moult and regrow their flight feathers about once a year.

moves_in_the_wild.text: Leer, Peck, Sand Attack, Swift, Agility, Fury Attack, Feint, Air Cutter, Spikes, Metal Sound, Steel Wing, Air Slash, Slash and Night Slash: blades of air and steel.

ecology.text: Its diet is unknown, so its place in the web is unset.
It sheds sharp feathers once a year: steel left on the ground where it lives.
On Route 45 it shares the slopes with Geodude, Graveler, Teddiursa, Spearow and the Aipom and Heracross of the trees.

humans.text: People in the past used feathers fallen from Skarmory to make swords and knives.
It is said that people once used the feathers as swords.

homestead.text: Collect its fallen feathers after the yearly moult: blades for knives and tools, as people once did.
Never let children near the bramble nests: the chicks, the parents and the feathers all cut.
Fast and armoured, in principle a scout and a messenger over the mountain.
The steel feather found under the brambles above Route 45, kept on the mantel and used to cut bread.

niche.foraging: unknown
niche.note: Guild left empty: the machine reading's lithovore comes from the Steel type alone.

relationships.note: Its nest sites.

ecotypes.name: Bramble guardian
ecotypes.reading: A lineage that holds the nest: it blows intruders away, hardens itself and trades defences. Fits thorny scrub where the nests are.
ecotypes.behavior: Stays near the brambles and drives off what comes close.

ecotypes.name: High-speed diver
ecotypes.reading: A lineage of the 180 mph flier (227.8): full-body dives and drilling strikes. Fits open high country with room to dive.
ecotypes.behavior: Strikes from a long, fast dive.

open_questions: What does Skarmory eat?
Do Skarmory pairs raise chicks together?
Does it fight Gligar or Fearow for the cliffs of Route 45?
Why is it in SoulSilver's wild and not HeartGold's?

folklore.text: It is said that people once used its feathers as swords.

Slowbro.summary: A Slowpoke with a Shellder clamped on its tail, and the Pokédex's clearest case of two species making one animal. A Slowpoke went hunting in the sea, a Shellder bit its tail, and it became Slowbro. The Shellder won't let go because of the tasty flavour oozing from the tail, and is said to feed on Slowbro's leftover scraps; its seeping poison has left Slowbro unable to feel pain. With the tail no longer usable for fishing, Slowbro has to swim and catch its prey instead. If the Shellder is thrown off, it becomes an ordinary Slowpoke again. In HeartGold and SoulSilver it lives in Slowpoke Well and the Seafoam Islands.

anatomy.text: An upright animal (Gen 4 shape upright), 1.6 m and 78.5 kg, typed Water and Psychic: the Hermit Crab Pokémon.
Its tail has a Shellder firmly attached with a bite.
If the Shellder on its tail comes off, or is thrown off in a harsh battle, it becomes an ordinary Slowpoke again.

diet.text: With the Shellder on its tail, the tail can't be used for fishing any more, so Slowbro grudgingly swims and catches prey instead.
Its prey isn't named; Slowpoke fish with their tails in the line's entries, so fish are the likely food.
The Shellder feeds on Slowbro's leftover scraps, it is said, and on the tasty flavour that oozes out of its tail.

habitat.text: It lives lazily by the sea; the Gen 3 Pokédex habitat is waters-edge.
In HeartGold and SoulSilver it lives in Slowpoke Well (surf 10%) and the Seafoam Islands (surf 10%, Lv 35-50), at any time, in both versions.
Slowpoke Well, a flooded well, and Seafoam, a sea cave, are both sheltered water.

behavior.text: It lives lazily and is naturally dull, usually dim-witted, but it seems to become inspired when the Shellder on its tail bites down.
It swims and catches prey only grudgingly, reluctantly.
Its activity pattern is not stated.

social.text: Its one partnership is with the Shellder on its tail.

Read as symbiosis, Shellder gets food (scraps and the tail's tasty ooze) and Slowbro gets a poison that numbs pain and a bite that sharpens it, and loses its fishing tail. Whether that nets out as mutualism or parasitism is open.

reproduction.text: Monster and Water 1 egg groups, 20 egg cycles, an even sex ratio, medium growth. Its eggs hatch as Slowpoke.

defense.text: It lost its ability to feel pain because of Shellder's seeping poison.
Withdraw (Lv 37, learned on evolving) is the Shellder's shell; Own Tempo keeps it from confusion and Oblivious from infatuation.

senses.text: It can't feel pain, because of the Shellder's poison.

life_cycle.text: When a Slowpoke went hunting in the sea, its tail was bitten by a Shellder, and that made it evolve into Slowbro.
In the games Slowpoke becomes Slowbro at level 37: the bite isn't modelled.
An evolution that reverses when the partner falls off is unique in the entries: Slowbro is a state, not a stage.

moves_in_the_wild.text: Curse, Yawn, Tackle, Growl, Water Gun, Confusion, Disable, Headbutt, Water Pulse, Zen Headbutt, Withdraw, Slack Off, Amnesia, Psychic, Rain Dance and Psych Up: a slow, psychic list, with Yawn and Slack Off for the laziness.

ecology.text: A reluctant predator of fish, and a host: it carries a Shellder that eats its scraps.
In Seafoam it shares the water with Seel, Dewgong, Horsea, Krabby and Gyarados.

humans.text: Nothing is said about Slowbro and people.

homestead.text: A calm, slow companion that feels no pain: gentle with children, hard to hurt.
Don't pull the Shellder off: it would become a Slowpoke again.
It needs water to swim and fish in, and it won't hurry.
The homestead's Slowbro, who has never once noticed that it is standing on your foot.

microhabitat: sheltered water by the sea (Seafoam, Slowpoke Well)
niche.foraging: swims and catches prey, grudgingly, since its tail can no longer fish
niche.note: 'Prey' is never named; fish read from the line's fishing habit.

relationships.note: Its prey, read as fish.
The Shellder on its tail; it eats Slowbro's scraps (said) and the tail's ooze.

ecotypes.name: Foresight sleeper
ecotypes.reading: A lineage that sleeps a great deal and acts ahead: foresight and two moves used in sleep. The laziest Slowbro, and perhaps the most inspired when the Shellder bites. Fits quiet, sheltered pools.
ecotypes.behavior: Dozes by the water; strikes before it is attacked.

ecotypes.name: Mud-sport basker
ecotypes.reading: A heavier, earthier lineage: wallowing in mud, a drum-belly display and a stamp. A Slowbro of muddy shores rather than clear caves.
ecotypes.behavior: Wallows on mudflats at low tide.

open_questions: Is the Shellder a parasite or a partner? It feeds on Slowbro's scraps and tail ooze; Slowbro loses pain and its fishing tail.
Does the Shellder ever let go on its own?
What does Slowbro catch when it swims?
How does a bite cause an evolution (80.8), when the games use level 37?

folklore.text: The Shellder that is latched onto Slowpoke's tail is said to feed on the host's leftover scraps.

Snorlax.summary: A 460 kg animal whose whole life is eating and sleeping. Snorlax is not satisfied until it has eaten roughly 400 kg of food a day, eats anything, moldy or rotten, off the ground if need be, and has a stomach that dissolves any poison; when it has eaten its fill it goes straight to sleep. It is so docile that children play on its belly, and Platinum notes that a full Snorlax is too lethargic to lift a finger. Its young, Munchlax, swallow their own weight in food every day and hide food under their long fur, then forget it is there.

anatomy.text: A huge, upright, round-bellied animal (2.1 m, 460.0 kg); its bulk builds as it eats.
Its stomach is the remarkable organ: its digestive juices dissolve any kind of poison, and moldy or rotten food doesn't upset it.
Its abilities match: Immunity (it can't be poisoned) and Thick Fat (resistant to fire and ice).
Munchlax (0.6 m, 105.0 kg) has long body hair under which it hides food.

diet.text: A generalist that eats anything, including moldy and rotten food and things off the ground.
It needs over 880 pounds (about 400 kg) a day, nearly its own body weight, and doesn't feel full until it has eaten nearly 900 pounds.
diet.analogy: Real large mammals eat a few percent of their body weight a day; an African elephant eats on the order of 150 kg for a body of several tonnes.

diet.text: Munchlax swallows its own weight in food once a day, whole and almost unchewed.
Snorlax stops eating only to sleep.

habitat.text: Its Gen 3 Pokédex habitat is mountain; no entry describes where it lives.

In every Gen I-IV game the wild Snorlax are single, sleeping animals blocking a route, woken with the Poké Flute: Route 11 in HeartGold and SoulSilver (with a second on Route 12 under a later story condition), Vermilion City in Gold, Silver and Crystal, and Routes 12 and 16 in Kanto's games.
Munchlax is found only on Honey-slathered trees in Sinnoh, and only in one of the honey-tree encounter groups.

behavior.text: Its typical day is eating and sleeping and nothing else; when it has finished eating it goes promptly to sleep.
It gets steadily lazier as it gets fatter.
What sounds like its cry may be its snoring or its hungry belly rumbling.
Munchlax gulps food so desperately that it forgets the food it has hidden in its fur.
No activity pattern is given; the encounter data show it asleep whenever it is found.

social.text: Docile toward people: children use its belly as a place to play.
Nothing is said about how it treats its own kind; every wild Snorlax in the games is alone.

reproduction.text: Monster egg group, 40 egg cycles (twice the usual), slow growth, and 87.5% male, a ratio most species outside the starters don't have. Munchlax is a baby Pokémon in the Undiscovered group and can't breed.

defense.text: Bulk and indifference: little is described as threatening it, and it is too lethargic to react when full.
Poison doesn't work on it: its stomach dissolves any kind, and Immunity stops poisoning in battle.
Its own moves suit an animal that sits tight: Defense Curl, Amnesia, Rest, and Block (Lv 36), which stops an opponent leaving.

senses.text: Satiety is its one described sense: it doesn't feel full until it has eaten nearly 900 pounds.
Munchlax has Odor Sleuth at Lv 1, which fits an animal that finds food by smell, though no entry says so.

life_cycle.text: Munchlax (0.6 m, 105.0 kg) becomes Snorlax (2.1 m, 460.0 kg) when it levels up with high friendship. The archive lists the line as Snorlax, Munchlax, but Munchlax is the first stage.
The young eat their weight daily and store food in their fur; the adult eats almost its weight daily and stores it as bulk. Hoarding gives way to sleeping it off.
Munchlax's own moves include Stockpile and Swallow (Lv 25 and 28), storing and then swallowing, which matches the hidden food stash; Recycle (Lv 17) re-uses an item already used.

moves_in_the_wild.text: Its level-up list is the canon in move form: Rest (Lv 25), then Snore and Sleep Talk (Lv 28), both used while asleep; Yawn (Lv 20) makes others drowsy.
Belly Drum (Lv 17) sacrifices half its health to raise its attack to the maximum, and Body Slam (Lv 33) and Giga Impact (Lv 49) use its mass.
Lick (Lv 12) is its own, and an egg move too.
Strength and Rock Smash, behind its hauling and clearing records, are machine moves.

ecology.text: An enormous consumer: at roughly 400 kg a day, one Snorlax would strip a local food supply quickly, which may be why each is found alone.
Because it eats moldy and rotten food, it also acts as a scavenger of spoiled material others won't touch.
Munchlax's forgotten food stashes could scatter seeds if food falls out of its fur unchewed.
ecology.note: Nothing says the food falls out or contains seeds.
ecology.analogy: Scatter-hoarders such as Eurasian jays (Garrulus glandarius) plant oaks by failing to recover the acorns they bury.

ecology.text: Trophic level about 2.5: whatever is available, plant or animal, fresh or spoiled.

humans.text: Safe with children: docile enough to be played on, and safe to bounce on when full.
An obstacle: in every Gen I-IV game a sleeping Snorlax blocks a road until someone plays the Poké Flute.

homestead.text: The cost: roughly 400 kg of food a day. No homestead can feed a Snorlax casually; plan the supply before it arrives.
Part of that can be waste: it eats moldy and rotten food without harm, so spoiled stores, kitchen scraps and windfall fruit can go to it.
Hauling: 460 kg of animal with hands; the capability record lists a harness. Strength is taught, and its laziness is the real limit.
A calm, safe animal around children, provided it is fed: the safety note in the Pokédex is about a full belly.
Munchlax will raid stores and carry food off in its fur; lock the kitchen and the berry store. Its Pickup ability also turns up items.
Where it sleeps, it stays: don't let it settle across a path or a gate. The games' Snorlax all block roads.

microhabitat: open routes and paths where it sleeps
niche.foraging: eats anything available in huge quantity, fresh or spoiled, then sleeps; the young hoard food in their fur

relationships.with: any available food, including spoiled food

relationships.note: Children play on its belly; Snorlax is unaffected.

ecotypes.name: Pass sleeper
ecotypes.reading: A lineage that cannot be moved: Curse makes it slower, stronger and tougher, and Counter returns physical blows double. The sleeping-roadblock habit as a whole strategy. Fits narrow mountain passes, its listed habitat, where lying across the way keeps a feeding area to itself.
ecotypes.behavior: Settles in one spot and won't shift; strikes back only when struck.

ecotypes.name: Charming beggar
ecotypes.reading: A lineage that gets fed: Charm sharply lowers an opponent's attack by being endearing, Lick can paralyse at close range. Together they suit an animal that lives off what others provide rather than foraging. Fits village and farm edges, where children already play on Snorlax.
ecotypes.behavior: Approaches people and waits to be fed; hard to stay angry at.

ecotypes.name: Larder guard
ecotypes.reading: A lineage that defends its food: Whirlwind blows rivals away from a feeding patch, and Pursuit hits harder at anything that runs off. For an animal that needs 400 kg a day, keeping competitors off is worth the effort. Fits contested feeding grounds such as berry thickets in a lean season.
ecotypes.behavior: Clears a food patch before eating; chases thieves.

open_questions: How can any animal eat nearly its own weight daily? Where does the mass go?
What do wild Snorlax mostly eat in practice?
Do they ever live together, or does food demand keep them solitary?
Why is Snorlax 87.5% male, like a starter line?
Does Munchlax ever eat its forgotten stash (446.4 says it does; 446.2 and 446.3 say it forgets)?
Is a hungry Snorlax still safe around children, or only a full one (143.11)?

contradictions.text: Munchlax's hidden food: Pearl and Platinum say it forgets the food it hides under its fur; HeartGold and SoulSilver say it carts the stash around and swallows it.
Daily intake: FireRed says over 880 pounds; Pearl says nearly 900. Consistent in scale, but 'over' and 'nearly' bracket the figure from opposite sides.
contradictions.note: Minor.

Spearow.summary: A tiny, fierce bird of grassy places that eats bugs: it flaps its short wings to flush insects out of tall grass and plucks them with its stubby beak. Spearow is inept at flying high and must beat its short wings fast to stay up, but darts around at high speed to protect its territory, flying ceaselessly and crying. Its high, keening cry carries over half a mile, and when it echoes all around, the Spearow are warning each other of danger. In HeartGold and SoulSilver it is one of the commonest birds in both regions: in the grass by day on Routes 33, 42, 46, 22, 3, 4, 7, 9 and 10, and shaken from the trees by Headbutt along most of Johto's mountain roads and in Kanto's towns.

anatomy.text: A tiny bird (Gen 4 shape wings), 0.3 m and 2.0 kg, typed Normal and Flying: the Tiny Bird Pokémon.
Short wings that it must flap at high speed to stay airborne, and a stubby beak.

diet.text: It eats bugs in grassy areas: it flaps its short wings to flush out insects from tall grass, then plucks them with its stubby beak.
diet.analogy: Real cattle egrets and some small hawks hunt insects flushed from grass.

diet.text: Using its beak, it searches in grass for prey.
The machine reading's omnivore comes from 'grass' in 21.9, where the grass is where it looks, not what it eats. It is an insect-eater.

habitat.text: Grassy areas and tall grass; the Gen 3 Pokédex habitat is rough terrain.

In HeartGold and SoulSilver it is in the grass by day and morning on Routes 33, 42 and 46 in Johto and Routes 22, 3, 4, 7, 9 and 10 in Kanto, and in the trees (Headbutt) at any time on Routes 33, 42, 44, 45 and 46 and Azalea Town, and in Kanto at Vermilion, Celadon and Routes 7, 11 and 16; in both versions. It is on Route 47 too, rarely.

behavior.text: Inept at flying high; it flies around very fast instead, busily flitting here and there.
Very protective of its territory, it darts around at high speed and flies ceaselessly, making high-pitched cries.
Diurnal: the grass tables have it by day and morning only.

social.text: Its loud cry can be heard over half a mile away; if its high, keening cry is heard echoing all around, they are warning each other of danger.
Territorial, yet warning each other: Spearow hold territories near enough to hear one another, a loose community.
social.analogy: Real songbirds defend territories and still answer each other's alarm calls.

reproduction.text: Flying egg group, 15 egg cycles, an even sex ratio, medium growth. Nothing describes how it breeds.

defense.text: Speed and noise: it darts at high speed and cries.
Even if it is frail, it can be a tough foe that uses Mirror Move (Lv 21).
Keen Eye keeps its aim true; Leer and Pursuit (Lv 13) chase off and run down.

senses.text: It hears its own kind's cries over half a mile.
It finds insects by flushing them, then sees them to pluck them.

life_cycle.text: It becomes Fearow at level 20: from 0.3 m and 2.0 kg to 1.2 m and 38.0 kg, from a bird inept at flying high to one that can stay aloft all day (22.1, 22.8).
Its adult still eats small insects, plucking them from under the ground with its long beak (22.4).

moves_in_the_wild.text: Peck, Growl, Leer, Fury Attack, Pursuit, Aerial Ace, Mirror Move, Agility, Assurance, Roost and Drill Peck: a beak and speed.

ecology.text: A small insect-eating bird of grass and trees, one of the commonest in both regions.
Its alarm calls warn its own kind; other animals in the grass may hear them too, as real birds' alarms are heard.
Small (2 kg) and everywhere, it is prey-sized for the cliff gliders and hawks of the same roads; nothing names what eats it.
In the headbutt trees it lives with Aipom and Heracross in Johto, and Combee and Heracross in Kanto.

humans.text: Nothing is said about Spearow and people directly; its loud cries carry half a mile.

homestead.text: An insect-eater for the fields: it flushes and eats bugs in the grass.
An alarm: its keening cry, echoing all around, means danger.
Territorial and noisy: one pair is enough.
The Spearow on the gatepost that screams whenever the Gligar goes over.

niche.foraging: flushes insects from tall grass and plucks them
niche.note: The machine reading's omnivore comes from 'grass' in 21.9.

ecotypes.name: Alarm-caller
ecotypes.reading: A lineage of the cry: noise, a fierce face and a startle. The Spearow whose keening carries half a mile (21.6). Fits open grass where sound carries.
ecotypes.behavior: Cries at the first sign of danger, and keeps crying.

ecotypes.name: Grass-flusher
ecotypes.reading: A lineage of the hunt: a quick dart, a flurry of feathers, a wind that blows things out of cover. The insect-flusher of 21.3. Fits tall grass.
ecotypes.behavior: Beats the grass with its wings until something jumps.

open_questions: Which insects does Spearow eat: Bug-type Pokémon, small non-Pokémon insects, or both?
How big are Spearow territories?
Do other Pokémon heed its alarm calls?
What eats Spearow?

Spinarak.summary: A small green web-spinning spider and a sit-and-wait predator. Spinarak spins a web of fine but durable thread, then lies still in the same pose for days, waiting for unsuspecting prey to wander close; if prey gets caught, it waits motionless until dark. Its web is said to work as a second nervous system: through the tiny vibrations in the strands it can tell what kind of prey is touching it. In HeartGold and SoulSilver it is HeartGold's: walking at night on a few routes and in the headbutt trees of nearly every wooded place, Viridian Forest among them.

anatomy.text: A small spider-like bug (Gen 4 shape armor), 0.5 m and 8.5 kg, typed Bug and Poison: the String Spit Pokémon.
It spins a web using fine but durable thread, thin but strong silk.

diet.text: It sets a trap by spinning a web, then waits patiently, motionless, for prey to be trapped or to arrive.
It lies still in the same pose for days in its web, waiting for unsuspecting prey to wander close.
If prey becomes ensnared, it waits motionlessly until dark before taking it.
The prey is never named. A 0.5 m spider's web in trees and grass would mostly catch flying insects.
diet.analogy: Orb-weaving spiders catch mostly flying insects in their webs.

diet.text: Leech Life (Lv 12) is the drinking bite; Poison Sting the venom.

habitat.text: The Gen 3 Pokédex habitat is forest; its web is its nest ('its nest of spun string').

In HeartGold and SoulSilver it is HeartGold's: walking at night on Routes 30, 31 and 37, by morning and night on Route 2, and in the headbutt trees of nearly every wooded route and town in Johto and Kanto, Viridian Forest (10%) among them. SoulSilver has Ledyba in the same slots.

behavior.text: A sit-and-wait predator: still for days in the same pose.
Nocturnal in practice: it waits until dark to take what its web has caught, and the HeartGold tables have it walking at night.
Insomnia, one of its abilities, keeps it from falling asleep: a watcher that never dozes in game terms.

social.text: Nothing is said about Spinarak together; every entry is about a single spider on its web.

reproduction.text: Bug egg group, 15 egg cycles, an even sex ratio, fast growth. Nothing describes eggs or young.

defense.text: Nothing in its entries describes defence. Its moves include Scary Face (Lv 5), Constrict, Night Shade and Shadow Sneak, and as a Poison type its sting carries venom.

senses.text: The web can be considered its second nervous system.
It is said to tell what kind of prey is touching its web by the tiny vibrations it feels through the strands.
senses.analogy: Real web spiders read their prey's size and struggles from the vibrations in the threads.

life_cycle.text: It becomes Ariados at level 22, from 0.5 m and 8.5 kg to 1.1 m and 33.5 kg.
Read as development, a web-sitter becomes a wanderer: Ariados doesn't keep a nest in one spot but roams for food after dark (168.3).

moves_in_the_wild.text: Poison Sting, String Shot, Scary Face, Constrict, Leech Life, Night Shade, Shadow Sneak, Fury Swipes, Sucker Punch, Spider Web (Lv 29: the target can't flee), Agility, Pin Missile, Psychic and Poison Jab. String Shot and Spider Web are the web; Sucker Punch the ambush.

ecology.text: A small trap predator of trees and grass, eating whatever its web holds.
As HeartGold's night counterpart to SoulSilver's morning Ledyba, it fills the same tree and grass slots at the other end of the day.

humans.text: Nothing is said about Spinarak and people. Its silk is fine and durable, the kind of thread people value.

homestead.text: Insect control around barns and orchards, if it will web where it is wanted.
homestead.note: Its prey is unnamed.

homestead.text: Its silk is fine but durable: cord and thread, if it can be gathered from old webs.
homestead.note: Untested.

homestead.text: Leave its web alone for days; it waits motionless and shouldn't be disturbed.
A Spinarak web across the potting-shed door that tells it exactly who came in last night.

microhabitat: webs in trees and tall grass
niche.foraging: sit-and-wait in a web, reading prey by vibration; takes ensnared prey after dark
niche.note: Prey never named; trophic level assumes insects.

relationships.with: unnamed prey caught in its web

relationships.note: What a small web in trees would catch; never named.
To hang its web on.

ecotypes.name: Toxic-floor trapper
ecotypes.reading: A lineage that poisons the ground under its web as well as the web: venom spikes and a poison jab. Fits dense undergrowth where prey walks beneath the web.
ecotypes.behavior: Its web and the ground under it are both a trap.

ecotypes.name: Vibration hunter
ecotypes.reading: The 'second nervous system' as a lineage: a sound blast, a signal and a move that stops a move. A Spinarak that reads and jams its prey. Fits windless forest where the web's vibrations carry cleanly.
ecotypes.behavior: Strikes the instant the web tells it what has landed.

open_questions: What does Spinarak catch?
Why wait until dark to take ensnared prey (167.3)?
Why only in HeartGold, with Ledyba in its place in SoulSilver?
Can its silk be gathered without harming it?

folklore.text: It is said that it can determine what kind of prey is touching its web just by the tiny vibrations it feels through the strands.

Swampert.summary: Swampert is a 1.5 m, 82 kg amphibious Pokémon of shores and mud, and enormously strong: it can drag a boulder of more than a ton, swim as fast as a jet ski while towing a large ship, and break rock with a swing of its arms. It nests on beaches, and it hears a storm coming in the sound of the waves and the tidal winds, then piles up boulders to shield its nest. The line grows up in mud: Mudkip breathes through gills on its cheeks and senses water movement with the fin on its head, and Marshtomp must keep its skin wet by playing in mud. No Gen I–IV game has it in the wild; every Swampert comes from a Mudkip given to a trainer.

anatomy.text: An upright, tailed body of 1.5 m and 81.9 kg, Water and Ground type.
Its thick arms are as hard as rock and can break a boulder into pieces with one swing.
It has fins sensitive enough to pick up subtle differences in the sound of waves and tidal winds.
In Mudkip, gills on the cheeks let it breathe in water, a large tail fin drives it through water, and the fin on its head works as a sensitive detector of water and air movement.
anatomy.analogy: The axolotl (Ambystoma mexicanum) also carries external gills on the sides of its head.

anatomy.text: Marshtomp's body is covered by a thin, sticky film that lets it live on land, but it weakens if its skin dries out.
anatomy.analogy: Amphibians lose water quickly through their thin, mucus-covered skin and must keep it moist.

anatomy.text: Whether the adult keeps gills, or breathes air only, is not stated.

diet.text: No entry for any stage says what the line eats.
Seeing clearly in murky water would help a hunter or a forager of the bottom alike, so it doesn't settle the question.

habitat.text: Gen 3 Pokédex habitat for the whole line: the water's edge.
The adult is coastal: it makes its nest on beautiful beaches and guards a seaside nest against storms and tidal waves.
The juveniles live in mud and fresh water: Mudkip sleeps buried in soil at the water's edge or rests covered in mud at the bottom of a river, and Marshtomp plays in beach mud at low tide.

Not found in the wild in any Gen I–IV game. Mudkip is a starter gift on Route 101 in Ruby, Sapphire and Emerald, and in HeartGold and SoulSilver it is given in Saffron City after beating Red, to a player who received a Kanto starter.

behavior.text: It predicts storms: it senses subtle changes in the sound of waves and tidal winds and, if a storm or tidal wave is coming, piles up boulders to protect itself and its nest.
behavior.analogy: Young blacktip sharks have been recorded leaving shallow nursery waters ahead of a tropical storm, apparently in response to falling air pressure; the cue differs, the early warning is the same.

behavior.text: It swims as fast as a jet ski.
Marshtomp is much faster in mud than in water, burrows into dirt to sleep, and is at its best on muddy ground with poor footing.
Its activity pattern is unknown.

social.text: No entry describes groups, pairs or territory.

reproduction.text: It nests on beaches and defends the nest by building boulder walls before storms.
reproduction.analogy: Sea turtles also nest on sandy beaches above the tide line, where storm surges are the main threat to their nests.

reproduction.text: Monster and Water 1 egg groups, 20 egg cycles, 87.5% male; the sex ratio is shared with the other starter lines and is probably a game convention.
What is in the nest, how long it is tended and by which parent, is not described.

defense.text: It bashes down foes with one swing of its rock-hard arms.
Marshtomp fights on its own ground: it quickly overwhelms foes struggling in mud.
In a tight spot even Mudkip can crush rocks bigger than itself.
Torrent strengthens its Water moves when it is close to defeat, matching the juvenile's burst of strength in a pinch; Protect (Lv 46) is its guard.

senses.text: Powerful vision lets it see even in murky water.
Its fins pick up the sound of waves and tidal winds.
Mudkip relies on its head fin instead of its eyes, sensing water and air movement to tell what is happening around it; the adult adds strong eyesight.
senses.analogy: The lateral line of fishes and aquatic amphibians detects water movement and pressure changes in the same way.

life_cycle.text: Mudkip (0.4 m, 7.6 kg, four-legged) becomes Marshtomp at level 16 (0.7 m, 28 kg, upright, gaining the Ground type) and Swampert at level 36 (1.5 m, 81.9 kg).
Marshtomp's hindquarters are well developed, so it can walk on its hind legs; living on muddy ground with poor footing has made its legs sturdy.

Read as development, the line moves from a gilled, fin-sensing animal of rivers and mud, through an upright mud-dweller that must stay damp, to a powerful swimmer of the coast that sees well in murky water.
life_cycle.analogy: Broadly like amphibian development, from a gilled, water-bound larva to a more land-capable adult, though Swampert returns to open water.

life_cycle.text: Strength is there from the start: Mudkip lifts large boulders by planting its four feet and heaving, and has the strength to crush them.

moves_in_the_wild.text: Mud: Mud-Slap (Lv 6), Mud Shot (Lv 16), Mud Bomb (Lv 25) and Muddy Water (Lv 39), the move form of a life spent in mud.
Arms and ground: Hammer Arm (Lv 69) is the rock-hard swing of its entries, and Earthquake (Lv 52) suits an 82 kg Ground type.
Foresight (Lv 20) sees through evasion, consistent with an animal that perceives its surroundings well in murky conditions.
Surf, Waterfall, Strength, Dig and Rock Climb are machine moves taught by people.

ecology.text: A builder: it piles boulders into storm walls around its nest, changing the shape of the beach.
Those boulder walls would give shelter to other shore animals as well, during and after storms.
ecology.note: Nothing says what else uses them.

ecology.text: Its trophic position is unknown because its diet is never given.

humans.text: It can swim while towing a large ship.
It is strong enough to drag a boulder of more than a ton with ease.
In the games it reaches people only as a starter gift.

homestead.text: Storm warning: it hears a storm coming in the waves and wind. On a mountain lake rather than a coast, how far that sense still works is untested.
Heavy hauling: it drags boulders of more than a ton and tows ships.
Dry-stone walling: it already piles boulders into protective walls of its own accord, which is close to useful building work.
Rock clearing: one swing breaks a boulder into pieces.
Water crossings: it swims as fast as a jet ski, and Surf is a taught move.
Needs: water and a mud wallow, especially for young Marshtomp, which weaken if their skin dries; on cold, dry highland days the mud must not freeze solid.

niche.foraging: not described
niche.note: Diet is never stated for any stage, so no guild or trophic level is given.

relationships.note: Marshtomp keeps its skin wet in mud; the young sleep buried in it.
Nest sites.
Piled into walls before storms.

ecotypes.name: Mudflat brawler
ecotypes.reading: Mud Bomb blinds with a blob of mud, Stomp tramples, and Counter returns a blow twice as hard. A lineage that fights on the soft ground where its rivals flounder, Marshtomp's 'overwhelms foes struggling in mud' kept into adulthood. Fits wide tidal mudflats and estuaries.
ecotypes.behavior: Draws a foe onto the mud and fights it there.

ecotypes.name: Storm-wall mason
ecotypes.reading: Ancient Power lifts and hurls rock, Double-Edge is a full-weight ram, and Curse trades speed for toughness. A lineage given over to building and holding ground, moving stone and bracing against what comes. Fits exposed rocky coasts where storms hit hardest and the nest needs the strongest wall.
ecotypes.behavior: Builds higher walls than its neighbours and sits behind them.

ecotypes.name: Channel ambusher
ecotypes.reading: Whirlpool traps a target in a vortex, and Bite seizes it. A lineage that hunts in moving water, holding prey in the current and then taking it. Fits tidal channels and river mouths with strong flow.
ecotypes.behavior: Lurks where the current narrows and spins up a trap.

ecotypes.name: Cold-river sleeper
ecotypes.reading: Ice Ball rolls a growing ball of ice, and Yawn brings on drowsiness. Read together, a lineage of cold, slow water that spends long spells buried and torpid, as Mudkip already rests covered in mud on the river bottom. Fits icy highland streams such as those around Blackthorn.
ecotypes.behavior: Winters half-asleep in the mud of a cold river bed.

open_questions: What does the line eat?
Does the adult keep Mudkip's gills, and can it stay underwater indefinitely?
Is it a sea animal, a freshwater animal, or both at different ages? (see contradictions)
What does it hear when it predicts a storm, and would that work on a mountain lake?
What is in its beach nest, and who tends it?
Can Marshtomp survive a highland winter if its mud freezes?

contradictions.note: HeartGold, SoulSilver and Emerald put Mudkip in river mud and at the water's edge (258.6, 258.3); Emerald and FireRed put Swampert's nest on beaches facing tidal waves (260.3, 260.4), and Ruby has Marshtomp on beaches at low tide (259.1). It may move from rivers to the coast as it grows, but no entry says so.

Swinub.summary: A small pig of the Ice Path that finds food by smell and digs it up with a nose tough enough for frozen ground. Its favourite food is a mushroom that grows under dead grass, and it also eats berries, which makes it the highlands' clearest link to the fungi that break down dead plants. While rooting it sometimes uncovers hot springs, even under ice. It has the highest encounter rate on every floor of the Ice Path in HeartGold and SoulSilver, which says it is easy to meet, not how many there are.

anatomy.text: A small quadruped, 0.4 m and 6.5 kg, typed Ice and Ground.
The tip of its nose is its digging tool, so tough that even frozen ground poses no problem.
Its nose is also very sensitive.
No Swinub entry mentions a coat. The thick, long hair for enduring cold is described for Piloswine.

diet.text: Its favourite food is a mushroom that grows under the cover of dead or dried grass.
diet.analogy: Wild boar and domestic pigs (Sus scrofa) root for underground fungi, and pigs have long been used to find truffles (Tuber) by smell.

diet.text: It also finds berries, and can locate mushrooms and berries buried under ice.
It forages by rubbing its snout along the ground to find food and dig it up.

Its foods are surface foods: mushrooms under dead grass and berries do not grow in an ice cave. Ice Path Swinub must forage outside on the slopes and meadows, or live on what reaches the cave from outside.
Odor Sleuth at Lv 1 is a scent-tracking move: the wild animal starts life following its nose.

habitat.text: In HeartGold and SoulSilver it is on all four floors of the Ice Path (1F, B1F, B2F, B3F) at 40%, the highest rate there, at any time of day; levels 21-23 on the upper floors and 22-24 on B2F and B3F. Gold and Silver have the same 40% at every time of day; Crystal has it only by day and morning.
The radio's Hoenn and Sinnoh sounds add Makuhita, Absol, Chingling and Bronzor to the same Ice Path tables. Those are radio-only and are not treated as Ice Path residents here.
Everywhere else it is also in cold places: Icefall Cave (FireRed, LeafGreen), Route 217 (a swarm in Diamond and Pearl, resident in Platinum) and Acuity Lakefront. The Gen 3 Pokédex habitat is cave.
Its entries put it on frozen ground and ice, with dead grass nearby: the ground at the edges of snow rather than deep inside rock.

behavior.text: If it smells something enticing, it dashes off headlong to find the source.
It sometimes discovers or roots out hot springs while foraging.
Crystal's tables have it only by day and morning, which hints at a day-active animal; HeartGold and SoulSilver don't split it by time.
behavior.note: Encounter-table time slots are a weak guide to activity, especially inside a cave.

social.text: Nothing is said about groups, pairs or herds. High encounter rates on every floor are not evidence of group size.

reproduction.text: Field egg group, 20 egg cycles, an even sex ratio; nothing in the Pokédex describes breeding or young.

defense.text: Snow Cloak raises its evasion in a hailstorm: in the games it is harder to hit in blowing snow.
Its wild defences are modest: Mud Sport and Mud-Slap, Endure (Lv 16), Mist (Lv 40) and a Take Down charge (Lv 32).
An animal that dashes headlong after smells is not a vigilant one; Piloswine, whose hair covers its eyes, carries this further and simply keeps charging.

senses.text: Smell is its main sense: a very sensitive nose that leads it to food, and to hot springs, even under ice.
Smell stays primary through the line: Piloswine cannot see through its coat and checks its surroundings with its nose, and it is very sensitive to sound.

life_cycle.text: It becomes Piloswine at Lv 33; Piloswine becomes Mamoswine on levelling up while it knows Ancient Power, which Swinub can carry as an egg move or be taught by a tutor, and which Piloswine has at Lv 1.
The digging habit carries through, with the tool changing: Swinub roots with its nose, Piloswine digs up food buried under ice with its tusks, and Mamoswine's tusks are made of ice.
Mamoswine flourished during the ice age and declined as the ice dwindled; a frozen one was dug from 10,000-year-old ice.
life_cycle.analogy: Woolly mammoths (Mammuthus primigenius) declined as the last ice age ended, and frozen carcasses have been recovered from Siberian permafrost.

life_cycle.text: Size through the line: 0.4 m and 6.5 kg, 1.1 m and 55.8 kg, 2.5 m and 291 kg.

moves_in_the_wild.text: The ground moves are its rooting kit: Odor Sleuth (Lv 1), Mud Sport (Lv 4), Mud-Slap (Lv 13), Mud Bomb (Lv 20) and later Earthquake (Lv 37). The ice moves fit its climate: Powder Snow (Lv 8), Icy Wind (Lv 25), Ice Shard (Lv 28), Blizzard (Lv 44).
Dig is a machine move, taught by people; the wild animal digs with its nose, not with the field move.

ecology.text: A fungivore that also eats fruit. Its favourite food is the fruiting body of a fungus living on dead grass, so much of the energy reaching Swinub comes through decomposition rather than straight from living plants.
ecology.analogy: In real grasslands much of the plant growth is never eaten alive and passes to decomposers; animals that eat fungi tap that detrital food chain.

ecology.text: Rooting turns over soil and litter, which would mix the ground and open bare patches.
ecology.note: Follows from the foraging method; the scale is unknown.
ecology.analogy: Rooting by wild boar turns over large areas of soil and changes which plants grow there.

ecology.text: Animals that eat mushrooms often spread the spores in their droppings; Swinub may disperse the fungus it feeds on.
ecology.note: Nothing in the pack says so.
ecology.analogy: Small mammals that eat truffles disperse truffle spores in their droppings.

ecology.text: Exposing hot springs would open warm, snow-free ground and unfrozen water for other animals.
ecology.note: How often it finds springs, and whether others use them, is not recorded.

ecology.text: No predator of Swinub is named. Golbat, which drinks the blood of Pokémon and shares every Ice Path floor with it, is the likeliest.
ecology.note: Co-occurrence plus Golbat's stated diet; no entry links them.

humans.text: No Swinub entry mentions people. An animal that finds hot springs is plainly useful to a mountain community.
It is easy to catch (catch rate 225) and common in the Ice Path, so it is likely one of the first highland species a trainer handles.

homestead.text: A forager for the cold months: it can find mushrooms and berries buried under ice by smell.

Its knack for rooting out hot springs is the most valuable thing it could do for a highland homestead: a found spring means heat and unfrozen water. Whether there is a spring near the homestead to find is unknown.
It can dig frozen ground with its nose.
It needs cold and ground to root in. Keep food stores sealed: it dashes headlong toward any enticing smell.
A Swinub on the vegetable beds in late winter, nosing out what the frost has left.

microhabitat: frozen ground and dead-grass meadows near the cave
niche.foraging: roots by smell, digging up mushrooms (its favourite food) and berries, including from under ice

relationships.with: mushroom that grows under dead grass (non-Pokémon)
mushroom that grows under dead grass (non-Pokémon)
relationships.note: Spore dispersal by fungus-eaters is common; not recorded for Swinub.
It roots them out, exposing warm water; whether that changes the habitat for others is untested.
Golbat drinks the blood of Pokémon and shares every Ice Path floor; no entry names Swinub as its prey.
SoulSilver only.

ecotypes.name: Deep rooter
ecotypes.reading: A move that splits the ground open and one that throws mud: a digging lineage for deep-frozen ground where food is buried deeper, such as the high meadows above the Ice Path.
ecotypes.behavior: Digs deeper pits and leaves broken ground behind it.

ecotypes.name: Ice-tusk line
ecotypes.reading: Ancient Power is what a Piloswine needs to become Mamoswine, and Icicle Spear matches the adult's ice tusks. A lineage on its way to the ice-age giant; fits the coldest, iciest ground.
ecotypes.behavior: More of them reach Mamoswine; armed with ice early.

ecotypes.name: Charging herd
ecotypes.reading: Three full-body charges, the habit Piloswine is known for (it keeps charging, hackles up). A lineage that meets threats head-on; fits open snowfields with nowhere to hide.
ecotypes.behavior: Charges first and roots afterwards.

open_questions: What is the mushroom, and what decomposes the dead grass it grows on? These are the decomposers at the base of Swinub's food chain, and nothing names them.
Where do Ice Path Swinub feed? There is no dead grass in an ice cave.
How does it find hot springs: smell, warmth, the sound of water? 220.8 credits its nose.
Is it day-active? Crystal suggests so; HeartGold and SoulSilver don't split it by time.
Does it eat animal food? Bite is an egg move, but the entries name only mushrooms and berries.
What eats Swinub? No predator is named.

Tangela.summary: A walking mass of thick blue vines, wide like seaweed and covered in fine hair, that hides whatever is inside: no one has seen the face behind them. The vines are always jiggling and swaying; they unnerve foes, tangle any moving thing that gets close, and tickle whoever is caught. Grabbed, they snap off painlessly so it can get away, and grow back the very next day; they are said never to stop growing. Its adult, Tangrowth, stands still like a shrub and ensnares prey that wanders near. In HeartGold and SoulSilver it lives on Route 44 below Blackthorn, on Route 28 and Mt. Silver, in the grass of Sea Route 21, and in the trees of the routes around Fuchsia.

anatomy.text: A legged mass of vines (Gen 4 shape legs), 1.0 m and 35.0 kg, typed Grass: the Vine Pokémon.
Its whole body is swathed with wide blue vines, similar to seaweed and covered in fine hair; its identity is hidden behind them.
The vines snap off easily and painlessly if grabbed, and are replaced by new growth the very next day.
anatomy.analogy: Real lizards drop their tails to escape and regrow them, though more slowly.

diet.text: No entry says what Tangela eats.
Grass-typed with Chlorophyll and Leaf Guard, and Absorb (Lv 8), Mega Drain (Lv 26) and Ingrain in its list: in game terms a sun-fed plant that can root and drain.
It entangles anything that gets close, and its adult ensnares prey that wanders near (465.3): the line may catch animals as well as live on light.
diet.analogy: Real sundews and pitcher plants live on sunlight and catch insects for what the soil lacks.

habitat.text: No entry says where it lives; the Gen 3 Pokédex habitat is grassland.

In HeartGold and SoulSilver it is in the grass of Route 44 (30%), Route 28 and Mt. Silver (Lv 39-41), and of Sea Route 21 by morning and night; and in the trees (Headbutt) on Routes 12, 13, 14, 15 and 18 and at Fuchsia City; in both versions.

behavior.text: Its vines are always jiggling and shake or sway as it walks.
It tangles any moving thing with its vines; their subtle shaking is ticklish if you get ensnared.
Its activity pattern is not stated; the tables have it at any time except on Sea Route 21 (morning and night).

social.text: Nothing is said about Tangela living together.

reproduction.text: Grass egg group, 20 egg cycles, an even sex ratio, medium growth. Nothing describes how it breeds.

defense.text: Its jiggling vines effectively unnerve its foes; in battle it moves them constantly to annoy its opponent.
Grabbed, its vines snap off without pain, allowing a quick getaway.
Sleep Powder (Lv 5), Poison Powder (Lv 15) and Stun Spore (Lv 29), with Constrict and Bind: powders and holds.

senses.text: It tangles any moving thing: it senses movement, in some way.
It is known to be ticklish.

life_cycle.text: It becomes Tangrowth when it levels up knowing Ancient Power (Lv 33): from 1.0 m and 35.0 kg to 2.0 m and 128.6 kg.
Its vines are said never to stop growing.

moves_in_the_wild.text: Ingrain, Constrict, Sleep Powder, Absorb, Growth, Poison Powder, Vine Whip, Bind, Mega Drain, Stun Spore, Ancient Power, Knock Off and Natural Gift: vines, powders and draining.

ecology.text: A producer, if it lives on sunlight, and perhaps a trapper of small animals too.
Vines it sheds when grabbed, regrown the next day, leave plant matter on the ground for whatever eats it.
On Routes 12 to 15 it shares the trees and grass with Chansey, Nidorina, Nidorino and Hoppip; on Route 44 with Bellsprout, Weepinbell, Lickitung and Poliwhirl.

humans.text: No one has seen the face hidden behind its vines.
Getting ensnared is ticklish, by 114.4; the entries make it a nuisance rather than a danger.

homestead.text: Its vines tangle anything that moves: keep it away from the hen-house and the washing line.
Its shed vines regrow overnight: a renewable source of cord and fibre, if they can be used.
The heap of blue vines by the compost that moved, and the cat that came out of it laughing, if cats laugh.

niche.foraging: unknown; most likely sun-fed, and it entangles anything that comes close
niche.note: Read from its type and abilities and from Tangrowth's ensnaring of prey; no entry gives Tangela's diet.

relationships.with: small insects and other animals caught in its vines
relationships.note: Its adult ensnares prey; nothing says Tangela eats what it tangles.

ecotypes.name: Seed-tangle
ecotypes.reading: A lineage that feeds on what it catches: seeds that drain, a draining touch, the power of the place. Fits rich, crowded grass with plenty passing through.
ecotypes.behavior: Lies still in the grass and drains what it tangles.

ecotypes.name: Hidden mind
ecotypes.reading: An odd lineage for a plant: psychic moves and a light-wall. Perhaps the face nobody has seen (114.10) belongs to something cleverer than it looks. Fits quiet highland routes.
ecotypes.behavior: Moves away from people before they come close.

open_questions: What is inside the vines?
Does Tangela eat what it tangles, or let it go?
Do its vines really never stop growing?
Why is it on Sea Route 21 only by morning and night?

folklore.text: The vines are said to never stop growing.

Teddiursa.summary: A little bear that always licks its paws, because they are soaked with honey; every set of paws tastes unique. When it finds honey its crescent mark glows, and it makes its own honey by blending fruits with pollen that Beedrill collected. Before food becomes scarce in winter it hoards food in many hidden places. It grows into Ursaring, a forest bear that snaps trees to eat the berries that fall and can smell food buried deep underground. In SoulSilver it lives on Route 45, the mountain road below Blackthorn, and on Mt. Silver; in HeartGold, Phanpy has its place.

anatomy.text: A small upright bear (Gen 4 shape upright), 0.6 m and 8.8 kg, typed Normal: the Little Bear Pokémon.
A crescent mark, which glows when it finds honey.
Its palms taste sweet from all the honey they have absorbed; every set of paws tastes unique.

diet.text: Honey: it always licks it, letting it soak into its paws so it can lick them all the time.
diet.analogy: Real bears raid bees' nests for honey and the grubs inside.

diet.text: It makes its own honey by blending fruits and pollen collected by Beedrill.
Before food becomes scarce in winter, it hoards food in many hidden places; what food is not said.
Its adult form eats fallen berries and finds buried food by smell (217.1, 217.2): the line is a forager of sweet and stored foods.

habitat.text: No entry says where it lives; the Gen 3 Pokédex habitat is mountain.
In SoulSilver it lives on Route 45 (10%, Lv 20) and Mt. Silver (10%, Lv 43-48), at any time; it is not wild in HeartGold, where Phanpy has the same places.
Its adult lives in forests with many streams and towering trees, it is said (217.4).

behavior.text: It always licks its honey-soaked paws.
It hoards food in many hidden locations before winter.
behavior.analogy: Real squirrels and jays scatter-hoard food in many small caches for winter.

behavior.text: Its activity pattern is not stated; the tables have it at any time.

social.text: Nothing is said about Teddiursa living together. Its adult leaves scratches on trees in its territory (217.8), so the line keeps territories.

reproduction.text: Field egg group, 20 egg cycles, an even sex ratio, medium growth. Nothing describes how it breeds.

defense.text: Fake Tears, Charm (Lv 36) and Feint Attack (Lv 15): it disarms and tricks rather than fights; Fury Swipes (Lv 8) and Slash are its claws.
Quick Feet speeds it up when it is ailing.

senses.text: It finds honey, and its mark glows when it does; how it finds it is not said. Its adult can distinguish any aroma (217.2).
Sweet Scent (Lv 22) is a smell move: the line deals in scent.

life_cycle.text: It becomes Ursaring at level 30: from 0.6 m and 8.8 kg to 1.8 m and 125.8 kg.
Read as development, a honey-licking cub that hoards becomes a bear that snaps trees for berries and digs up buried food.

moves_in_the_wild.text: Covet, Scratch, Leer, Lick, Fake Tears, Fury Swipes, Feint Attack, Sweet Scent, Slash, Charm, Rest, Snore, Thrash and Fling. Covet (stealing an item) and Pickup (finding items) fit a hoarder.

ecology.text: A honey and fruit feeder that takes pollen gathered by Beedrill: it lives partly on another species' work.
Food hoarded in many hidden places and not all dug up again would plant seeds: a disperser of the fruits it stores, if they are fruits.
ecology.analogy: Forgotten squirrel and jay caches plant many of the world's oaks.

ecology.text: On Route 45 and Mt. Silver it shares the ground with Geodude, Graveler, Skarmory (on Route 45), Ursaring (on Mt. Silver) and the Aipom and Heracross of the trees.

humans.text: Nothing is said about Teddiursa and people.

homestead.text: A honey-finder: its mark glows when it finds honey.
It hoards before winter: let it, and learn where it hides things.
Keep the hives and the honey jars shut.
Every spoon in the kitchen sticky, and one small bear with a glowing chest asleep in the larder.

niche.foraging: licks honey, makes its own from fruit and pollen, and hoards food for winter

relationships.note: Blended into its honey.
If forgotten caches grow.

ecotypes.name: Winter sleeper
ecotypes.reading: A lineage of the long sleep: drowsy, talking in its sleep and fattening up. The hoarder that sleeps the winter away beside its caches. Fits high cold places like Mt. Silver.
ecotypes.behavior: Eats and hoards hard in autumn, then sleeps.

ecotypes.name: Hive-raider
ecotypes.reading: A lineage that takes honey and pollen from Beedrill by force: claws, jaws and a counterblow for the stings. Fits forests with Beedrill nests.
ecotypes.behavior: Goes after nests and takes the stings.

open_questions: How does Teddiursa get the pollen Beedrill collected?
What does it hoard, and does it find all of it again?
Does it sleep through the winter?
Why is it in SoulSilver's wild and not HeartGold's?

Tentacool.summary: A drifting jellyfish of shallow seas, its body almost entirely water. Tentacool floats along on the waves and currents, very hard to see, and stabs anything it touches with its toxic feelers; anglers and fishermen who hook one by accident are often stung. Out of the sea it dries up like parchment, and when the tide goes out its shriveled remains wash up on the shore. Its crystal-clear eyes shoot beams of light, made, in one entry, by refracting sunlight through the water in its body. In HeartGold and SoulSilver it is the commonest thing on the surface of the sea in both regions, from New Bark Town and the Whirl Islands to Pallet Town and the seas around Cinnabar.

anatomy.text: A tentacled sea animal (Gen 4 shape tentacles), 0.9 m and 45.5 kg, typed Water and Poison: the Jellyfish Pokémon.
Its body is almost entirely composed of water.
Two long tentacles with poison stingers at their tips, and transparent, crystal-like eyes.
Its eyes shoot beams of light; one entry says it absorbs sunlight and refracts it through the water in its body to make the beam energy.

diet.text: No entry says what Tentacool eats.
The machine reading files it as living on sunlight, from 72.7; but that entry turns sunlight into beam energy, not food.
Stinging anything it touches, and the young of a hunter (Tentacruel ensnares and poisons prey, 73.1, 73.2), it most likely catches small animals that brush its feelers.
diet.analogy: Real jellyfish are passive hunters: they drift with stinging tentacles out and eat whatever small animals touch them.
diet.note: From its stings and its adult form; no entry names its food.

diet.text: Constrict (Lv 8), Acid (Lv 12) and Wrap (Lv 22) are holding and dissolving moves; Wring Out (Lv 43) squeezes.

habitat.text: Shallow seas, drifting in the waves and sea currents; the Gen 3 Pokédex habitat is sea.
It cannot live out of water: removed from the sea it dries up like parchment, and it shrivels if washed ashore.

In HeartGold and SoulSilver it is on the surf tables of almost every shore in both regions: New Bark, Cherrygrove, Olivine and Cianwood, Routes 32, 34 and 47, Sea Routes 40 and 41, the Whirl Islands and Union Cave's water in Johto; Routes 12, 13, 26 and 27, Pallet Town, Vermilion City, Cinnabar Island and Sea Routes 19, 20 and 21 in Kanto. It is up to nine encounters in ten on the water, at any time, in both versions.

behavior.text: It drifts aimlessly in the waves and floats along with the sea currents.
Very difficult to see in water, it may not be noticed until it stings.
Its activity pattern is not stated; the tables have it at any time.

social.text: Nothing is said about whether Tentacool drift alone or together. The surf tables make them by far the commonest animal on the water, so they meet constantly.
Its adult form flashes the red orbs on its head to alert others to danger (73.11), so the line does signal to its own kind.

reproduction.text: Water 3 egg group, 20 egg cycles, an even sex ratio, slow growth. Nothing describes how it breeds.

defense.text: Its toxic feelers stab anything they touch; anglers who hook one are punished by its stinging acid, and countless fishermen are hurt by its stingers.
Being almost invisible in water is its first defence.
Clear Body keeps its stats from being lowered and Liquid Ooze hurts whatever drains it; Barrier (Lv 26) and Toxic Spikes (Lv 15) are its other guards.

senses.text: Nothing is said about how it senses its surroundings. Its crystal-like eyes are named for the beams they shoot, not for sight.
Supersonic (Lv 5) and Screech (Lv 36) are sound moves: the line uses sound, as Tentacruel's orbs do before an ultrasonic blast (73.6).

life_cycle.text: It becomes Tentacruel at level 30: from 0.9 m and 45.5 kg to 1.6 m and 55.0 kg, and from two tentacles to 80.
When the tide goes out, dehydrated Tentacool remains are found washed up on the shore; one tossed back into the sea revives.

moves_in_the_wild.text: Poison Sting, Supersonic, Constrict, Acid, Toxic Spikes, Bubble Beam, Wrap, Barrier, Water Pulse, Poison Jab, Screech, Hydro Pump and Wring Out: stings, holds, acid and water.

ecology.text: The commonest drifting stinger of the coasts, so most likely a key small predator of the surface water in both regions.
ecology.note: From its numbers and stings; no entry names its prey.

ecology.text: Its stranded, shriveled remains on beaches at low tide are food for shore scavengers, if anything eats them; no entry says what does.
Everywhere it drifts it shares the water with Magikarp; on Kanto's southern seas with Chinchou, Shellder and Lanturn, and on Johto's western coast with Krabby, Staryu and Corsola.

humans.text: Anglers who hook them by accident are often stung, and countless fishermen are hurt by its stingers.
Swimmers are hurt too, in principle: it may not be noticed until it stings.
People toss stranded Tentacool back into the sea to revive them.

homestead.text: Not a highland animal: it needs the sea and dies dry. The homestead meets it only on trips to the coast.
Tell anyone fishing the coast to watch for it on the line: its stingers hurt.
A shriveled Tentacool on the beach after a storm, and the child who carries it back to the water in a bucket.

microhabitat: surface of shallow seas and coasts
niche.foraging: unknown; most likely catches what brushes its stinging feelers
niche.note: The machine reading's phototroph comes from 72.7, where sunlight becomes beam energy, not food. Filed with Tentacruel as a predator.

relationships.with: small fish and other small sea animals
relationships.note: From its stings and its adult form.

ecotypes.name: Beam-eyed drifter
ecotypes.reading: A lineage of light: a beam, a reflection of what hits it, a confusing glow. The crystal eyes that shoot mysterious beams (72.9), developed further. Fits clear, sunny water where light carries.
ecotypes.behavior: Flashes at what comes near before it stings.

ecotypes.name: Murky-shallows stinger
ecotypes.reading: A lineage of turbid shallows: it clouds the water, knocks things loose and spins itself free of tangles. Fits muddy coasts and river mouths where it can't be seen anyway.
ecotypes.behavior: Stays near the bottom in silty water.

open_questions: What does Tentacool eat?
Does its sunlight-to-beam trick (72.7) feed it at all, or only arm it?
Do Tentacool drift alone or in blooms?
How long can a stranded Tentacool survive before it can't be revived?

Tentacruel.summary: The adult of Tentacool: a jellyfish with 80 tentacles that it keeps short and extends on hunts, stretching them almost endlessly as they absorb water to make a poisonous net that entangles prey and is difficult to escape. It can catch up to 80 prey at once, and weakens them with a harsh toxin. It lives among complex rock formations on the ocean floor. Two large red orbs on its head glow when it is excited or agitated, flash stridently to alert others to danger, and glow before it lashes the area with an ultrasonic blast that raises rough waves. In HeartGold and SoulSilver it shares Tentacool's shores in both regions, rarer and deeper, on the surf and the super rod.

anatomy.text: A tentacled sea animal (Gen 4 shape tentacles), 1.6 m and 55.0 kg, typed Water and Poison: the Jellyfish Pokémon.
Eighty tentacles that it can stretch and contract freely; normally kept short, they absorb water and stretch almost endlessly.
Large red orbs on its head, which glow.

diet.text: A hunter: on hunts its tentacles are extended to ensnare and immobilize prey, then weaken it with poison.
Its 80 feelers become a net to entangle prey, and it can catch up to 80 prey at the same time.
No entry names the prey. Eighty at once suggests small animals, fish and the like, rather than large ones.
diet.analogy: The lion's mane jellyfish trails hundreds of stinging tentacles and catches fish, shrimp and other jellyfish in them.

diet.text: Constrict, Wrap (Lv 22) and Wring Out (Lv 55) are the squeezing net in game form.

habitat.text: It lives in complex rock formations on the ocean floor; the Gen 3 Pokédex habitat is sea.

In HeartGold and SoulSilver it is on the same shores as Tentacool in both regions, from Cherrygrove and the Whirl Islands to Pallet Town, Vermilion and the seas around Cinnabar. It is one surf encounter in ten at most places and up to three in ten at the Whirl Islands and Sea Route 41, and is hooked on the super rod at many, at any time, in both versions.
Rarer at the surface than Tentacool and on the deeper-water rod: in line with an adult that lives on the sea floor.

behavior.text: It keeps its tentacles short and extends them on hunts.
Its red orbs glow when it grows excited or agitated, and glow before it lashes the vicinity with a harsh ultrasonic blast; its outburst creates rough waves.
Its activity pattern is not stated; the tables have it at any time.

social.text: It alerts others to danger by stridently flashing the red orbs on its head.
A warning signal implies others nearby to warn: Tentacruel most likely live near each other, though no entry says how many.

reproduction.text: Water 3 egg group, 20 egg cycles, an even sex ratio, slow growth. Nothing describes how it breeds.

defense.text: In battle it extends all 80 tentacles to entrap its opponent inside an encircling poisonous net that is difficult to escape.
Its tentacles sting, causing poisoning and sharp, stabbing pain.
The ultrasonic blast is a weapon too; Supersonic, Screech (Lv 42) and Barrier are in its list, with Clear Body and Liquid Ooze.

senses.text: Nothing is said about how it senses prey. Its orbs are described as signals and weapons, not as eyes.

life_cycle.text: It evolves from Tentacool at level 30: from 0.9 m and 45.5 kg, two long tentacles and a drifting life at the surface, to 1.6 m and 55.0 kg, 80 tentacles and the rock formations of the sea floor.
Read as development: a drifter at the surface that settles on the reef as it grows.
life_cycle.analogy: Many real jellyfish alternate between a drifting form and one fixed to rock, though the other way round.

moves_in_the_wild.text: Poison Sting, Supersonic, Constrict, Acid, Toxic Spikes, Bubble Beam, Wrap, Barrier, Water Pulse, Poison Jab, Screech, Hydro Pump and Wring Out.

ecology.text: A net-hunter of the reef: up to 80 prey at a time makes it a heavy predator of small sea animals where it lives.
On Kanto's southern seas it shares the water with Tentacool, Chinchou, Shellder and Lanturn; on Johto's western coast with Krabby, Kingler, Staryu and Corsola.
Magikarp, everywhere it lives and small, would be prey of the right size; nothing names it.
ecology.note: Size and co-occurrence only.

humans.text: Nothing is said about Tentacruel and people directly; its sting causes sharp, stabbing pain.
Its outburst creates rough waves around it: a hazard to small boats nearby, in principle.

homestead.text: Not a highland animal: a sea-floor hunter. Met only on coastal trips.
If the orbs on its head start to glow, back away: it is agitated, and the blast comes next.
The fishing boat that turns back when the red lights come up under the swell.

microhabitat: complex rock formations on the ocean floor
niche.foraging: extends 80 tentacles into a poisonous net and catches up to 80 prey at a time

relationships.with: small fish and other small sea animals
relationships.note: It catches up to 80 prey at once; what they are is unnamed.
Small, everywhere it lives; nothing names it as prey.

ecotypes.name: Reef net
ecotypes.reading: A lineage of the rock formations (73.8): it clouds the water, sharpens its own strikes and strips prey of what protects it. Fits rocky sea floors.
ecotypes.behavior: Waits spread among the rocks, net open.

ecotypes.name: Signal-orb shoal
ecotypes.reading: A lineage of light: confusing glows, a protecting veil, a beam. The orbs that flash warnings to others (73.11), as a way of life among many. Fits open coastal water where many drift together.
ecotypes.behavior: Flashes to its neighbours at the first sign of danger.

open_questions: What are the 80 prey it can catch at once?
When does a drifting Tentacool settle on the sea floor?
Who does it warn with its orbs: other Tentacruel, or any animal nearby?
Does the ultrasonic blast stun prey, or only drive off enemies?

Typhlosion.summary: A large grassland animal with blazing fur that hides behind its own heat. Typhlosion makes the air around it shimmer with intense flame and conceals itself in the haze; when the shimmer rises it is ready to fight, and at the peak of its rage anything that touches it bursts into flame. Its young, Cyndaquil, are timid animals that curl into a ball and flare the fire on their backs only when startled, and whose flames sputter with incomplete combustion when they are tired.
